Drain Punch is one of the best moves the line can receive under permadeath rules because every successful attack simultaneously restores health, while Mach Punch can remove weakened faster threats before they act. Guts can turn an accidental burn or poison into an offensive advantage, but deliberately carrying damaging status throughout a run creates unnecessary chip and should only be considered when the payoff is controlled. Psychic and Flying are the original major weaknesses, with Fairy joining them from Generation VI onward, and the line's poor Speed means strong special attacks often land before it can respond. If trading is unavailable, Eviolite Gurdurr is still an excellent practical final form, making this family much less dependent on its trade evolution than many others.

pokemon.name: Timburr
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Timburr always carries a squared wooden beam and uses it both for training and combat. It becomes strong enough to evolve when it can easily lift timber weighing nearly three times its own body weight. Timburr loves assisting human construction crews and is commonly found around building sites. If rain forces construction work to stop, it may throw a tantrum and swing its log in frustration.

pokemon.name: Gurdurr
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Gurdurr carries a steel I-beam as a training weight and uses it to build its muscles. Individuals compare their strength with other Gurdurr and even Machoke, and a Gurdurr that performs poorly may hide away for a time in embarrassment. It is strong enough to remain standing even when attacked by a group of professional wrestlers. Unlike Timburr, which enjoys helping to build structures, Gurdurr is particularly suited to demolition work.

pokemon.name: Conkeldurr
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Conkeldurr carries enormous concrete pillars and often uses them as weapons or supports, but when fighting at full strength it throws the pillars aside and attacks directly with its fists. The species can manufacture concrete, and legend says humans learned the technique from Conkeldurr roughly 2,000 years ago. Concrete mixed by Conkeldurr is described as stronger than ordinary concrete even when both use the same ingredients. It remains closely associated with construction sites and continues to work alongside human builders.

playthrough: Tympole evolves into Water/Ground Palpitoad at level 25 and then into Seismitoad at level 36, giving the family one of the strongest defensive type combinations available during a Unova playthrough. Seismitoad has base 105 HP and balanced offenses; its Attack was base 85 in Generation V and increased to 95 from Generation VI onward, while Special Attack remains 85. Surf or Scald, Earthquake or Earth Power, Drain Punch, Sludge Wave, Rock coverage, Stealth Rock, and later Power Whip or Knock Off allow physical, special, mixed, and utility sets. Swift Swim doubles Speed in rain, Poison Touch can poison targets hit by contact moves, and the Hidden Ability Water Absorb grants complete Water immunity and restores one-quarter of maximum HP when hit by a Water attack. Water/Ground also grants an Electric immunity and leaves Grass as the line's only ordinary weakness, but that weakness deals quadruple damage. Modest or Adamant suit offensive approaches, while Bold or Impish can emphasize the excellent defensive typing and HP.
competitive: Seismitoad debuted as a strong BW NU utility Pokemon rather than an OU star, using Water/Ground typing, 105 HP, Water Absorb, Stealth Rock, Scald, Earthquake or Earth Power, and respectable mixed offenses to function as a defensive pivot or rain attacker. Swift Swim also gave it an offensive route, while Water Absorb made it especially useful against opposing Water-types, but its lack of reliable recovery and crippling quadruple Grass weakness kept it from becoming an elite wall. Its Attack increased from 85 to 95 in Generation VI, and it continued to occupy useful NU and RU roles through later generations. Sword and Shield briefly elevated Seismitoad's importance much further: Water Absorb and its typing made it one of the most practical defensive answers to enormously powerful Water attacks in the early metagame, while Stealth Rock and utility prevented it from being a completely passive counterpick. Even after that environment changed, SS tiering settled Seismitoad in RU, where Water immunity, Electric immunity, Knock Off, Toxic, and Stealth Rock still provide valuable role compression.
nuzlocke: Seismitoad is one of the safer Water-types for Nuzlockes because Water/Ground has only a single type weakness, grants an Electric immunity, and base 105 HP provides substantial room for ordinary neutral hits. Water Absorb is the safest ability where available because it adds a second immunity and can actively heal Seismitoad when switched into a known Water attack. The entire defensive profile must be discarded against Grass coverage, however: Energy Ball, Giga Drain, Grass Knot, Leaf Blade, and similar moves deal quadruple damage and can kill from surprisingly high HP. Swift Swim can make Seismitoad very difficult to outspeed in rain, while Drain Punch can provide recovery for physical sets, but inaccurate coverage such as Power Whip should not be used when safer attacks already win. Bold, Impish, or other defensive natures can improve its margin further, but scouting Grass moves is more important than any nature choice.

pokemon.name: Tympole
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Tympole vibrates the bumps on its cheeks to create sounds at frequencies too high for humans and many other Pokemon to hear. Groups communicate by arranging those sounds into rhythms, particularly to warn one another of danger. Their high-pitched singing creates graceful ripples across the surface of the water. Tympole are also known to swim and attack cooperatively in groups.

pokemon.name: Palpitoad
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Palpitoad is amphibious and captures prey with a long sticky tongue. The large bumps on its head can be vibrated to produce intense sounds, waves, and even earthquake-like tremors that weaken prey. Individuals with larger lumps can generate a wider range of sounds. Its ability to operate both in water and on land marks a major ecological transition from the fully aquatic Tympole stage.

pokemon.name: Seismitoad
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Seismitoad's many body lumps perform different functions. The bumps on its head can fire a paralyzing liquid, while those on its hands can be vibrated to amplify punching power strongly enough to reduce a boulder to rubble. It can also generate earthquake-like tremors or use vibration simply to torment an opponent. Humans have found a gentler use for the same anatomy: elderly people are said to enjoy massages produced by Seismitoad's vibrations. The species also wields venom and is biologically related to Croagunk and Toxicroak.

playthrough: Throh is a single-stage pure Fighting-type built around bulk rather than Speed, with base 120 HP, 100 Attack, 85 Defense, 85 Special Defense, and only base 45 Speed. Fighting STAB through Storm Throw, Brick Break, Revenge, Superpower, or other generation-specific options combines with Rock Slide, Earthquake, elemental punches, Payback, and Bulk Up to give it respectable physical coverage. Guts raises Attack by 50 percent while statused and ignores burn's normal Attack penalty, Inner Focus prevents flinching, and the Hidden Ability Mold Breaker lets Throh ignore opposing abilities when using its moves. Storm Throw is especially notable because it always lands a critical hit when it connects, allowing Throh to bypass opposing Defense boosts; its base power increased from 40 to 60 beginning in Generation VI. Brave or Adamant suit straightforward offense, while Careful can reinforce its already good special bulk. Throh is dependable in a normal playthrough when used as a slow tank, but Psychic and Flying attacks are dangerous in Generation V and Fairy joins those weaknesses from Generation VI onward.
competitive: Throh has spent most of its competitive history in lower tiers, but its combination of 120 HP, solid 85/85 defenses, Guts, and base 100 Attack gives it a real niche as a bulky Fighting-type. In BW-era doubles, Smogon specifically highlighted it as an effective Trick Room attacker because its base 45 Speed becomes an advantage under reversed turn order, while Guts plus Flame Orb supplies immediate power and Storm Throw guarantees critical hits. In singles it has also used Bulk Up, RestTalk, Circle Throw, Knock Off in later generations, and status-activated Guts sets to function as a durable brawler rather than a fast breaker. The recurring limitation is competition: Conkeldurr offers much greater Attack and Mach Punch, while other Fighting-types often bring either higher Speed or broader utility. Throh therefore works best when its unusual bulk, phazing, or Trick Room suitability matters more than raw offensive efficiency.
nuzlocke: Throh is unusually forgiving in a Nuzlocke because base 120 HP and balanced 85/85 defenses give it a large margin against neutral attacks, while it arrives fully evolved and does not require a trade or item. Guts can turn an accidental burn or poison into extra Attack, but deliberately carrying damaging status through a permadeath run creates avoidable chip and is usually less safe than simply using Throh's natural bulk. Storm Throw is valuable against opponents that boost Defense because the guaranteed critical hit ignores those defensive boosts, while Revenge or Circle Throw can exploit Throh's low Speed but also require allowing the opponent to act first. Psychic, Flying, and later Fairy attacks remain the principal dangers, especially strong special attacks that can still overwhelm its HP. Careful or Adamant are both sensible depending on whether safety or damage is the priority.

pokemon.name: Throh
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Throh is a male-only species that travels and trains in groups of five. Wild individuals weave their own belts from vines, and tightening the belt increases their fighting power; the material also grows darker as it absorbs more of Throh's sweat. A Throh that cannot keep pace with its group discards its belt and leaves. The species is driven by an instinct to seize and throw opponents larger than itself.

playthrough: Sawk is a single-stage pure Fighting-type that trades Throh's enormous HP for far greater offensive tempo, combining base 125 Attack with base 85 Speed and average 75/75/75 bulk. Close Combat is its defining STAB attack and can break through many neutral opponents immediately, while Rock Slide or Stone Edge, Earthquake, elemental punches, Knock Off in later games, Poison Jab, and Bulk Up provide useful coverage. Sturdy allows Sawk to survive an otherwise fatal hit from full HP in modern mechanics, Inner Focus prevents flinching, and Mold Breaker lets its attacks ignore abilities such as Sturdy, Levitate, or other defensive effects when applicable. The main story drawback is that Close Combat lowers both Defense and Special Defense after use, so repeated use can leave Sawk vulnerable even when the first knockout was easy. Adamant maximizes its excellent Attack, while Jolly can push its middling Speed high enough to beat more opponents before they move.
competitive: Sawk established itself as a strong BW NU attacker through a simple but effective package: base 125 Attack, Close Combat, good physical coverage, and enough Speed to outrun many bulky Pokemon. Choice Band and Choice Scarf sets both exploit that immediate power, while Sturdy provides emergency insurance from full HP and Mold Breaker can bypass defensive abilities that would otherwise complicate a sweep. Later generations improved its coverage with moves such as Knock Off and Poison Jab, and SM analyses still gave Sawk a lower-tier niche as a hard-hitting Fighting-type that could pressure common defensive cores. It has never become a sustained upper-tier staple because base 85 Speed is only moderate and 75/75/75 bulk is not enough to repeatedly absorb hits after Close Combat drops. Even so, Sawk's competitive identity is much clearer than many low-tier Pokemon: it is a straightforward physical breaker whose usefulness rises when Sturdy or Mold Breaker solves a specific matchup.
nuzlocke: Sawk is a strong Nuzlocke encounter because it is fully evolved immediately, base 125 Attack shortens dangerous battles, and Sturdy can guarantee survival from full HP against one otherwise lethal hit. Keeping Sturdy intact matters enormously: chip damage from hazards, weather, status, or earlier attacks removes that guarantee, so healing before a major fight can be worth more than squeezing out extra damage. Close Combat is powerful and accurate but lowers both defenses, making it risky when multiple opponents remain or the target is unlikely to faint. Psychic and Flying are the original major weaknesses, with Fairy added from Generation VI onward, and faster special attackers can exploit Sawk's merely average bulk. Adamant provides excellent damage, while Jolly can be safer when moving first prevents a dangerous retaliation.

pokemon.name: Sawk
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Sawk is a male-only mountain-dwelling species that devotes itself almost entirely to martial-arts training. Individuals punch trees and boulders high in the mountains, and the sound of that training can carry over long distances. Tightening the black belt around its waist increases its strength and focus. Sawk becomes angry when training is interrupted, and Pokédex lore claims a fully trained individual can split an ocean with a karate chop.

playthrough: Sewaddle evolves into Swadloon at level 20, and Swadloon evolves into Leavanny through high friendship, so the final evolution can arrive relatively early if the middle stage is kept healthy and active. Leavanny is Bug/Grass with base 103 Attack, 92 Speed, and respectable 75/80/70 bulk, giving it solid physical offense through X-Scissor, Leaf Blade, Seed Bomb, Shadow Claw, and later Knock Off or other coverage. The typing supplies useful resistances to Water, Electric, Fighting, Ground, and especially Grass, but it also creates severe weaknesses, including quadruple damage from both Fire and Flying. Swarm boosts Bug attacks at low HP, Chlorophyll doubles Speed in harsh sunlight, and the Hidden Ability Overcoat prevents weather chip and powder effects in modern mechanics. Swords Dance can turn Leavanny into a strong physical sweeper, while Sticky Web in later generations gives it an important team-support role by lowering the Speed of grounded opponents that switch in. Adamant or Jolly are natural offensive natures, but the family is safest when brought into resisted attacks rather than relying on setup in front of Fire- or Flying-capable opponents.
competitive: Leavanny was a BW ZU Pokemon whose best attributes were base 103 Attack, base 92 Speed, and strong physical Grass/Bug STAB, but its competitive ceiling was sharply limited by a typing that is quadruple weak to Fire and Flying and weak to Stealth Rock. Swords Dance, Leaf Blade, X-Scissor, and coverage let it threaten slower teams, while Chlorophyll provided a potential sun niche, but stronger and more defensively stable Grass- and Bug-types were usually easier to justify. The introduction of Sticky Web in Generation VI gave Leavanny a much clearer support identity: its Speed lets it establish the hazard before many opposing leads act, and offensive STAB prevents it from being completely passive. It still competes with dedicated Sticky Web setters that offer stronger defensive typing or utility, so Leavanny has remained a lower-tier specialist rather than a metagame staple. Its historical value therefore comes less from raw sweeping dominance and more from combining respectable offense with one of the game's most influential forms of Speed control.
nuzlocke: The Sewaddle line can be useful in a Nuzlocke because it evolves to Swadloon at level 20 and can reach Leavanny soon afterward through high friendship, giving the player a reasonably strong final-stage attacker without waiting for a late level. Leavanny's base 92 Speed and 103 Attack often allow it to remove Water-, Ground-, or Psychic-type threats before they attack, and its resistances can create safe switches when the opposing movepool is known. The problem is the typing: Fire and Flying moves deal quadruple damage, while Ice, Rock, Bug, and Poison are also super effective, so a single unexpected coverage move can be fatal. Swords Dance should only be used against opponents that cannot threaten Leavanny immediately, and Sticky Web can provide safer teamwide value in later generations without requiring repeated setup. Jolly can be especially useful when an extra Speed threshold prevents a dangerous retaliation.

pokemon.name: Sewaddle
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Sewaddle produces thread from its mouth and uses chewed leaves to make clothing, although Leavanny often prepares the first leafy outfit for newly hatched individuals. Its leaf hood can be folded over the face to hide from predators while awake or asleep. When food is scarce, Sewaddle can eat its own leaf clothing. Individuals also greet one another by rubbing together the sensory bumps on their heads.

pokemon.name: Swadloon
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Swadloon wraps itself in a cloak of leaves that keeps its body warm while it lives on the forest floor. The leaf structures on its head detect air movement and help it sense the surrounding environment. It feeds on fallen leaves and converts them into nutrients, enriching the soil and helping nearby plant life grow. The stage is therefore relatively sedentary compared with both Sewaddle and Leavanny.

pokemon.name: Leavanny
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Leavanny is strongly nurturing toward small Pokemon. When it encounters a young creature, it cuts leaves into suitable shapes with the blades on its arms and stitches them together using sticky silk produced from its mouth, creating protective clothing much like it does for Sewaddle. Its warm body can help keep eggs from becoming cold. The species combines predatory insect anatomy with unusually parental and caretaking behavior.

playthrough: Venipede evolves into Whirlipede at level 22 and Scolipede at level 30, giving the family a relatively quick route to a fully evolved Bug/Poison attacker. Standard Scolipede has excellent base 112 Speed and, from Generation VI onward, base 100 Attack; its Attack was only 90 in Generation V. Megahorn, Poison Jab, Earthquake, Rock Slide, Aqua Tail, Swords Dance, Spikes, Toxic Spikes, and later Baton Pass or other utility give it both offensive and support options. Poison Point can punish contact, Swarm boosts Bug attacks at low HP, and the Hidden Ability changed from Quick Feet in Generation V to the much stronger Speed Boost from Generation VI onward, raising Speed by one stage at the end of each turn. Bug/Poison provides quadruple resistance to Fighting and Grass but leaves Fire, Flying, Psychic, and Rock weaknesses, while mediocre 60/89/69 bulk means Scolipede prefers to attack or set hazards before taking heavy damage. Mega Scolipede is radically different: it remains Bug/Poison but shifts to 140 Attack, 149 Defense, 99 Special Defense, and only 62 Speed, with Shell Armor preventing critical hits; Adamant or Impish can exploit its new physical profile far better than the Jolly nature commonly favored by the fast standard form.
competitive: Standard Scolipede was a BW NUBL Pokemon with a useful UU niche as a very fast offensive Spikes setter, combining base 112 Speed with Megahorn and enough resistances to force selected switches. Generation VI transformed its competitive identity by increasing Attack from 90 to 100 and replacing the Hidden Ability Quick Feet with Speed Boost. Speed Boost plus Swords Dance turned Scolipede into a dangerous cleaner and wallbreaker, while Substitute, Protect, and Baton Pass also made it one of the central engines of early XY Baton Pass chains; those strategies became important enough to contribute directly to repeated Baton Pass restrictions in XY and ORAS. In SM, Scolipede sat in UUBL and remained a threatening Speed Boost sweeper using Swords Dance, Megahorn, Earthquake, Aqua Tail, or Z-Moves. Mega Scolipede is a much newer form and should be evaluated separately: confirmed modern data gives it 140 Attack, 149 Defense, 99 Special Defense, only 62 Speed, and Shell Armor, trading the base form's famous Speed for extreme physical bulk and much stronger immediate Attack. It does not yet possess the decades-long tier résumé of standard Scolipede, so historical claims about the Mega should remain conservative.
nuzlocke: Standard Scolipede is useful in Nuzlockes because it evolves by level 30, base 112 Speed helps it avoid incoming damage, and its quadruple Fighting and Grass resistances can create excellent planned switches. Poison Point can occasionally punish contact, but Speed Boost is the most valuable later-generation ability because every completed turn makes Scolipede harder to revenge kill without requiring a risky setup move. Fire, Flying, Psychic, and Rock coverage are dangerous, and its special bulk is poor enough that even neutral special attacks deserve respect. Megahorn's imperfect accuracy is a liability under permadeath rules, so X-Scissor or another reliable attack can be preferable when the extra power is unnecessary. Mega Scolipede flips the safety profile: Shell Armor completely removes critical-hit risk and 149 Defense is extraordinary, but base 62 Speed means it takes far more attacks before acting; the Mega form is therefore better used as a physical tank and breaker than as the fast cleaner represented by standard Scolipede.

pokemon.name: Venipede
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Venipede senses its surroundings through antennae and rear feelers that detect vibrations in the air. It is highly aggressive for its small size, and its fangs inject venom strong enough to paralyze large bird Pokemon. Venipede often fights with Sizzlipede, a related species. It hunts opportunistically and may attack any Pokemon it believes it can eat.

pokemon.name: Whirlipede
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Whirlipede normally remains motionless while storing energy for evolution, protected by a hard segmented shell covered in poisonous spikes. When threatened, however, it can spin its body like a wheel and charge at roughly 60 miles per hour. The stage remains highly aggressive despite its cocoon-like appearance and will stab approaching predators with its venomous barbs.

pokemon.name: Scolipede
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Scolipede is an aggressive forest predator that chases enemies at high speed and attacks relentlessly with its horns until it wins. It clamps prey with the claws around its neck, immobilizes it, and then injects powerful venom. Scolipede can also curl into a ball and roll like Whirlipede. It engages in fierce territorial battles with Centiskorch, and Pokédex records state that the victor may eat the loser.

pokemon.name: Scolipede
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Mega Scolipede develops much heavier armor and greatly enlarged horn and claw structures while retaining its Bug/Poison typing. Its venom becomes faintly luminescent, and the toxin affects Scolipede's own mind, making the Mega form even more vicious than the ordinary species. The heavier body no longer appears adapted to the same high-speed rolling behavior associated with standard Scolipede. Its Shell Armor ability also reflects the transformation's greatly increased physical protection.

playthrough: Cottonee evolves into Whimsicott with a Sun Stone. In Generation V both stages are pure Grass, but from Generation VI onward the family becomes Grass/Fairy, gaining a Dragon immunity, several useful additional resistances, and a quadruple Poison weakness. Whimsicott has only base 77 Special Attack but excellent base 116 Speed and a deep support movepool including Tailwind, Encore, Taunt, Leech Seed, Stun Spore, Cotton Guard, Sunny Day, U-turn, and later Moonblast. Prankster gives status moves +1 priority and is the line's defining ability; from Generation VII onward, Dark-type opponents are immune to opposing Prankster-boosted status moves that target them. Infiltrator lets attacks and status bypass Substitute and screens, while Chlorophyll doubles Speed in sun. Timid is the most natural nature for offensive or fast-support sets, though Bold or Calm can support bulkier play; Whimsicott's real strength is controlling tempo rather than dealing large amounts of direct damage.
competitive: Whimsicott has one of Generation V's most enduring support identities because Prankster gives priority to an enormous collection of non-damaging moves. In BW RU, Smogon highlighted Encore, Taunt, Stun Spore, Memento, Tailwind, and weather support as the core of its niche, allowing Whimsicott to disrupt setup and provide speed control despite poor offensive stats. Generation VI added Fairy typing and Moonblast, giving it meaningful offensive pressure against Dragon-, Dark-, and Fighting-types while improving its defensive profile. Its doubles résumé is even stronger: across multiple VGC generations, Prankster Tailwind, Encore, Taunt, Helping Hand, Sunny Day, Fake Tears, and other support have made Whimsicott a recurring hyper-offense staple, and modern VGC analyses still describe it as a reliable priority Tailwind setter. In singles its tier placement has moved downward over time, but the underlying competitive identity remains consistent—Whimsicott wins games by acting before faster threats and manipulating their options rather than through raw damage.
nuzlocke: Whimsicott can be extremely useful in Nuzlockes because Prankster lets it use Tailwind, Encore, Taunt, status, or other utility before most opponents can act. From Generation VI onward, Grass/Fairy also grants a Dragon immunity and useful resistances to Fighting, Dark, Water, Grass, Ground, and Electric, although the new typing creates a quadruple Poison weakness plus Fire, Ice, Flying, and Steel weaknesses. Its 60 HP and merely average defenses mean those weaknesses can still lead to sudden deaths, so support should be used from favorable matchups rather than expecting Whimsicott to tank neutral hits. Encore can lock an opponent into a harmless setup or status move and create very safe turns, but its value depends on knowing what the opponent just selected. Timid Whimsicott is best used to control the battle for stronger teammates rather than trying to become the team's primary damage dealer.

pokemon.name: Cottonee
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Cottonee is so light that ordinary wind carries it through the air, and groups gather together on the breeze during mating season. Rain soaks the cotton and makes the Pokemon too heavy to drift, causing it to shelter beneath trees until it dries. When threatened, Cottonee sheds cotton as a distraction and escapes while the lost material rapidly regrows. Its cotton is valuable to humans for extremely soft bedding and, when woven together with Eldegoss cotton, luxury fabrics.

pokemon.name: Whimsicott
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Whimsicott can squeeze through gaps no matter how narrow and uses that ability to enter homes, move objects, play pranks, and leave tufts of cotton behind. Like Cottonee, it can ride wind currents but becomes too heavy to move properly when soaked with water, forcing it to remain where it is until dry. Whimsicott grows its cotton in sunlight and tears away excess fluff when too much accumulates. Its reputation as a prankster is therefore tied directly to its unusually light, flexible body rather than to aggressive territorial behavior.

playthrough: Petilil evolves with a Sun Stone into either Unovan Lilligant or, in Hisui, Hisuian Lilligant. Unovan Lilligant is a pure Grass special attacker with base 110 Special Attack and 90 Speed, and Quiver Dance is its defining setup move because one turn raises Special Attack, Special Defense, and Speed simultaneously. Giga Drain or Energy Ball provide reliable STAB, while Sleep Powder, Petal Dance, Leech Seed, and later Pollen Puff or coverage options can support sweeping or utility; Own Tempo is especially useful with Petal Dance because it prevents the usual confusion at the end of the move. Chlorophyll instead doubles Speed in harsh sunlight, while Leaf Guard prevents status under sun. Hisuian Lilligant changes the role completely: Grass/Fighting, base 105 Attack and 105 Speed, Close Combat, Leaf Blade or Solar Blade, and the signature Victory Dance make it a physical setup attacker, with Victory Dance raising Attack, Defense, and Speed in modern turn-based games. Adamant or Jolly suit Hisuian Lilligant, while Timid or Modest are natural for Unovan Lilligant; both forms remain vulnerable to common Grass weaknesses, and Hisuian Lilligant is especially vulnerable to Flying attacks.
competitive: Unovan Lilligant was a strong BW RU setup sweeper rather than a generic lower-tier Grass-type. Quiver Dance could simultaneously patch its Speed and Special Defense while pushing base 110 Special Attack to threatening levels, and Sleep Powder often created the free turn needed to begin that setup; Chlorophyll also gave it a secondary role on sun teams. Its recurring limitation was coverage, because Grass STAB plus Hidden Power or a small number of secondary options made Steel-, Fire-, Dragon-, and opposing Grass-types difficult to break without support. Hisuian Lilligant has a very different modern niche: in SV it is primarily a fast physical sun attacker, using Chlorophyll with Close Combat and strong Grass STAB or Victory Dance to function as speed control and a late-game cleaner. Hustle offers even more power but introduces an accuracy penalty, while Victory Dance can make it less dependent on sunlight by boosting Attack, Defense, and Speed at once. The two forms therefore share a setup-oriented identity but succeed through opposite attacking stats and different team structures.
nuzlocke: Petilil and both Lilligant forms can be effective in Nuzlockes, but their safety profiles are different. Unovan Lilligant can use Quiver Dance to improve both offense and special durability and can recover through Giga Drain, but Sleep Powder's imperfect accuracy makes it unsafe as the sole plan for surviving a dangerous opponent. Hisuian Lilligant is more physically aggressive and Victory Dance improves Defense while raising Attack and Speed, yet its Grass/Fighting typing adds weaknesses to Fairy, Psychic, and especially Flying, which deals quadruple damage. Chlorophyll can make either appropriate form extremely fast under sun, reducing incoming damage by letting it attack first, while Hustle should be used cautiously because the accuracy reduction can turn an otherwise favorable fight into a miss-and-death scenario. In runs where a Sun Stone is scarce, the timing of evolution also matters because evolving too early can alter which level-up moves are conveniently available.

pokemon.name: Petilil
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Petilil prefers moist, nutrient-rich soil near clean water, and areas where it lives are considered especially good for growing plants. The three leaves on its head are extremely bitter but can restore energy when eaten, dried, or brewed into an infusion, making the species popular with older people. Those leaves regrow after being removed, and their condition can indicate the Pokemon's health. Petilil leaves an area if the soil or water quality deteriorates.

pokemon.name: Lilligant
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Unovan Lilligant grows a large flower crown whose fragrance is calming and varies according to the soil in which the Pokemon was raised. Producing a perfect bloom is difficult even for skilled gardeners, and wild Lilligant are said to develop especially beautiful flowers. Essential oil made from the flower is highly prized and extremely expensive. Once blooming, the flower can wilt if Lilligant is neglected, and some Pokédex accounts say it also darkens and droops after the Pokemon finds a male partner.

pokemon.name: Lilligant
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Hisuian Lilligant developed long, powerful legs in the snowy mountains of ancient Hisui, allowing it to leap with exceptional height and grace. It fights with movements compared to ballet or dance, and the fragrance from its flower crown is said to hearten nearby people and Pokemon. A special Noble Hisuian Lilligant was revered in the Crimson Mirelands because of its descent from one of the ancient Pokemon blessed by Arceus.

playthrough: Basculin is a fast, aggressive pure Water Pokemon with base 92 Attack and 98 Speed, but only the White-Striped Form can evolve. Red-Striped Basculin commonly uses Reckless or Adaptability, Blue-Striped Basculin can use Rock Head or Adaptability, and White-Striped Basculin instead has Rattled or Adaptability; all three can have Mold Breaker as a Hidden Ability in modern games. White-Striped Basculin evolves into Basculegion after accumulating at least 294 HP of recoil damage without fainting, with the exact level-up requirement differing slightly in Legends: Arceus. Basculegion becomes Water/Ghost and gains enormous base 120 HP; males emphasize physical offense with base 112 Attack and 80 Special Attack, while females have base 92 Attack and 100 Special Attack. Swift Swim doubles Speed in rain, Adaptability increases the same-type attack bonus from 1.5 to 2 times, and Mold Breaker bypasses opposing abilities, giving either sex several viable approaches. Wave Crash, Aqua Jet, Shadow Ball, Hydro Pump, Flip Turn, and other coverage make the family dangerous, but recoil-heavy evolution and attacks require much more caution in ordinary story play than the raw offensive numbers suggest.
competitive: Red- and Blue-Striped Basculin were always niche lower-tier attackers, valued mostly for base 98 Speed, Adaptability-boosted Water STAB, and aggressive options such as Aqua Jet or recoil moves. Basculegion raised the family's competitive ceiling dramatically in Generation IX. Male Basculegion is the stronger physical wallbreaker, using base 112 Attack, Adaptability or Swift Swim, Wave Crash, and Aqua Jet, while female Basculegion trades 20 Attack for 20 Special Attack and functions more naturally as a special wallbreaker with Hydro Pump, Shadow Ball, and Flip Turn. Last Respects was so powerful on Basculegion and Houndstone that Smogon ultimately banned the move itself from SV OU after Pokémon HOME rather than leaving the Pokemon banned solely because of that one attack. Without Last Respects, the forms settled into more ordinary lower-tier roles—male Basculegion is currently NU and female Basculegion RU—but both remain dangerous rain abusers and Adaptability wallbreakers. Their middling base 78 Speed outside rain and limited defensive stats besides HP keep them manageable without the banned move.
nuzlocke: The Basculin family presents an unusual Nuzlocke dilemma because the evolution requirement itself asks White-Striped Basculin to take large amounts of recoil damage. The required 294 HP can be accumulated across battles and healed between them, but fainting resets the progress in ordinary modern mechanics—and in a permadeath run fainting would end the attempt entirely. Once evolved, Basculegion is much safer because base 120 HP, Normal and Fighting immunities, and Water/Ghost resistances create useful defensive opportunities, while Aqua Jet can finish weakened opponents before they move. Adaptability is the most straightforward damage ability, whereas Swift Swim can make Basculegion extremely fast in rain; Wave Crash is powerful but its recoil should be reserved for situations where the extra damage is truly necessary. The quadruple-free typing is useful, but Electric, Grass, Ghost, and Dark moves still hit super effectively, so its large HP pool should not encourage careless switching.

pokemon.name: Basculin
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Red-Striped Basculin are extremely aggressive, energetic fish that form schools and frequently fight Blue-Striped Basculin over territory. Their vitality allows populations to multiply rapidly. They are sometimes called the 'Thug of the River,' although larger predators such as Dondozo and Bombirdier still prey on them.

pokemon.name: Basculin
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Blue-Striped Basculin form schools largely with others of the same color and treat schools of Red-Striped Basculin as major rivals. Their jaws are powerful enough to leave tooth marks in sheets of iron. Like the red form, they are extremely vicious and territorial.

pokemon.name: Basculin
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: White-Striped Basculin live in cold seas, form cooperative schools, and share food with one another. When the proper season arrives, they migrate back toward the rivers where they were born. Their ecology differs so sharply from Red- and Blue-Striped Basculin that researchers have debated whether the white-striped population should be considered a separate species.

pokemon.name: Basculegion
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Basculegion forms when a White-Striped Basculin becomes possessed by the souls of other Basculin from its school that died during the dangerous upstream journey. Those spirits strengthen the survivor and attack with it, giving the species its Ghost typing. Male Basculegion are physically stronger than females and have red markings and more aggressive facial features.

pokemon.name: Basculegion
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Female Basculegion share the same origin as males, carrying the souls of Basculin that failed to survive their migration. They have pale blue markings, a softer or more mournful facial appearance, and shorter smoke-like facial structures. Their base statistics emphasize Special Attack rather than the stronger physical Attack of male Basculegion.

playthrough: Sandile evolves into Krokorok at level 29 and Krookodile at level 40, producing a Ground/Dark physical attacker with excellent offensive typing, base 117 Attack, and base 92 Speed. Krookodile's Defense was base 70 in Generation V and increased to 80 from Generation VI onward, slightly improving its ability to use Intimidate as a physical pivot. Earthquake and Crunch or later Knock Off form strong STAB, while Rock Slide or Stone Edge, Brick Break or Close Combat in later games, Gunk Shot, Stealth Rock, Taunt, and other coverage let it function as a breaker or utility attacker. Intimidate lowers opposing Attack on entry and is the safer all-purpose ability, while Moxie raises Krookodile's Attack after it scores a knockout and can quickly turn one KO into a sweep; Anger Point can maximize Attack after a critical hit but is much less predictable. Ground/Dark also gives complete Electric and Psychic immunities, although Water, Grass, Ice, Fighting, Bug, and later Fairy attacks are super effective. Jolly is usually ideal because base 92 Speed sits in a valuable but crowded range, while Adamant maximizes damage when the extra Speed is unnecessary.
competitive: Krookodile was a strong BW UU Pokemon and a common VGC 2011 choice because Intimidate, Moxie, Ground/Dark STAB, and base 92 Speed let it compress several roles into one slot. Choice Scarf sets were particularly effective: Earthquake and Crunch provided strong coverage, and Moxie could turn a revenge kill into a late-game sweep as Krookodile accumulated Attack boosts. Pursuit historically gave it an additional niche against Psychic- and Ghost-types, while later generations added stronger Knock Off, Stealth Rock, Taunt, and improved physical coverage. Its Defense increase from 70 to 80 after Generation V strengthened Intimidate utility sets, and modern SV Krookodile remains a strong RU progress-maker that can set hazards, remove items, and threaten sweeps with Choice items. Lack of reliable recovery and a large collection of common weaknesses keep it from functioning as a true wall, but few Ground-types have maintained such a consistent combination of offense, utility, and two premium immunities.
nuzlocke: Krookodile is a very strong Nuzlocke Pokemon because both Intimidate and Moxie are useful without complicated setup. Intimidate immediately reduces physical damage when Krookodile enters and is generally the safest ability, while Moxie can let it snowball through teams once the first knockout is secured. Electric and Psychic immunities provide completely safe switches against known moves, but Water, Grass, Ice, Fighting, Bug, and later Fairy coverage can be dangerous and the line's special bulk is only average. Earthquake and Crunch are accurate, powerful attacks that do not cause recoil or stat drops, making them particularly friendly to permadeath play. Jolly Krookodile is often safer than Adamant when the extra Speed prevents a retaliation, and Anger Point should be regarded as an occasional bonus rather than a strategy worth deliberately triggering with a critical hit.

pokemon.name: Sandile
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Sandile lives almost entirely in deserts and usually buries most of its body beneath the sand, leaving only its eyes and snout exposed. A dark membrane shields its eyes from blowing sand and harsh sunlight. Moving just beneath the hot surface also helps regulate Sandile's body temperature. In Alola, the warm climate allows the species to survive outside strictly desert habitats.

pokemon.name: Krokorok
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Krokorok lives in small desert groups usually led by a female, while males commonly gather food. The dark membrane around its eyes both protects against sandstorms and detects heat, allowing Krokorok to perceive warm objects and navigate in darkness. It dislikes cold and burrows deeply into warm sand at night. Krokorok also buries captured prey to preserve it for periods when hunting is unsuccessful.

pokemon.name: Krookodile
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Krookodile is an exceptionally aggressive desert predator whose powerful jaws can crush automobiles and tear through thick iron plate. Its eyes can focus over very long distances, helping it spot prey across open desert, and it can move through loose sand almost as if swimming through water. Krookodile sometimes cooperates with Flygon, hiding inside Flygon's sandstorms while hunting and then sharing the captured prey. It has been nicknamed the 'Bully of the Sands' because of its violent hunting behavior.

playthrough: Unovan Darumaka evolves into Darmanitan at level 35, while Galarian Darumaka evolves into Galarian Darmanitan with an Ice Stone. Standard Unovan Darmanitan is a Fire-type physical wallbreaker with base 140 Attack and 95 Speed, and Sheer Force boosts attacks with secondary effects by 30 percent while removing those secondary effects; Flare Blitz, Fire Punch, Rock Slide, Earthquake, Superpower, and U-turn give it excellent immediate offense. Its Hidden Ability Zen Mode activates at or below half HP, transforming it into Fire/Psychic with 140 Special Attack, 105 Defense, 105 Special Defense, and only 55 Speed, but deliberately dropping below half HP to access that state is awkward and dangerous in normal play. Galarian Darmanitan keeps the same Standard Mode stat spread but becomes pure Ice and uses Gorilla Tactics, which boosts Attack by 50 percent while locking it into the first selected move like a built-in Choice Band. Its Hidden Zen Mode instead transforms below half HP into Ice/Fire with base 160 Attack and 135 Speed. Jolly is often best for either offensive Standard Mode, while the Zen forms require very different planning and are generally less straightforward than simply using the powerful normal abilities.
competitive: Unovan Darmanitan has a long history as a terrifying UU-style wallbreaker. Base 140 Attack plus Sheer Force makes Flare Blitz extraordinarily difficult to switch into, and Choice Band or Choice Scarf sets use U-turn, Earthquake, Rock Slide, and Superpower to maintain offensive pressure; its main weaknesses are recoil, Stealth Rock, poor 55/55 defenses, and a base 95 Speed tier that is good rather than elite. Galarian Darmanitan was dramatically stronger. Gorilla Tactics effectively gives it a free Choice Band while still allowing a second held item, so Choice Scarf variants combined enormous power and Speed while Choice Band variants became almost impossible to wall; Smogon's SS OU council unanimously banned Galarian Darmanitan on December 29, 2019, and it thereafter competed in Ubers. Zen Mode has always been more specialized competitively because reaching half HP safely is unreliable, though Galarian Zen Mode's 160 Attack and 135 Speed are spectacular once active. The family therefore contains one historically strong lower-tier wallbreaker and one regional form powerful enough to be removed from standard OU play.
nuzlocke: Darmanitan can end fights extremely quickly, but it is also one of the easiest powerful Pokemon to lose through self-inflicted damage. Sheer Force-boosted attacks are excellent, yet Flare Blitz recoil can consume huge portions of Darmanitan's HP, and its 55/55 defenses mean that an opponent surviving the attack may retaliate very hard. Unovan Zen Mode and Galarian Zen Mode both require being at or below half health, a threshold that should generally be treated as an emergency state rather than a goal in a permadeath run. Galarian Darmanitan's Gorilla Tactics provides enormous damage without recoil by itself, but move locking can become dangerous if the next opposing Pokemon resists the selected attack. Rock, Ground, and Water threaten Unovan Darmanitan; Galarian Standard Mode is weak to Fire, Fighting, Rock, and Steel. Accurate non-recoil moves are often the safer option when they already guarantee the knockout.

pokemon.name: Darumaka
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Unovan Darumaka carries an internal flame that makes it hyperactive and difficult to calm while burning strongly. As the flame weakens it falls asleep, pulling its limbs into its body like a tumbler doll; even at rest its internal temperature remains around 1,100 degrees Fahrenheit. Ancient people reportedly placed Darumaka's unusually warm droppings inside clothing for heat. The species is also regarded as a symbol of good luck.

pokemon.name: Darumaka
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Galarian Darumaka developed a thick white coat after adapting to Galar's cold environment. Its ancestral flame sac has largely become dormant, and the species instead produces cold air and stores freezing energy. It is playful in snow and commonly forms snowballs, using them for both recreation and combat.

pokemon.name: Darmanitan
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Unovan Darmanitan is an intensely energetic Fire-type whose internal fire allows it to generate tremendous physical power. Its punches can destroy heavy structures, and it becomes particularly fierce when fighting. Despite its intimidating strength, Darmanitan can become calm and controlled when its energy is depleted enough to trigger Zen Mode.

pokemon.name: Darmanitan
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: When a Zen Mode Darmanitan falls below half health, its body hardens and the Pokemon becomes almost completely motionless. It enters a meditative state and shifts from relying on physical force to using sharpened mental and spiritual power, reflected by the form's Fire/Psychic typing and much higher Special Attack and defenses. It can remain in this calm state even while carrying out ordinary activities such as gathering food.

pokemon.name: Darmanitan
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Galarian Darmanitan adapted to cold climates by developing an organ that produces frigid air while its original flame sac became dormant. This change also altered its disposition from belligerent to gentle and timid. When humans approach, it may freeze in place and imitate a snowman. The large snowball on its head stores food and other objects and can be frozen solid for powerful headbutts.

pokemon.name: Darmanitan
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: When Galarian Darmanitan enters Zen Mode, its dormant flame sac reignites and its normally timid personality changes into an uncontrollable rage. The Pokemon begins hopping and spraying fire without regard for its surroundings or even for its own body as the heat melts parts of its icy form. It continues rampaging until the rage finally subsides.

playthrough: Maractus is a single-stage pure Grass Pokemon with base 106 Special Attack, 86 Attack, and only base 60 Speed, so it is better suited to deliberate offense or support than fast sweeping without weather. Giga Drain and Energy Ball provide reliable special STAB, while Spikes, Leech Seed, Synthesis, Sunny Day, Cotton Guard, Sucker Punch, and other utility can let it contribute beyond direct damage. Water Absorb grants a complete Water immunity and restores one-quarter of maximum HP when activated, Chlorophyll doubles Speed in harsh sunlight, and the Hidden Ability Storm Drain also creates a Water immunity while raising Special Attack when hit by Water moves. In Generation V sun teams, Chlorophyll can turn Maractus's poor natural Speed into a genuine advantage and strengthen Solar Beam-based offense, though its shallow special coverage remains a major limitation. Modest is the simplest offensive nature, while Calm can support a defensive Spikes role. Fire, Ice, Flying, Bug, and Poison attacks are all super effective, so Maractus should usually enter through its Water immunity or a resisted Ground or Grass move rather than neutral damage.
competitive: Maractus has never been a high-tier competitive Pokemon, but it has had a real niche in weather and hazard support. BW NU sun teams used Chlorophyll to bring its base 60 Speed to useful levels, allowing Maractus to set Spikes quickly while threatening opponents with base 106 Special Attack and sun-enabled Solar Beam. Water Absorb or Storm Drain can instead let it function as a Water-type switch-in, with Storm Drain providing a Special Attack boost and later sets adding Knock Off, Synthesis, and Giga Drain to a defensive-support toolkit. Smogon's SS analysis still treats Maractus as a niche Spikes setter because its typing, mediocre 75/67/67 bulk, and limited coverage leave it outclassed by sturdier Grass-types such as Roselia. Its competitive value therefore comes from unusual role combinations—Water immunity, Spikes, and strong Grass offense—rather than raw overall efficiency.
nuzlocke: Maractus can fill a useful Nuzlocke niche if it has Water Absorb or Storm Drain, because either ability provides a complete Water immunity and can create extremely safe switches against known Water attacks. Giga Drain and Synthesis can restore health, while Spikes provides teamwide value without requiring Maractus to defeat every opponent itself. The drawback is defensive consistency: base 75 HP with only 67 in both defenses is not enough to absorb strong neutral hits comfortably, and Fire, Ice, Flying, Bug, and Poison moves all hit super effectively. Chlorophyll can make Maractus very fast in sun but does nothing to solve those weaknesses if the opponent survives. Modest or Calm are both reasonable, and accurate Giga Drain is usually preferable to riskier or more situational high-power options when the damage is already sufficient.

pokemon.name: Maractus
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Maractus lives in arid desert regions and moves its cactus-like body rhythmically, producing rattling sounds similar to maracas. It combines those sounds with upbeat dances to scare away bird Pokemon that try to eat its flower seeds. Once each year, Maractus scatters nutrient-rich seeds across the desert, providing an important seasonal food source for other desert Pokemon.

playthrough: Dwebble evolves into Crustle at level 34, producing a Bug/Rock Pokemon with excellent base 125 Defense and, from Generation VI onward, base 105 Attack; in Generation V its Attack was 95. Rock Slide or Stone Edge and X-Scissor provide straightforward physical STAB, while Earthquake, Rock Blast, Stealth Rock, Spikes, and Shell Smash let Crustle function as either a utility lead or a setup attacker. Sturdy guarantees survival from full HP against one otherwise lethal hit in modern mechanics, Shell Armor prevents critical hits entirely, and Weak Armor can trade Defense for Speed when struck physically. Shell Smash is the defining offensive option because it sharply raises Attack, Special Attack, and Speed at the cost of both defenses, but base 45 Speed means Crustle still benefits from careful matchup planning even after boosting. Water, Rock, and Steel attacks are super effective, and Bug/Rock provides surprisingly few useful resistances for such a physically bulky Pokemon. Adamant is the most natural offensive nature, while Impish can reinforce a hazard-setting or Shell Armor role.
competitive: Crustle was a legitimate BW RU Pokemon whose best role was not conventional walling but hyper-offense support. Sturdy combined with both Stealth Rock and Spikes let it establish hazards reliably, while Shell Smash gave it the unusual ability to punish passive leads and potentially sweep rather than simply accept being sacrificed after setting hazards. Smogon specifically highlights the flexibility of Shell Smash lead sets, with Rock Blast, Earthquake, and X-Scissor allowing Crustle to pressure opposing leads after boosting. Later generations raised its Attack from 95 to 105 and changed Weak Armor so physical hits could provide even larger Speed boosts, but Crustle remained a lower-tier specialist because base 45 Speed, limited resistances, and a weakness to Stealth Rock made it high-maintenance. In SM ZU it still retained two coherent roles—Shell Smash sweeper and suicide hazard lead—showing that its competitive identity remained stable even as overall power creep increased.
nuzlocke: Crustle has two unusually Nuzlocke-friendly abilities. Sturdy can guarantee survival from full HP against a single otherwise lethal hit, while Shell Armor removes critical hits entirely and therefore makes physical damage far more predictable. The tradeoff is that Sturdy disappears as soon as chip damage breaks full health, and Shell Smash deliberately lowers both defenses, so the strongest competitive strategy is not always the safest permadeath strategy. Base 125 Defense allows Crustle to take many neutral physical hits, but Water, Rock, and Steel attacks are dangerous and its Special Defense is only average. Rock Slide is safer than Stone Edge when the extra power is unnecessary, while accurate X-Scissor and Earthquake reduce avoidable failure states. For a Nuzlocke, a Shell Armor or carefully maintained Sturdy Crustle used as a physical tank and hazard setter is usually safer than repeatedly trying to sweep with Shell Smash.

pokemon.name: Dwebble
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Dwebble searches carefully for a suitable rock to use as a shell, then secretes a corrosive liquid from its mouth to carve a cavity into the stone. If its shell breaks, it becomes agitated and will not settle down until it finds a replacement. This dependence on rocks makes Dwebble a natural rival of Roggenrola and Rolycoly. When no suitable stone can be found, Dwebble may live temporarily inside the sand ports of a Hippowdon, clearing trapped stones from those openings in exchange for protection.

pokemon.name: Crustle
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Crustle carries an enormous layered rock as a shell and has legs strong enough to haul that weight across dry terrain for long periods. Members of the species fight fiercely over territory, and a Crustle whose shell breaks during such a battle is considered defeated and may become weak and uncertain afterward. Its claws are powerful enough to break the armored carapace of a Rhyperior. Crustle dislikes rain and may refuse to emerge from its shell on rainy days.

playthrough: Scraggy evolves into Scrafty at level 39, giving the player a Dark/Fighting Pokemon with low base 58 Speed but excellent 115 Defense and 115 Special Defense. Drain Punch, High Jump Kick, Crunch or Knock Off, Ice Punch, Rock Slide, Poison Jab, Dragon Dance, and Bulk Up give Scrafty several viable physical routes. Shed Skin gives a 33 percent chance each turn to cure major status, Moxie raises Attack after every knockout, and the Hidden Ability Intimidate lowers opposing Attack on entry, making all three abilities useful in different ways. Dragon Dance compensates for Scrafty's low Speed, while Bulk Up and Drain Punch emphasize its natural bulk and longevity. From Generation VI onward, Fairy attacks are a severe problem because Dark/Fighting is quadruple weak to Fairy, while Flying and Fighting are also super effective. Adamant works well for immediate damage, Jolly can help Dragon Dance sets, and Careful is excellent for a slower Bulk Up approach.
competitive: Scrafty has enjoyed a durable lower-tier and doubles career because its 65/115/115 bulk, unusual Dark/Fighting typing, and three excellent abilities support several different roles. In singles it has used Dragon Dance with Moxie for sweeping and Bulk Up with Shed Skin plus Rest or Drain Punch for slow win conditions; by SM NU, Smogon still described it as a major setup threat capable of breaking common defensive cores. Intimidate gave it an even stronger identity in doubles and VGC, where Fake Out, Knock Off, Fighting STAB, and low Speed made it an effective support Pokemon on Trick Room teams; Smogon characterized it as one of the bulkiest Fake Out users in VGC 2018. Fairy typing dramatically worsened its defensive matchups from Generation VI onward by creating a quadruple weakness, but it did not erase Scrafty's utility. Mega Scrafty is a much newer form and should be evaluated separately: current data gives it 130 Attack, 135 Defense, 135 Special Defense, 68 Speed, and Intimidate, substantially improving the exact bulky-support profile that standard Scrafty has used for years without yet giving the Mega a long historical tier résumé.
nuzlocke: Scrafty is very safe in many Nuzlocke matchups because both defenses are base 115 and it has a complete Psychic immunity. Intimidate is the most immediately reliable ability for reducing physical damage, Shed Skin can unexpectedly cure burns, poison, paralysis, or sleep, and Moxie rewards clean knockouts without requiring a setup turn. Drain Punch is particularly valuable because it combines accurate Fighting STAB with healing, whereas High Jump Kick can inflict devastating crash damage if it misses or fails and is much less attractive under permadeath rules. Fairy attacks from Generation VI onward are the critical danger because they deal quadruple damage, and strong Flying or Fighting attacks also need respect. Mega Scrafty improves both defenses to 135 and Attack to 130, making it even harder to break, but its Fairy weakness remains just as severe.

pokemon.name: Scraggy
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Scraggy carries loose, rubbery skin around its legs and can pull that skin upward to reduce damage from attacks. It is highly confrontational and may headbutt anyone who meets its gaze, relying on an unusually hard skull despite the fact that the skull's weight makes balancing difficult. Scraggy travel in small groups and take pride in the looseness of their hanging skin, with baggier individuals receiving more respect. Evolution is associated with that skin becoming fully stretched.

pokemon.name: Scrafty
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Scrafty lives in territorial groups and attacks intruders, with social rank determined by the size of the red crest on the head; the individual with the largest crest becomes the leader. It can kick through concrete blocks and spit acidic liquid, while the loose skin around its body can be pulled up or folded to shield itself during combat. Despite its aggressive and arrogant reputation, Scrafty protects both its territory and individuals it cares about. A Scrafty may remain in the same territory for its entire life.

pokemon.name: Scrafty
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Mega Evolution turns Scrafty's shed skin from yellow to white and makes it much tougher and more resilient. The skin forms separate hood-like and trouser-like sections, giving Mega Scrafty heavier protection while leaving the tail exposed. It adopts an even more imposing slouched posture and is depicted cracking its neck when Mega Evolution activates. Its temperament remains feisty rather than becoming fundamentally different from the standard form.

playthrough: Sigilyph is a single-stage Psychic/Flying special attacker with base 103 Special Attack, 97 Speed, and respectable 72/80/80 bulk. Psychic or Psyshock and Air Slash provide dual STAB, while Ice Beam, Energy Ball, Heat Wave, Shadow Ball, Roost, Calm Mind, Cosmic Power, Stored Power, and Psycho Shift allow both straightforward offense and unconventional setup strategies. Magic Guard is the defining ability because Sigilyph takes damage only from direct attacks, ignoring poison, burn damage, weather, entry hazards, recoil from Life Orb, and many other forms of residual damage. Wonder Skin instead reduces the reliability of status moves used against it, while the Hidden Ability Tinted Lens doubles the damage of resisted attacks and makes its STAB much harder to switch into. Ground immunity and a quadruple Fighting resistance create excellent entry opportunities, but Dark, Electric, Ghost, Ice, and Rock attacks are super effective. Timid is generally ideal because preserving base 97 Speed matters greatly for both offensive and Cosmic Power sets.
competitive: Sigilyph was a major BW RU threat because Magic Guard interacts extraordinarily well with its movepool. The famous Cosmic Power set used Flame Orb to burn Sigilyph without taking burn damage, Psycho Shift to transfer that burn to an opponent, Roost for recovery, and Stored Power to become stronger as Cosmic Power repeatedly raised both defenses. Magic Guard also lets offensive sets use Life Orb without recoil or ignore Stealth Rock despite the Flying typing, while Tinted Lens provides an alternative approach that punishes nominal Psychic- or Flying-resistant switch-ins. Smogon describes Sigilyph as one of the standout threats in BW RU, and it also had legitimate VGC 2011 utility through Tailwind and Magic Guard. Its moderate raw bulk and five weaknesses keep it from being universally safe, but the combination of residual-damage immunity, recovery, setup, and a strong base 103 Special Attack gives it an unusually distinctive competitive identity.
nuzlocke: Magic Guard makes Sigilyph exceptionally useful in Nuzlockes because it eliminates many sources of gradual or indirect damage that normally create unexpected deaths. Poison and burn chip, sand or hail damage, entry hazards, and Life Orb recoil do not damage a Magic Guard Sigilyph, while its Ground immunity and strong Fighting resistance create predictable switches. The Cosmic Power and Stored Power strategy can become extremely safe once several boosts are established, but setting up repeatedly is dangerous against critical hits or strong super-effective Dark, Electric, Ghost, Ice, and Rock moves. Psycho Shift can transfer a status condition, but intentionally activating Flame Orb for competitive purposes is often unnecessary in a permadeath run when simpler attacks already win. Timid Sigilyph is safest when its Speed and immunities are used proactively rather than relying only on accumulated defensive boosts.

pokemon.name: Sigilyph
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Sigilyph is a constantly levitating Psychic-type associated with deserts, ruins, and an ancient civilization. It retains memories of guarding an ancient city and follows the same flight route over and over as if continuing its old patrol. Anyone entering the territory it watches can be attacked with psychic power. Its behavior is therefore unusually ritualized, with modern individuals still performing a protective function tied to a civilization that no longer exists.

playthrough: Ordinary Yamask evolves into Cofagrigus at level 34, while Galarian Yamask follows a unique route to Runerigus: after taking at least 49 HP of qualifying damage without fainting, it must pass beneath a specific stone arch or equivalent landmark. Cofagrigus is pure Ghost with base 145 Defense, 105 Special Defense, 95 Special Attack, and only base 30 Speed, making it excellent for Trick Room, Will-O-Wisp, Shadow Ball, Nasty Plot, Hex, Toxic Spikes in later games, and physical walling. Its Mummy ability replaces the Ability of a Pokemon that makes contact with Cofagrigus, which can disable dangerous effects such as Huge Power, Guts, or other contact-dependent offensive advantages. Runerigus is Ground/Ghost with the same 58/145/105 defensive core but base 95 Attack instead of Cofagrigus's 95 Special Attack; Earthquake, Poltergeist or Shadow Claw, Stealth Rock, Toxic Spikes, Will-O-Wisp, and Trick Room suit its physical profile. Wandering Spirit swaps Runerigus's Ability with that of an opponent that makes contact, producing more complex interactions than Mummy. Quiet is excellent for offensive Trick Room Cofagrigus, while Impish or Careful suit defensive Runerigus.
competitive: Cofagrigus was a strong BW UU Pokemon because its base 145 Defense and Ghost typing made it one of the tier's most reliable answers to powerful Fighting-types while simultaneously blocking Rapid Spin. Mummy weakened physical attackers that relied heavily on their abilities, and Cofagrigus was not purely passive: base 95 Special Attack, Nasty Plot, Shadow Ball, Hidden Power Fighting in the era, and Trick Room supported a dangerous offensive set in addition to defensive Will-O-Wisp builds. Runerigus inherited the same extraordinary physical Defense but shifted into a Ground/Ghost utility role with Stealth Rock, Toxic Spikes, Earthquake, and Wandering Spirit. Smogon places Runerigus in SS ZU and notes that its excellent physical bulk and wide support movepool are offset by five common weaknesses and the absence of reliable recovery, leaving it easier to wear down than the defensive stats suggest. The family therefore contains two related but strategically distinct walls: Cofagrigus is the stronger special attacker and historical spinblocker, while Runerigus offers Ground STAB, an Electric immunity, hazards, and ability-swapping utility.
nuzlocke: Cofagrigus is one of the safer physical walls available in a Nuzlocke because base 145 Defense, Normal and Fighting immunities, and Mummy can neutralize dangerous contact-based abilities. Its base 58 HP is much lower than the defenses imply, however, and strong Dark or Ghost attacks can still break through quickly; recovery is also limited compared with dedicated walls that have Recover or Slack Off. Trick Room can turn base 30 Speed into an advantage, but the safest use is usually Will-O-Wisp, reliable Ghost damage, and deliberate immunity switches. Runerigus adds an Electric immunity and Rock resistance but gains weaknesses to Water, Grass, Ice, Ghost, and Dark, so its Ground/Ghost typing is more matchup-dependent. The evolution requirement for Galarian Yamask is itself risky under permadeath rules because it must accumulate at least 49 HP of attack damage without fainting, so the process should be performed against carefully selected weak opponents rather than during an important battle.

pokemon.name: Yamask
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Unovan Yamask is said to arise from the spirit of a human buried in a grave long ago. It retains memories of its former human life and carries a golden mask shaped like the face it once had, sometimes staring at that mask and crying. Yamask becomes furious if the mask is taken away and may wander ruins searching for someone who recognizes its former face. In animation, a human wearing the mask can even be possessed by the Yamask.

pokemon.name: Yamask
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Galarian Yamask is bound to a fragment of an ancient clay slab covered in cursed markings rather than carrying the golden human-face mask of the Unovan form. Pokédex accounts describe the slab as absorbing Yamask's dark power, while other accounts say a vengeful spirit and cursed tablet became bound together. The slab is swung as a weapon and becomes part of the completed rune image when Yamask evolves into Runerigus.

pokemon.name: Cofagrigus
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Cofagrigus resembles an ornate golden sarcophagus and inhabits tombs and ancient ruins. Legends claim it traps grave robbers who mistake it for an ordinary coffin, swallowing them into its body and turning them into mummies. It is said to have once been human but no longer remembers its former life, in contrast with Yamask's retained memories. Cofagrigus consumes gold nuggets and has historically been used as a symbol of the wealth of ancient kings.

pokemon.name: Runerigus
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Runerigus forms when the cursed painting carried by Galarian Yamask absorbs the Pokemon's spirit and reassembles into a larger clay slab. Its body depicts a red serpent-like figure held together by shadowy tendrils. Anyone who touches the shadowy parts of Runerigus is forced to experience the memories connected to the creation of the ancient painting. Reassembly of the slab allows the curse's malicious power to be fully released.

playthrough: Tirtouga evolves into Carracosta at level 37, producing a Water/Rock Pokemon with base 108 Attack, enormous base 133 Defense, and extremely low base 32 Speed. Waterfall, Aqua Jet, Stone Edge or Rock Slide, Rock Blast, Earthquake, Crunch, and Shell Smash support a powerful physical setup role, while Stealth Rock and its defensive abilities also allow more conservative play. Solid Rock reduces damage from super-effective attacks to three-quarters of normal, Sturdy guarantees survival from full HP against one otherwise lethal hit, and the Hidden Ability Swift Swim doubles Speed in rain. Shell Smash raises both offenses and Speed by two stages while lowering both defenses by one, making Carracosta dramatically faster and stronger but less safe if the target survives. Water/Rock resists Fire particularly well but is weak to Electric, Fighting, and Ground and quadruple weak to Grass. Adamant maximizes physical damage, while Jolly can matter after Shell Smash by improving which fast opponents Carracosta can overtake.
competitive: Carracosta was one of BW NU's premier Shell Smash sweepers. Base 108 Attack, base 133 Defense, Water/Rock STAB, and Solid Rock let it set up on attacks that would force out frailer sweepers, while Sturdy could instead guarantee survival from full HP and Aqua Jet gave it priority to finish weakened Choice Scarf users even after a Speed boost failed to outrun them. Smogon describes Carracosta as one of the tier's best setup sweepers and also notes that Stealth Rock, Curse, and defensive sets gave it useful alternatives to all-in Shell Smash offense. It remained effective in later lower tiers, including SM PU, because the core combination of Shell Smash, priority, physical bulk, and strong STAB never stopped being threatening. Its weaknesses are equally enduring: base 32 Speed is terrible before setup, Grass attacks deal quadruple damage, and special bulk is only base 65, so faster special attackers or priority can punish it after Shell Smash lowers its defenses.
nuzlocke: Carracosta can be extremely safe against physical attacks but dangerously fragile in the wrong matchup. Sturdy provides a one-hit safety net from full HP, while Solid Rock reduces all super-effective damage and can make ordinary Electric, Fighting, or Ground coverage more survivable than expected. Grass attacks remain a severe exception because they deal quadruple damage, and base 65 Special Defense means strong special Grass moves can be lethal even through Solid Rock. Aqua Jet is excellent for finishing faster weakened opponents, while Rock Slide is generally safer than Stone Edge when the extra power is unnecessary. Shell Smash can win boss fights immediately but lowers both defenses, so in a permadeath run it should be used only when the opposing moveset and expected damage are well understood.

pokemon.name: Tirtouga
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Tirtouga lived in warm ancient seas roughly 100 million years ago and survives in the modern era primarily through fossil restoration. Its shell is strong enough to withstand dives to depths of around 1,000 meters, yet it was not restricted to the ocean and actively crawled onto land while hunting. Its hunting range therefore extended from deep water to terrestrial environments. Researchers consider Tirtouga a likely ancestor of many modern turtle Pokemon.

pokemon.name: Carracosta
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Carracosta was a powerful ancient predator that hunted both in the ocean and on land. It can hide inside its shell and resemble a boulder while waiting to ambush prey, then use its strong flippers and jaws to overpower the target. Its bite is strong enough to crush rocks and steel frames, and Carracosta consumes shells and bones along with flesh; those hard materials help reinforce its own shell. Because it moves relatively slowly on land, Carracosta may drag terrestrial prey into the water before finishing the hunt, and fossil-era prey included Omanyte and Omastar.

playthrough: Archen evolves into Archeops at level 37, producing one of the most offensively gifted Fossil Pokemon in the series: base 140 Attack, 112 Special Attack, and 110 Speed. Rock/Flying STAB through Acrobatics, Rock Slide or Stone Edge, and later options such as Dual Wingbeat combines with Earthquake, Crunch, U-turn, Heat Wave, Dragon Claw, and Roost to support physical or mixed offense. The enormous drawback is Defeatist, which halves both Attack and Special Attack whenever Archeops is at half of its maximum HP or lower, so maintaining health is far more important for this family than for most sweepers. Rock/Flying also creates weaknesses to Water, Electric, Ice, Rock, and Steel, while base 65 Defense and Special Defense mean Archeops can fall into Defeatist range after only one strong neutral hit. Jolly is usually ideal because preserving base 110 Speed helps prevent damage entirely, while Naive or Hasty can support mixed coverage. In a normal playthrough Archeops is extraordinarily strong when healthy, but much less forgiving than its raw offensive stats suggest.
competitive: Archeops was a major offensive threat in BW RU and retained a legitimate UU niche despite Defeatist. Its 140 Attack, 112 Special Attack, and 110 Speed let it use Flying Gem Acrobatics, Stone Edge, Earthquake, Head Smash, U-turn, and special coverage to pressure nearly every conventional switch-in, and Smogon described it as an offensive juggernaut when properly supported. Defeatist is the entire reason those near-legendary offensive stats did not push Archeops into much higher tiers: once it falls to half HP or below, both attacking stats are cut in half, and a Stealth Rock weakness makes repeated switching particularly punishing. Roost can sometimes restore Archeops above the threshold, while U-turn preserves momentum but risks additional hazard damage later. Later generations continued to use Archeops as a fast lower-tier attacker or occasional suicide lead, but the ability has consistently prevented it from converting elite raw stats into elite long-term tier placement.
nuzlocke: Archeops can be devastating in a Nuzlocke because base 110 Speed and 140 Attack often allow it to eliminate dangerous opponents before they act. The central safety rule is to keep it above half HP: once Defeatist activates, both offenses are halved and a fight that looked like a clean one-hit knockout can suddenly become a dangerous two-turn exchange. Its Ground immunity and resistances to Normal, Fire, Flying, Bug, and Poison provide planned switch opportunities, but five weaknesses and mediocre defenses mean blind switching is risky. Head Smash is especially dangerous under permadeath rules because recoil can activate Defeatist or simply remove too much HP, while Rock Slide or other accurate non-recoil options are usually safer when they already secure the knockout. Jolly Archeops is best used as a healthy fast attacker rather than a Pokemon expected to absorb damage and continue sweeping afterward.

pokemon.name: Archen
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Archen is an extinct feathered reptile revived from fossils. It was once widely believed to be the ancestor of all bird Pokemon, although later research has cast doubt on that conclusion. Its wings are too weak for true flight, so it lives in trees, hops between branches, and glides to seize prey. Animated portrayals also show Archen preferring certain naturally grown Berries over ordinary prepared Pokemon food.

pokemon.name: Archeops
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Archeops can fly, but its wing muscles are comparatively weak and it is much more naturally adapted to running. To become airborne it must build up substantial speed on the ground, with Pokédex descriptions stating that it may run close to 25 miles per hour over a long distance before taking off. All four limbs carry flight feathers, giving the species an unusual four-winged profile. Its fragile plumage and awkward takeoff requirements make its flight ability much less effortless than that of most modern Flying-type Pokemon.

playthrough: Trubbish evolves into Garbodor at level 36, producing a pure Poison Pokemon with balanced physical bulk, base 95 Attack, and excellent access to entry hazards. Gunk Shot or Poison Jab provides STAB, while Seed Bomb, Drain Punch, Rock Blast, Body Slam, Stomping Tantrum in later games, and Explosion or utility coverage give it enough offense to avoid complete passivity. Spikes and Toxic Spikes are the family's most distinctive support tools, allowing Garbodor to weaken entire opposing teams over repeated switches. Stench can cause flinches with damaging moves, Weak Armor trades Defense for Speed after physical hits, and the Hidden Ability Aftermath damages a contact attacker when Garbodor is knocked out, although the last effect is naturally undesirable in a Nuzlocke. Poison typing grants resistances to Grass, Fighting, Poison, Bug, and Fairy from Generation VI onward and automatically absorbs Toxic Spikes upon switching in while grounded. Adamant or Impish are sensible depending on whether the player values offense or physical durability.
competitive: Garbodor was one of BW NU's premier Spikes users and one of the few fully evolved Pokemon in the tier with access to both Spikes and Toxic Spikes. Its Poison typing, respectable physical bulk, lack of a Stealth Rock weakness, and ability to punish contact through Rocky Helmet plus Aftermath made it especially effective at repeatedly setting hazards against Fighting-types and passive defensive Pokemon. Clear Smog prevented setup sweepers from exploiting it freely, while Pain Split in relevant generations gave limited recovery and Gunk Shot ensured that Taunt did not make it useless. Later generations preserved this identity, with Garbodor repeatedly appearing in lower tiers as a durable hazard setter rather than a conventional sweeper. Gigantamax Garbodor has a separate Generation VIII doubles-oriented niche because G-Max Malodor damages all opposing targets and poisons them, but Gigantamax does not alter Garbodor's base statistics and is tied to Dynamax formats rather than representing a permanently stronger evolution.
nuzlocke: Garbodor is a useful Nuzlocke support Pokemon because pure Poison typing provides several resistances, removes Toxic Spikes simply by entering the field, and its defenses are solid enough to handle many physical neutral attacks. Spikes can make long trainer battles progressively safer by weakening every grounded opponent that switches in, while Toxic Spikes can wear down bulky teams without requiring Garbodor to stay exposed.
