Gunk Shot is powerful but inaccurate, so Poison Jab or another reliable move is usually safer when the extra damage is unnecessary. Weak Armor can become dangerous because a physical hit lowers Defense even while increasing Speed, and Aftermath only activates when Garbodor faints, so neither should be treated as a primary survival plan. Gigantamax Garbodor is considerably safer in formats where Dynamax is available because of the temporary HP increase, while G-Max Malodor adds guaranteed teamwide poison pressure without changing its underlying weaknesses to Ground and Psychic.

pokemon.name: Trubbish
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Trubbish is an artificial Pokemon believed to have originated when household garbage and industrial waste underwent a chemical reaction. It lives in unsanitary places and feeds on trash, rotten food, and other refuse. The gases it belches are highly toxic and can leave a person bedridden for days, with especially vulnerable children and young Pokemon at greater risk. Once Trubbish forms a close bond with someone, however, it can stop producing the foul odor around that person.

pokemon.name: Garbodor
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Garbodor consumes garbage and incorporates the waste into its own body, with the exact composition of its poison changing according to what it has eaten. It sprays extremely toxic liquid from the fingertips of its right hand and uses its heavier left arm to seize or strike opponents. The species thrives around landfills and other heavily polluted areas. In Alola, introduced Grimer and Muk preyed on Garbodor so heavily that the population declined, with surviving individuals reportedly becoming stronger.

pokemon.name: Garbodor
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Gigantamax energy greatly thickens Garbodor's toxic gas until it visibly congeals into masses resembling discarded toys, vehicles, dolls, a Master Ball, and other refuse embedded around its enormous body. It can release toxic gas from both its mouth and fingers. Pokédex descriptions warn that this gas can penetrate victims deeply enough for the toxins to reach the bones. The form is therefore essentially a gigantic living landfill whose pollution has become physically denser and more dangerous.

playthrough: Unovan Zorua evolves into Zoroark at level 30, while Hisuian Zorua evolves into Hisuian Zoroark at the same level. Standard Zoroark is a pure Dark special attacker with base 120 Special Attack, 105 Attack, and 105 Speed, while Hisuian Zoroark shifts slightly toward special offense with base 125 Special Attack and 110 Speed. Both use Illusion, appearing as the last eligible Pokemon in the party until direct damage breaks the disguise, which can bait opponents into selecting ineffective or resisted moves if party order is planned carefully. Standard Zoroark uses Dark Pulse or Night Daze with Flamethrower, Focus Blast, U-turn, Nasty Plot, and physical coverage, while Hisuian Zoroark's Normal/Ghost typing gives it complete immunities to Normal, Fighting, and Ghost and only one conventional weakness, Dark. Bitter Malice is strongly associated with the Hisuian form in Legends: Arceus, while Shadow Ball, Hyper Voice, Flamethrower, Focus Blast, and Nasty Plot support modern special sets. Timid is excellent for either form because their low 60-range defenses make moving first far more important than trying to absorb damage.
competitive: Standard Zoroark was a niche but dangerous BW UU wallbreaker because Illusion created unique information and prediction advantages. Its 120 Special Attack, 105 Speed, Nasty Plot, Dark Pulse or Night Daze, Flamethrower, Focus Blast, U-turn, and mixed options could punish opponents that selected moves based on the Pokemon Zoroark appeared to be, although entry-hazard damage and careful scouting often exposed the disguise. Its poor 60/60 defenses prevented it from functioning as a normal pivot, so Illusion was most valuable when it manufactured one crucial free turn. Hisuian Zoroark improved the underlying offensive profile with 125 Special Attack, 110 Speed, and an exceptional Normal/Ghost typing that grants three immunities and only a Dark weakness, and modern SV Smogon places it in RUBL with viable UU usage. Even there, Illusion remains stronger as a mind-game tool than as guaranteed deception because hazards, team preview, and damage calculations can reveal the disguise. Both forms therefore succeed through offensive pressure plus uncertainty rather than durability.
nuzlocke: Zoroark can be excellent in Nuzlockes when Illusion is deliberately planned rather than treated as a cosmetic gimmick. By placing a teammate with very different weaknesses in the final party slot, Zoroark can sometimes lure the AI into using a move that Zoroark resists or ignores, creating a free attack or setup turn; the disguise itself does not change Zoroark's real typing or defenses. Standard Zoroark has a Psychic immunity but is weak to Fighting, Bug, and later Fairy, while Hisuian Zoroark is considerably safer defensively because Normal/Ghost grants Normal, Fighting, and Ghost immunities and leaves Dark as its only ordinary weakness. Both forms are still physically and specially frail, so once Illusion breaks they should not remain in unfavorable matchups. Timid is especially useful, and direct reliable attacks are safer than betting a run on repeated Illusion mind games after the opponent has already revealed its moves.

pokemon.name: Zorua
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Unovan Zorua is a mischievous illusionist that disguises itself as other Pokemon and sometimes even as human children. It uses these disguises to surprise others, obtain food, or escape danger rather than physically transforming its body. Inexperienced Zorua may fail to hide the tail when imitating a human, and touching the tail can break the illusion. The species is playful and enjoys startling people.

pokemon.name: Zorua
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Hisuian Zorua is a Normal/Ghost form created from the spirits of Zorua that died after humans drove them into the harsh environment of ancient Hisui. Their resentment toward humans and other Pokemon rebirthed them as ghostly creatures. The wispy fur on the head releases spiteful energy that creates frightening illusions, often taking the appearance of the victim itself. Hisuian Zorua appears to draw strength from the terror these illusions cause.

pokemon.name: Zoroark
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Zoroark creates illusions convincing enough to deceive large groups of people simultaneously and can even cover entire forest areas with false scenery to hide its den. The illusions do not represent physical transformation, and ordinary Zoroark illusions do not directly injure the target, even when they appear completely real. Zoroark lives in tightly bonded groups and is fiercely protective of its pack, especially Zorua. It may carry young Zorua inside its mane and retaliate harshly against humans or Pokemon that threaten its family.

pokemon.name: Zoroark
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Hisuian Zoroark resembles a ghostly embodiment of death and channels intense malice through its long white-and-red fur. Unlike the purely deceptive illusions of ordinary Zoroark, its spiteful illusions can inflict genuine physical and psychological harm, with descriptions claiming that terror from them can drive victims toward madness. It attacks enemies so recklessly that the same bitter energy can injure its own body. Despite its hatred toward most living beings, Hisuian Zoroark can become deeply protective and compassionate toward Hisuian Zorua or trusted companions.

playthrough: Minccino evolves into Cinccino with a Shiny Stone, producing a very fast pure Normal attacker with base 115 Speed and base 95 Attack. Tail Slap is the signature-style centerpiece, while Rock Blast and Bullet Seed provide valuable coverage; the Hidden Ability Skill Link guarantees that all of these multi-hit moves strike the maximum five times. Technician instead increases moves of 60 base power or less by 50 percent and can support a different group of weaker attacks, while Cute Charm is much less consistent. Skill Link Tail Slap is usually the easiest way to exploit Cinccino's stats because five hits can break Substitute, Focus Sash, Sturdy, and other single-hit defensive effects while dealing strong total damage. U-turn, Knock Off in later generations, Encore, Thunder Wave, and Triple Axel in some formats provide additional utility or coverage, but 75/60/60 bulk means Cinccino should rarely be used as a switch-in. Jolly is generally ideal because maintaining the excellent base 115 Speed is central to its safety.
competitive: Cinccino was a major BW RU offensive threat, where Skill Link allowed Tail Slap to hit all five times and reach extremely high effective power while also breaking Substitute and Focus Sash. Rock Blast and Bullet Seed received the same guaranteed five-hit treatment, giving Cinccino unusually strong coverage from moves that are normally inconsistent. Base 115 Speed made it one of the fastest Pokemon in the tier and let it outrun threats such as Scolipede, while U-turn preserved momentum. Its weaknesses were equally clear: base 95 Attack is good rather than exceptional without Skill Link, Steel- and Ghost-types could wall older movepools, and 75/60/60 bulk meant almost any serious neutral attack could remove it. Later generations added useful tools such as Knock Off and other coverage, but Cinccino has remained a fast lower-tier cleaner whose entire competitive ceiling rises dramatically when Skill Link is available.
nuzlocke: Cinccino is attractive in Nuzlockes because base 115 Speed prevents many opponents from moving and Skill Link removes the randomness from multi-hit moves. A five-hit Tail Slap, Bullet Seed, or Rock Blast can break Sturdy or Focus Sash and still continue dealing damage, which is especially valuable against opponents that would otherwise survive one hit and retaliate. The drawback is accuracy: Tail Slap and Rock Blast can still miss entirely even though Skill Link guarantees five hits after they connect, so reliable alternatives may be safer when the extra power is unnecessary. Pure Normal leaves only a Fighting weakness and provides a Ghost immunity, but Cinccino has almost no natural resistances and poor defenses. Jolly Cinccino is safest as a fast cleaner brought in after a KO or through a Ghost immunity rather than as a general-purpose pivot.

pokemon.name: Minccino
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Minccino is obsessed with cleanliness and uses its long fluffy tail like a broom or mop to clean its den and any dirty objects it encounters. It also brushes other Minccino with the tail as a greeting, and the individual with the fluffier tail tends to act more proudly. Minccino prefers clean habitats and washes its own tail in clear spring water whenever it becomes dirty. Its compulsive cleaning can make it useful around humans, although the behavior can also become excessive.

pokemon.name: Cinccino
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Cinccino's extremely soft white fur is coated in a special oil that repels dust, reduces static electricity, and helps attacks slide away from the body. It spreads the same oil around its nest to keep the living area clean. The oil is valuable to humans and is sold as a treatment for irritated or unhealthy skin. Cinccino is therefore naturally protected from dirt in a way that complements Minccino's behavioral obsession with cleaning.

playthrough: Gothita evolves into Gothorita at level 32 and Gothitelle at level 41, producing a slow but bulky pure Psychic Pokemon with base 95 Defense, 110 Special Defense, and 95 Special Attack. Psychic or Psyshock provides reliable STAB, while Thunderbolt, Energy Ball, Shadow Ball, Calm Mind, Trick Room, Reflect, Light Screen, Thunder Wave, and later support options let Gothitelle function as either a special tank or utility attacker. Frisk reveals opposing held items and can provide valuable information in ordinary play, Competitive raises Special Attack sharply when an opponent lowers one of Gothitelle's stats in generations where that ability is available, and the Hidden Ability Shadow Tag prevents many opposing Pokemon from switching. Base 65 Speed is poor for normal offense but useful under Trick Room, while 70/95/110 bulk gives Gothitelle enough time to set support moves or Calm Mind. Bug, Ghost, and Dark attacks are the main weaknesses. Modest or Calm are straightforward choices, while Quiet is especially useful on a dedicated Trick Room team.
competitive: Gothitelle's competitive history is defined far more by Shadow Tag than by its raw statistics. In BW and later generations, Shadow Tag let Gothitelle trap selected opposing Pokemon and prevent normal switching, allowing it to remove passive walls or support targets with combinations of Taunt, Trick, Calm Mind, Rest, Psychic, coverage, and Choice items. That same mechanic made Gothitelle valuable in doubles, where trapping both opposing positions could create temporary two-on-one situations and pair naturally with Trick Room or Helping Hand. Because trapping is extraordinarily powerful, Shadow Tag has repeatedly been restricted or banned in many standard singles environments, meaning Gothitelle can be listed in a low usage tier while still appearing in Ubers or specialized formats where the ability is legal. Without Shadow Tag, Gothitelle is simply a bulky but slow Psychic-type with modest offensive pressure; with it, the Pokemon can fundamentally alter the opponent's ability to reposition. Modern SV analysis still uses this trapping identity in Ubers-oriented formats despite Gothitelle's ordinary ZU usage tier.
nuzlocke: Gothitelle is much safer in a Nuzlocke than its Speed suggests because 95 Defense and 110 Special Defense give it reliable mixed bulk, and Frisk can reveal dangerous held items before they cause an unexpected problem. Trick Room can reverse the Speed disadvantage for several turns, while screens, Thunder Wave, Calm Mind, and accurate Psychic attacks support controlled fights without requiring risky recoil or low-accuracy moves. Shadow Tag can be useful for preventing an opponent from escaping, but AI trainers rarely switch as aggressively as competitive players, so the ability is generally less transformative in a story run than in PvP. Bug, Ghost, and Dark coverage should still be respected, particularly from strong physical attackers before Gothitelle has boosted. Calm is excellent for special tanking, while Quiet makes sense when deliberately building around Trick Room.

pokemon.name: Gothita
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Gothita amplifies psychic power through the bow-like sensory structures around its head. It often stares fixedly at something that other creatures cannot see and can become so absorbed in that observation that it fails to notice an incoming attack. Gothita is usually quiet and innocent, but it sometimes makes muted cries even while alone. Some researchers interpret those sounds as communication with invisible beings.

pokemon.name: Gothorita
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Gothorita draws psychic power from starlight and can arrange rocks into patterns resembling constellations. Its hypnosis is powerful enough to control both people and Pokemon and lead them away from familiar places. Folklore surrounding the species is much darker than Gothita's, including stories that Gothorita puts children to sleep and carries them away, which has earned it the title 'Witch of Punishment.' Claims that the species itself came from outer space remain unconfirmed.

pokemon.name: Gothitelle
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Gothitelle can distort the space around itself with immense psychic power, creating visions of distant stars and even images connected to past events. By studying the positions and movements of stars, it can predict the future with remarkable accuracy. Pokédex accounts say Gothitelle may become visibly sorrowful after seeing the remaining lifespan of a beloved Trainer. Despite the unsettling scope of its psychic abilities, the species is described as disliking conflict.

playthrough: Solosis evolves into Duosion at level 32 and Reuniclus at level 41, producing an extremely slow but powerful pure Psychic special attacker with base 125 Special Attack, 110 HP, and only base 30 Speed. Psychic or Psyshock provides reliable STAB, while Shadow Ball, Focus Blast, Energy Ball, Thunder, Recover, Calm Mind, Trick Room, and later coverage options let Reuniclus function as either a bulky setup attacker or dedicated Trick Room sweeper. Magic Guard is the standout ability because it prevents indirect damage from poison, burn, weather, entry hazards, recoil from Life Orb, and many other passive effects; Overcoat instead protects against weather damage and, from Generation VI onward, powder moves, while the Hidden Ability Regenerator restores one-third of maximum HP whenever Reuniclus switches out. Its terrible Speed becomes an advantage under Trick Room, where a Quiet nature and low Speed investment let Reuniclus move before most opponents while using its enormous Special Attack. Bug, Ghost, and Dark moves remain the main threats, and physical attackers can exploit the merely base 75 Defense if Reuniclus has not boosted. Quiet is ideal for Trick Room, while Modest, Bold, or Calm can support slower bulky sets.
competitive: Reuniclus was a genuine BW OU staple and one of the generation's defining bulky Psychic-types. Magic Guard makes it immune to virtually every form of passive damage, allowing it to ignore sand, hazards, Toxic damage, and Life Orb recoil, which gives it an extraordinary matchup against defensive teams that rely on gradual wear rather than direct attacks. Calm Mind plus Recover turns Reuniclus into a durable win condition, while Trick Room sets use base 30 Speed, base 125 Special Attack, and recoil-free Life Orb to become powerful offensive sweepers; it was also one of VGC 2011 and VGC 2012's strongest Trick Room setters for the same reasons. Duosion even developed its own lower-tier niche with Eviolite and Magic Guard, functioning as a bulky Calm Mind user despite not being fully evolved. Later generations moved Reuniclus into lower usage tiers as power creep increased, but Magic Guard, Regenerator, Recover, Calm Mind, Future Sight, and Trick Room have kept it strategically relevant for many generations rather than reducing it to a historical curiosity.
nuzlocke: Reuniclus is exceptionally safe in Nuzlockes when it has Magic Guard because poison, burn chip, weather, entry hazards, and other indirect damage simply cannot reduce its HP. Recover provides reliable healing, while Trick Room can turn its awful Speed into a major advantage and allow Reuniclus to attack before much faster opponents for several turns. Regenerator is also excellent if the Hidden Ability is available because switching restores health without spending a turn, while Overcoat can protect against weather and later powder effects. The main danger is direct super-effective damage from Bug, Ghost, and Dark moves, particularly strong physical attacks against its lower Defense. Quiet or Bold are both useful depending on whether the player wants a Trick Room attacker or a safer bulky pivot, and accurate Psychic or Psyshock is usually preferable to gambling on Focus Blast unless the coverage is truly necessary.

pokemon.name: Solosis
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Solosis is enclosed in a green, gel-like liquid that protects its body and allows it to survive in extremely hostile environments, including the vacuum of space. Heavy impacts can cause some of that protective fluid to leak away. It communicates telepathically and uses psychic power to drive away threats. The species' cellular appearance reflects a body structure that remains largely suspended inside its protective membrane.

pokemon.name: Duosion
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Duosion has two separate brains that can think independently, sometimes causing the Pokemon to attempt two different actions at once. When both brains reach the same conclusion, however, its psychic power increases dramatically and can affect objects from roughly half a mile away. The two-brain arrangement therefore makes the species capable of both unusual coordination problems and extraordinary bursts of mental power.

pokemon.name: Reuniclus
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Reuniclus controls its large liquid arms through psychic power, and those arms can grip with enough force to crush rock. Individuals can link their brains by shaking hands, forming a network that increases their combined psychic power. The fluid surrounding Reuniclus has a dangerous reputation: folklore says drinking it grants wisdom, but the liquid is actually highly toxic. The species is regarded as remarkably intelligent despite its unusual gelatinous anatomy.

playthrough: Ducklett evolves into Swanna at level 35, producing a Water/Flying Pokemon with base 98 Speed and equal base 87 Attack and Special Attack. Surf or Scald and Air Slash or Hurricane provide strong special STAB, while Fly or Brave Bird, Ice Beam, Roost, Rain Dance, Defog in later games, and other support options allow physical, special, or utility play. Hydration cures status at the end of each turn while rain is active, creating a particularly useful combination with Rest in generations where both are available; Keen Eye prevents accuracy reduction, while Big Pecks prevents Defense drops. Water/Flying grants a Ground immunity and useful resistances to Fire, Water, Fighting, Bug, and Steel, but Electric attacks deal quadruple damage and Rock attacks are also super effective. Timid is the most straightforward nature for special sets because base 98 Speed is one of Swanna's best traits. Its 75/63/63 bulk is mediocre, so it performs best when using Speed and good offensive typing rather than attempting to tank repeated hits.
competitive: Swanna was a meaningful BW rain attacker despite never becoming an upper-tier staple. In BW NU it used base 98 Speed, Surf, and Hurricane to become a dangerous rain sweeper because Hurricane becomes perfectly accurate in rain while Surf simultaneously receives a power boost; Hydration plus Rest could also restore Swanna completely without leaving it asleep once the turn ended. Smogon classified Swanna in PUBL while noting that its combination of Water and Flying STAB was difficult for many teams to resist cleanly. Later generations gave it additional utility through Defog, and by SM ZU it was considered one of the tier's better offensive Flying-types and one of its strongest offensive hazard removers. Its limitations have remained consistent: mediocre 87 attacking stats, poor defenses, a Stealth Rock weakness, and a quadruple Electric weakness mean Swanna needs favorable positioning and usually cannot afford many mistakes.
nuzlocke: Swanna is a useful Nuzlocke Pokemon because its Ground immunity, good base 98 Speed, and Water/Flying coverage create several safe and favorable matchups. Roost provides reliable recovery where available, while Hydration can eliminate status under rain and can make Rest much safer in generations that support the combination. Electric attacks are the overwhelming danger because they deal quadruple damage, and Swanna's 63 Special Defense gives it little chance to survive a strong unexpected Thunderbolt or similar move. Rock attacks are also super effective, while Brave Bird recoil and Hurricane's poor accuracy outside rain introduce avoidable risk. Timid Swanna with reliable Surf or Scald and Air Slash is generally safer than a high-variance mixed or recoil-heavy approach.

pokemon.name: Ducklett
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Ducklett lives around ponds and rivers and is much better at swimming and diving than at flying. Young individuals watch Swanna carefully and imitate their movements while learning to fly. Ducklett can spray water from its feathers to distract predators and escape. Repeated deep diving strengthens its body and helps it search for its preferred foods, including peat and bog moss.

pokemon.name: Swanna
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Swanna can fly for thousands of miles without resting and commonly takes flight around sunrise. At dusk, flocks gather to perform coordinated dances, with the flock's leader positioned at the center. Despite its graceful appearance, its flexible neck and strong bill allow extremely accurate and forceful thrusting attacks. Artists are said to have drawn inspiration from Swanna's elegant dawn and evening dances.

playthrough: Vanillite evolves into Vanillish at level 35 and Vanilluxe at level 47, making this one of Unova's later-evolving pure Ice families. Vanilluxe has base 110 Special Attack, 95 Special Defense, 85 Defense, and 79 Speed, giving it strong Ice offense through Ice Beam, Blizzard, Freeze-Dry in later generations, Flash Cannon, Mirror Coat, and other limited coverage. Ice Body restores HP gradually in hail, Weak Armor can trade Defense for Speed after a physical hit, and from Generation VII onward Vanilluxe gained Snow Warning as a standard ability, automatically summoning hail in Generations VII and VIII or snow in Generation IX. Snow Warning dramatically improves Blizzard by making it perfectly accurate in hail or snow-supporting rulesets, while Generation IX snow also raises the Defense of Ice-types by 50 percent. Pure Ice has only an Ice resistance and weaknesses to Fire, Fighting, Rock, and Steel, so Vanilluxe is much safer as an attacker than as a general switch-in. Modest maximizes special damage, while Timid can improve important Speed matchups.
competitive: Vanilluxe had a modest BW competitive résumé at first, appearing primarily in ZU and lower-tier play as a special Ice attacker with base 110 Special Attack, Ice Beam or Blizzard, and limited coverage. Its competitive identity changed substantially in Generation VII when it gained Snow Warning. Automatic hail made Blizzard perfectly accurate and allowed Vanilluxe to function as a far more dangerous wallbreaker, reaching NUBL in SM and becoming a genuine RU threat. In Sword and Shield, Choice Specs Snow Warning Vanilluxe could overwhelm even many Ice-resistant switch-ins with repeated perfectly accurate Blizzards, and Smogon described it as a unique UU wallbreaker despite its narrow movepool. The species remains held back by pure Ice typing, Stealth Rock vulnerability, base 79 Speed, and limited coverage, but the addition of Snow Warning transformed it from an ordinary low-tier Ice attacker into a specialized weather wallbreaker with a clear competitive identity.
nuzlocke: The Vanillite line provides excellent Ice damage but requires careful matchup control in a Nuzlocke because pure Ice typing offers very little defensive protection. Fire, Fighting, Rock, and Steel attacks are all super effective, and the family evolves relatively late at levels 35 and 47, so Vanillish may need to carry the role for a substantial portion of the game. Ice Beam is extremely safe and reliable, while Blizzard becomes much more attractive when Vanilluxe has Snow Warning because the weather removes its normal accuracy problem. Weak Armor is risky under permadeath rules because taking a physical hit lowers Defense even while increasing Speed, whereas Snow Warning can improve both offense and, in Generation IX snow, physical durability. Modest Vanilluxe is excellent when it can attack from a favorable matchup, but it should not be used as a blind defensive pivot.

pokemon.name: Vanillite
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Vanillite is said to be born from icicles struck by morning sunlight that do not want to melt. The white 'ice cream' swirl covering its head is actually snow, and if enough heat or touching melts that layer away, Vanillite becomes embarrassed by the exposed icy head underneath. It can exhale air as cold as −58 degrees Fahrenheit, creating ice crystals and snowfall nearby. Vanillite sleeps buried beneath snow and gains energy from morning sunlight; Glalie is one of its natural predators.

pokemon.name: Vanillish
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Vanillish lives in snowy southern mountains and is believed to have migrated there during an ancient ice age. It drinks water and freezes that water inside its body, then exhales air as cold as −148 degrees Fahrenheit to hide itself or freeze opponents. Despite possessing enough force to shatter frozen targets with headbutts, Vanillish is described as kind-natured and normally spares creatures that it freezes. Hot climates can shrink its icy body, and refreezing after partial melting may leave its shape distorted.

pokemon.name: Vanilluxe
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Vanilluxe forms when two Vanillish become stuck together after melting in daylight and freezing together again overnight. It drinks large quantities of water and uses that water to create internal snow clouds. When both heads become angry or act in agreement, they can release powerful blizzards simultaneously from both mouths. Vanilluxe can survive normally even if one head is lost, and its ability to create snow almost anywhere makes it popular around skiing and snowboarding areas.

playthrough: Deerling evolves into Sawsbuck at level 34, producing a Normal/Grass physical attacker with base 100 Attack, 95 Speed, and balanced 80/70/70 bulk. Horn Leech is the family's defining Grass STAB because it restores half the damage dealt, while Return in older games, Double-Edge, Body Slam, Jump Kick in generations where available, Wild Charge, Megahorn, and Swords Dance provide Normal STAB, coverage, or setup. Chlorophyll doubles Speed in harsh sunlight, Sap Sipper grants complete Grass immunity while raising Attack by one stage when hit by a Grass move, and the Hidden Ability Serene Grace doubles the chance of secondary effects. The four seasonal forms are mechanically identical: in Generation V their appearance changes with the in-game season, while in Generation IX Paldea their form instead changes according to the area where the game is loaded. Normal/Grass gives a Ghost immunity and useful Water, Electric, Grass, and Ground resistances but creates six weaknesses to Fire, Ice, Fighting, Flying, Poison, and Bug. Jolly helps preserve Sawsbuck's useful base 95 Speed, while Adamant makes Horn Leech and Normal STAB noticeably stronger.
competitive: Sawsbuck was a respectable BW NU attacker whose main strengths were base 100 Attack, base 95 Speed, Horn Leech, and two very useful ordinary abilities. Chlorophyll made it a dangerous sun sweeper by doubling Speed, while Sap Sipper created a Grass immunity and an Attack boost that could punish moves such as Sleep Powder, Giga Drain, or Leech Seed. Swords Dance, Horn Leech, Return or Double-Edge, and coverage gave it real sweeping potential, and Horn Leech's recovery helped offset recoil or chip damage. It also had a VGC 2011 niche on teams that could combine sun, Tailwind, or Sap Sipper support. Sawsbuck's long-term problem is defensive typing: six weaknesses and only average bulk make it difficult to switch in repeatedly, while newer generations introduced many stronger Grass and Normal attackers. Its seasonal forms are cosmetic and do not create separate competitive roles.
nuzlocke: Sawsbuck can be quite effective in Nuzlockes because Horn Leech combines accurate Grass damage with substantial healing, letting it recover HP while attacking instead of spending separate turns on recovery. Sap Sipper is especially safe because it provides a full Grass immunity and can convert a predicted Grass move into an Attack boost, while Chlorophyll can make Sawsbuck extremely fast in sun. Its main weakness is the sheer number of type vulnerabilities: Fire, Ice, Fighting, Flying, Poison, and Bug moves all hit super effectively, so matchup knowledge matters more than its decent 80/70/70 bulk. Double-Edge recoil is often unnecessary under permadeath rules when Body Slam or another reliable Normal move is sufficient. Jolly can be safer than Adamant when moving first prevents an otherwise dangerous hit.

pokemon.name: Deerling
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Deerling's fur changes color and scent with the seasons, helping it blend into the surrounding grass and vegetation. Spring individuals have a delicate sweet scent, summer Deerling smell more strongly of grass, autumn Deerling have a softer sweet scent, and winter Deerling have essentially no scent. When they sense hostility, they hide in vegetation rather than immediately fighting. Deerling usually remain close to Sawsbuck but are curious enough to wander away and sometimes become lost.

pokemon.name: Sawsbuck
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Sawsbuck's antlers and coat change dramatically with the seasons, growing pink flowers in spring, green leaves in summer, red-brown foliage in autumn, and white winter growth in cold conditions. Herds are led by the Sawsbuck with the most impressive antlers. The species migrates with seasonal changes and has historically been called a harbinger of spring. Seasonal behavior also differs: autumn males are notably short-tempered and fight one another frequently, while winter Sawsbuck are considered calmer and easier to tame.

playthrough: Emolga is a single-stage Electric/Flying Pokemon built around Speed and utility, with base 103 Speed but only base 75 in both attacking stats and 55/60/60 bulk. Volt Switch and Acrobatics or Air Slash provide dual STAB and momentum, while U-turn, Encore, Taunt, Thunder Wave, Roost in applicable games, Knock Off, and other support moves let Emolga contribute without relying on raw damage. Static has a 30 percent chance to paralyze an opponent that makes contact, while the Hidden Ability Motor Drive grants complete Electric immunity and raises Speed by one stage when hit by an Electric move. Electric/Flying also provides a Ground immunity and useful resistances to Fighting, Flying, Bug, Grass, and Steel, while only Ice and Rock are super effective. Jolly or Timid are the natural choices because base 103 Speed is clearly Emolga's strongest stat. It is most effective as a fast pivot or support Pokemon rather than a conventional sweeper.
competitive: Emolga was much stronger in BW ZU than its later reputation suggests. Smogon describes it as a premier offensive pivot there because base 103 Speed, Acrobatics, U-turn or Volt Switch, Taunt, Encore, and Knock Off allow it to maintain momentum and disrupt slower teams. Motor Drive provides a second immunity on top of Flying's Ground immunity and can punish opposing Volt Switch attempts by raising Emolga's Speed. Its 75 attacking stats limit direct wallbreaking, but Flying Gem Acrobatics gave BW sets enough immediate power to threaten neutral targets while pivoting around defensive answers. Later power creep was much less kind: in SM and SS, Smogon regarded Emolga as badly outclassed because its low offenses and frail defenses no longer compensated for the Speed and utility. Its competitive history is therefore generation-dependent—an excellent BW ZU facilitator, but a far more marginal option in later formats.
nuzlocke: Emolga has useful Nuzlocke traits despite its poor bulk. Ground immunity is always valuable, and Motor Drive can add a complete Electric immunity while increasing Speed, creating several opportunities for completely free switches when the opponent's move is known. Base 103 Speed lets Emolga use Encore, Taunt, Thunder Wave, Volt Switch, or U-turn before many opponents can respond, making it effective at controlling rather than tanking fights. Ice and Rock moves are the primary type weaknesses, but even strong neutral attacks can be dangerous because 55 HP and 60 in both defenses leave little margin for critical hits. Jolly or Timid Emolga is safest as a fast utility pivot brought in through immunities or after a knockout rather than as a Pokemon expected to absorb repeated damage.

pokemon.name: Emolga
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Emolga lives in treetops and glides between them using the cape-like membranes stretching between its limbs. It generates electricity in cheek pouches, stores that charge in the gliding membranes, and releases electricity while airborne to frighten bird Pokemon and secure access to food. Emolga eats both Berries and Bug-type Pokemon and often cooks its food with small electric shocks before eating it. Its habit of stuffing its cheeks with food can occasionally make the body too heavy for comfortable gliding.

playthrough: Karrablast evolves into Escavalier only when traded specifically for a Shelmet, which evolves into Accelgor at the same time. This makes Escavalier powerful but potentially inconvenient in a normal playthrough because the evolution depends on access to trading and the correct partner species. Once evolved, Escavalier is a Bug/Steel physical tank with base 135 Attack, 105 Defense, 105 Special Defense, and only base 20 Speed. Megahorn and Iron Head provide extremely strong physical STAB, while Drill Run, Knock Off in later generations, Razor Shell, Swords Dance, and other coverage or utility give it enough flexibility to break bulky targets. Shell Armor prevents critical hits, Swarm strengthens Bug attacks at low HP, and Overcoat protects from weather damage and, from Generation VI onward, powder and spore moves. Bug/Steel gives Escavalier a huge resistance list and only one conventional weakness, but Fire deals quadruple damage, so even mediocre Fire coverage must be treated as a major threat. Adamant maximizes damage, while Brave is especially natural on Trick Room teams because Escavalier is so slow that lowering Speed is usually beneficial rather than harmful.
competitive: Escavalier was one of the defining tanks of BW RU. Its Bug/Steel typing, 70/105/105 bulk, enormous base 135 Attack, and access to Megahorn made it extraordinarily difficult to switch into while also letting it absorb a wide range of resisted attacks. Smogon specifically describes Escavalier as one of the best Pokemon in BW RU, where Choice Band Megahorn, Iron Head, Pursuit, and coverage allowed it to trap Psychic- and Ghost-types and force so much respect that Fire coverage became more common partly because of Escavalier's presence. Its base 20 Speed also gives it a strong Trick Room niche in singles and doubles, turning a severe normal disadvantage into an advantage under reversed turn order. The quadruple Fire weakness and total dependence on taking hits before moving are the major limitations, and stronger generations have gradually pushed it lower, but its combination of huge Attack, excellent mixed bulk, and unusually efficient defensive typing has given it a genuine long-term lower-tier identity rather than a one-generation gimmick.
nuzlocke: Escavalier is exceptionally safe against many physical and special opponents because Bug/Steel supplies numerous resistances and Shell Armor can eliminate critical hits entirely. Its 105 Defense and 105 Special Defense are excellent, but base 20 Speed means it almost always has to absorb an attack before retaliating, making matchup knowledge essential. Fire is the overwhelming danger because it deals quadruple damage, and even weak or unexpected Fire coverage can bypass Escavalier's otherwise impressive defenses. Overcoat becomes especially useful from Generation VI onward because it prevents powder and spore effects in addition to weather damage, giving the family another layer of reliability. The biggest practical obstacle is the evolution itself: if trading for a Shelmet is impossible under the run's rules, Karrablast cannot reach Escavalier and the line loses most of its value.

pokemon.name: Karrablast
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Karrablast lives in forests and fields and often hides in trees or tall grass when threatened. When danger becomes unavoidable, it sprays an acidic liquid from its mouth. Shelmet is both its preferred prey and its evolutionary counterpart: Karrablast can melt through Shelmet's shell and eat the creature inside, while the unusual exchange of energy that occurs when the two species are traded causes both to evolve.

pokemon.name: Escavalier
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Escavalier wears the shell taken from Shelmet as full-body armor, while its forelimbs end in long lance-like weapons used for jousting attacks. Despite carrying heavy steel armor, it is capable of flying at high speed and striking opponents directly with those lances. Escavalier is described as exceptionally brave and continues facing opponents even when badly outmatched. In Galar it became culturally prominent enough that a famous painting depicts an Escavalier dueling a Sirfetch'd.

playthrough: Foongus evolves into Amoonguss at level 39, producing one of the slowest but most durable Grass/Poison support Pokemon in the series. Amoonguss has base 114 HP, 70 Defense, 80 Special Defense, and only base 30 Speed, with modest base 85 offenses that are secondary to its utility. Spore is its signature practical strength because it is normally 100 percent accurate, while Giga Drain, Sludge Bomb, Clear Smog, Synthesis, Pollen Puff in later games, and Rage Powder in doubles provide healing, offense, stat-resetting, and redirection. Effect Spore can inflict poison, paralysis, or sleep on opponents that make contact, while the Hidden Ability Regenerator restores one-third of Amoonguss's maximum HP whenever it switches out. Grass/Poison resists Water, Electric, Fighting, Fairy from Generation VI onward, and Grass especially well, but is weak to Fire, Ice, Flying, and Psychic. In Generation VI onward, Grass-types, Overcoat users, and Safety Goggles users are immune to Spore and other powder moves, so Spore is not universally reliable even though its listed accuracy is perfect. Calm, Bold, or Sassy are strong defensive natures, and minimum Speed can be useful on Trick Room teams.
competitive: Amoonguss has one of the most enduring support careers of any Generation V Pokemon. In BW it was officially an RU Pokemon but had a genuine OU niche because Regenerator, 114 HP, defensive Grass/Poison typing, and sleep support let it pivot repeatedly into threats such as Keldeo, Breloom, Politoed, Rotom-W, and Thundurus-T. Its doubles and VGC résumé is even stronger: Spore creates reliable sleep pressure, Rage Powder redirects attacks away from teammates, Clear Smog removes setup boosts, Pollen Puff can heal an ally, and Regenerator restores health whenever Amoonguss rotates out. Its base 30 Speed is often an asset under Trick Room because it can move before faster opponents once turn order is reversed. Amoonguss remains a relevant modern VGC support Pokemon in Regulation-era Scarlet and Violet despite low singles usage, which is a good example of how tier labels alone can understate a Pokemon's actual competitive importance. Its main limitations are passivity, common Fire- and Psychic-type threats, and the increasing number of mechanics that block powder moves.
nuzlocke: Amoonguss is extremely useful in Nuzlockes because its huge HP, good defensive typing, and Regenerator can let it recover large amounts of health simply by switching. Spore is one of the safest control moves available when the target is susceptible because it does not require damage or recoil and normally cannot miss, but from Generation VI onward Grass-types and several anti-powder effects are immune, so target knowledge matters. Giga Drain adds healing while attacking, while Clear Smog can erase dangerous setup boosts without relying on a stat move of its own. Effect Spore can occasionally inflict a helpful status condition but is random and should not be relied upon for survival. Fire, Ice, Flying, and Psychic attacks remain dangerous, and Amoonguss is so slow that it will usually take a hit before acting outside Trick Room.

pokemon.name: Foongus
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Foongus is a small mushroom Pokemon whose cap closely resembles a Poké Ball. It uses that pattern to lure curious people and Pokemon close enough to release poisonous spores, although the disguise is not always convincing. Properly dried Foongus spores can be processed into stomach medicine. The species prefers damp habitats around trees and can move by hopping or even rolling on its cap.

pokemon.name: Amoonguss
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Amoonguss is a carnivorous mushroom Pokemon that uses the Poké Ball-like patterns on its head and arms to lure prey, though Pokédex material notes that the tactic often works poorly. It releases clouds of poisonous spores, and mushrooms can grow wherever those spores land if they are not washed away quickly. Amoonguss prefers damp areas and often remains nearly motionless in tall grass with only its cap visible. It is particularly attracted to places where Poké Balls have been dropped.

playthrough: Frillish evolves into Jellicent at level 40, producing a Water/Ghost Pokemon with base 100 HP, 105 Special Defense, and 85 Special Attack. Surf or Scald, Shadow Ball or Hex, Recover, Will-O-Wisp, Taunt, Trick Room, and later Strength Sap in some formats give Jellicent both excellent defensive utility and enough offense to avoid being completely passive. Water Absorb grants a full Water immunity and restores one-quarter of maximum HP when hit by a Water move, Cursed Body has a chance to disable a move that strikes Jellicent, and Damp prevents Explosion and Self-Destruct effects while Jellicent is active. Water/Ghost also gives natural Normal and Fighting immunities plus useful resistances to Fire, Water, Ice, Bug, Poison, and Steel. Dark, Ghost, Electric, and Grass are the main weaknesses, while base 60 Speed is low enough to support Trick Room without being completely unusable outside it. Bold or Calm are excellent defensive natures, while Quiet can support a slower offensive Trick Room set.
competitive: Jellicent was a genuine BW OU staple and one of the generation's premier spinblockers. Water/Ghost typing, 100 HP, 105 Special Defense, Water Absorb, Recover, Taunt, Will-O-Wisp, and Scald let it simultaneously check rain teams, block Rapid Spin from several important hazard removers, and disrupt defensive cores. Smogon describes it as one of BW OU's best answers to rain offense and one of the only consistently good Ghost-type spinblockers in the tier. Its Normal and Fighting immunities also made it especially useful against common Fighting-types, while Taunt plus recovery prevented many slower walls from simply healing or setting hazards in front of it. Jellicent later lost some of its unique importance as Defog became more central to hazard removal, but it retained useful lower-tier and doubles niches through Water immunity, recovery, burns, and Trick Room. Its major weaknesses are status, Electric and Grass coverage, and only moderate physical Defense before burn support.
nuzlocke: Jellicent is exceptionally safe in planned Nuzlocke matchups because it naturally ignores Normal and Fighting attacks, and Water Absorb can add a third complete immunity while healing it. Recover gives reliable long-term sustain, while Will-O-Wisp can sharply reduce the threat of physical attackers if it lands. Cursed Body can unexpectedly disable a dangerous move, but the effect is random and should be treated as a bonus rather than part of the core plan. Dark, Ghost, Electric, and Grass attacks are the major threats, and Jellicent's physical Defense is only base 70, so strong physical super-effective moves remain dangerous despite the high HP. Bold or Calm Jellicent is best used as an immunity pivot and controlled wall rather than a Pokemon expected to absorb every neutral attack indefinitely.

pokemon.name: Frillish
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Frillish lives in extremely deep ocean water, with dens roughly five miles below the surface where pressure and darkness are intense. It drifts quietly until prey approaches, then wraps the victim in veil-like limbs lined with tens of thousands of nearly invisible poisonous stingers. The poison numbs or paralyzes the prey, allowing Frillish to drag it down toward its deep-sea den. The species shows obvious sexual dimorphism: males are blue and females pink, and female Frillish are described as having slightly longer poisonous stingers.

pokemon.name: Jellicent
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Jellicent is composed largely of seawater and propels itself by absorbing water and forcefully expelling it from the top of its body. Schools of Jellicent gather to hunt during the full moon, and they are feared by sailors because legends claim ships entering their territory disappear and become part of their underwater lairs. Jellicent feeds on life energy, and Pokédex lore says the crown-like structure on its head grows larger as it absorbs more. Male and female Jellicent have dramatically different blue and pink appearances, but their underlying behavior and abilities are the same.

playthrough: Alomomola is a single-stage pure Water Pokemon with an enormous base 165 HP stat, base 80 Defense, and only base 40 Special Attack and 45 Special Defense. Its role is therefore almost entirely defensive and supportive: Wish, Protect, Scald in generations where available, Aqua Jet, Knock Off, Flip Turn in modern games, Helping Hand, and other support moves let it heal teammates, spread burns, scout, and pivot. Regenerator is by far its strongest single-battle ability because switching out restores one-third of maximum HP, while Hydration cures status each turn in rain and Healer can cure an ally's status in doubles. Wish is particularly powerful because the amount healed is based on Alomomola's enormous HP, allowing it to restore large portions of a teammate's health. Pure Water leaves only Electric and Grass weaknesses and resists Fire, Water, Ice, and Steel, but the extremely low Special Defense means even neutral special attacks can be much more dangerous than its HP bar suggests. Bold or Impish are natural for physical walling, while a specially defensive nature can partially compensate for its weak Special Defense.
competitive: Alomomola has had one of the most dramatic long-term rises of any relatively unchanged Generation V Pokemon. In BW it was an NU defensive pivot already valued for its enormous base 165 HP, Wish, and Regenerator, making it one of the best Wish passers in the game and an effective answer to many physical attackers. By SM it had become a major UU wall, where Regenerator let it repeatedly pivot into physical threats, pass enormous Wishes, spread burns with Scald, and use Protect or Knock Off to support stall and balance teams. In Scarlet and Violet it rose even further and is currently an OU Pokemon, with Regenerator plus Flip Turn giving it an exceptionally efficient slow-pivot role; it can absorb a hit, bring a teammate in safely, and recover one-third of its own HP in the process. Modern Assault Vest variants can even patch its historically terrible Special Defense, while Wish sets remain some of the strongest team-healing options available. Its main limitation has always been passivity: base 40 Special Attack and 75 Attack give opponents opportunities to set up unless Alomomola can burn them, remove items, or pivot into a stronger teammate.
nuzlocke: Alomomola is an outstanding Nuzlocke support Pokemon because its enormous HP creates huge Wishes for both itself and teammates, while Regenerator restores health simply by switching. Pure Water typing has only Electric and Grass weaknesses, and base 80 Defense plus 165 HP allows it to absorb many physical neutral attacks with a very large margin. The weakness is special damage: base 45 Special Defense is poor enough that powerful neutral special attacks can still take huge chunks of health despite the massive HP total. Wish also heals on the following turn rather than immediately, so protecting or switching correctly is important when Alomomola itself is already low. Bold or Impish are especially safe for physical walling, and a slow Flip Turn in later games can move a fragile teammate into battle without exposing that teammate to the incoming attack.

pokemon.name: Alomomola
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Alomomola lives in the open sea and has a special membrane or mucus covering its body that can heal wounds. When it finds an injured or weakened Pokemon floating in the water, it gently holds the victim in its fins, treats the injuries, and carries it back toward shore. Later Pokédex accounts suggest the behavior may be partly self-protective: predators attracted to an injured Pokemon could also threaten Alomomola if the victim remained nearby. Smaller Water-type Pokemon frequently gather around it, and fishermen historically brought Alomomola on long voyages because its healing ability could reduce the need for doctors or medicine.

playthrough: Joltik evolves into Galvantula at level 36, producing a fast Bug/Electric special attacker with base 108 Speed and 97 Special Attack. Thunder and Bug Buzz form powerful dual STAB, while Volt Switch, Energy Ball or Giga Drain, Electro Ball, Thunder Wave, and from Generation VI onward Sticky Web provide offense and team support. Compound Eyes multiplies move accuracy by 1.3, raising Thunder from 70 percent to roughly 91 percent accuracy and making Galvantula's strongest Electric attack far more reliable outside rain. Unnerve prevents opponents from consuming Berries, while the Hidden Ability Swarm strengthens Bug attacks at low HP. Bug/Electric has only Fire and Rock weaknesses while resisting Electric, Fighting, Grass, and Steel, but 70/60/60 bulk is poor enough that even resisted strong attacks can hurt badly. Timid is usually ideal because Speed is the line's best defensive tool, and Sticky Web can make slower teammates dramatically more effective by lowering the Speed of grounded opponents when they switch in.
competitive: Galvantula began BW as a legitimate RU special attacker. Base 108 Speed, base 97 Special Attack, Bug/Electric STAB, Volt Switch, and Compound Eyes gave it a distinctive niche, with Compound Eyes raising Thunder to about 91 percent accuracy and turning an otherwise unreliable 120-base-power Generation V attack into a practical primary STAB. Its competitive identity changed further in Generation VI when it gained Sticky Web. Galvantula became one of the most recognizable offensive Sticky Web leads because it could establish teamwide Speed control while still threatening opponents with Thunder, Bug Buzz, Energy Ball, and Volt Switch instead of becoming passive after setting the hazard. It remained a useful Sticky Web specialist through later lower tiers, including SM, while modern SV lists it in PU and still supports offensive sets. Its frailty and Stealth Rock weakness make repeated entries difficult, but few hazard setters combine comparable Speed, immediate offensive pressure, and an unusually accurate Thunder.
nuzlocke: Galvantula can be very useful in Nuzlockes because base 108 Speed helps it avoid attacks, and Sticky Web can make an entire team safer by slowing grounded opponents that enter later. Compound Eyes makes Thunder much more reliable than normal, but roughly 91 percent accuracy is still not perfect; Thunderbolt is safer whenever the extra power is unnecessary. Bug/Electric has only Fire and Rock weaknesses, yet Galvantula's 60 Defense and 60 Special Defense mean strong neutral moves can still be dangerous despite the favorable weakness count. Volt Switch is excellent for dealing damage while escaping bad matchups, and Energy Ball can punish Ground-types that are immune to Electric STAB. Timid Galvantula is best used as a fast attacker and momentum generator rather than a Pokemon expected to take repeated hits.

pokemon.name: Joltik
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Joltik is one of the smallest known Pokemon and is too small to generate enough electricity entirely on its own. It compensates by clinging to larger Pokemon and feeding on the static electricity stored in their bodies. Joltik can produce silk from its mouth and use that silk to hang from branches or other surfaces. Its tiny size and dependence on borrowed electricity define much of its ecology.

pokemon.name: Galvantula
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Galvantula spins electrically charged silk that functions as both a hunting tool and a defensive barrier. It places electrified threads around bird Pokemon nests to capture chicks that cannot yet fly, and prey struck by its electrical attacks can remain stunned for as long as three days and nights while Galvantula feeds at its leisure. Strong pedipalps help hold struggling prey in place. Galvantula is not normally indiscriminately aggressive, but groups can attack when provoked, and animated portrayals show adults behaving protectively toward Joltik.

playthrough: Ferroseed evolves into Ferrothorn at level 40, producing one of the strongest defensive Grass/Steel Pokemon available in a normal playthrough. Ferrothorn has base 131 Defense, 116 Special Defense, and only base 20 Speed, allowing it to absorb a huge range of neutral and resisted attacks while using Power Whip, Gyro Ball, Knock Off in later games, Leech Seed, Spikes, Stealth Rock, Thunder Wave, and Protect. Iron Barbs damages opponents that make contact, which can punish physical attackers without Ferrothorn spending a turn, while the Hidden Ability Anticipation warns of certain dangerous moves but is usually less generally useful. Its extreme slowness makes Gyro Ball unusually powerful and also makes a Speed-lowering nature such as Relaxed or Sassy beneficial rather than harmful. Grass/Steel gives a long list of resistances and a Poison immunity, but Fighting is super effective and Fire deals quadruple damage, so even weak unexpected Fire coverage can be lethal. Ferrothorn lacks conventional instant recovery, making Leech Seed, Leftovers, Protect, and careful switching central to keeping it healthy over long routes.
competitive: Ferrothorn is one of the defining support Pokemon of BW OU. Its 74/131/116 bulk and Grass/Steel typing let it repeatedly switch into many of the generation's strongest Water-, Dragon-, Electric-, and Rock-type attacks, making it especially valuable in a weather metagame dominated by rain and powerful Dragons. Spikes, Stealth Rock, Leech Seed, Thunder Wave, Knock Off in later rulesets, and Iron Barbs give it enormous role compression, while Power Whip and a very strong Gyro Ball prevent it from becoming completely passive. Smogon describes Ferrothorn as one of BW OU's most effective supporters and one of its best Spikes setters, and that general identity persisted through multiple later generations of OU play. Fire and Fighting coverage remain the primary answers, while burn and the absence of reliable one-turn recovery can gradually undermine it, but few defensive Pokemon have matched Ferrothorn's combination of hazard setting, contact punishment, typing, and mixed bulk.
nuzlocke: Ferrothorn is extremely safe in many Nuzlocke matchups because its defensive stats and typing allow it to wall large portions of ordinary trainer teams. Iron Barbs punishes contact automatically, while Leech Seed can provide sustainable recovery and reduce the need to spend healing items in long fights. Gyro Ball is especially effective because Ferrothorn's very low Speed naturally maximizes the move against fast opponents, and Power Whip provides strong Grass damage without recoil. The critical exception is Fire: a quadruple weakness means an unexpected Flamethrower, Fire Punch, or similar coverage move can kill even a healthy Ferrothorn, while Fighting attacks are also dangerous. Relaxed or Sassy are excellent natures because lowering Speed improves Gyro Ball and barely affects Ferrothorn's intended role.

pokemon.name: Ferroseed
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Ferroseed prefers mossy caves, where it drives its spikes into rock walls and absorbs iron and other minerals. When threatened, it fires a barrage of spikes and uses the distraction to roll away from danger. Young Ferroseed are initially inaccurate when launching their spikes and improve through practice. In animation, nutrients absorbed from different rocks can influence the moss Ferroseed grows, showing that its mineral diet directly affects its body.

pokemon.name: Ferrothorn
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Ferrothorn hangs from cave ceilings or moves along surfaces using its three long, spiked feelers. Those appendages also absorb nutrients from rock, continuing the mineral-feeding behavior of Ferroseed. Its steel-hard spikes can be fired as projectiles and are strong enough to smash boulders or incapacitate opponents. The species is therefore both a stationary mineral feeder and a surprisingly mobile ambush defender despite its extremely low battle Speed.

playthrough: Klink evolves into Klang at level 38 and Klang evolves into Klinklang at level 49, making the family slow to mature but eventually rewarding the player with a physically sturdy pure Steel setup attacker. Klinklang has base 100 Attack, 115 Defense, 85 Special Defense, and 90 Speed, with Shift Gear as its defining setup move because one use raises Attack by one stage and Speed by two. Gear Grind is a two-hit Steel STAB move with 50 base power per hit, letting Klinklang break Substitute, Focus Sash, and Sturdy while dealing strong total damage, although its 85 percent accuracy creates meaningful risk. Wild Charge, Return in older generations, Magnet Rise, Substitute, and limited utility provide most of its additional options, and the line's narrow movepool is its greatest practical drawback. Clear Body prevents opposing stat drops and is usually the most useful ability in singles, while Plus and Minus raise Special Attack when paired with an ally using the complementary ability and are mainly relevant in doubles. Adamant is usually best for sweeping after Shift Gear, while Jolly can improve some pre-setup Speed matchups.
competitive: Klinklang was a BW RU Pokemon built almost entirely around Shift Gear and Gear Grind. Base 115 Defense and Steel typing create setup opportunities against weaker physical or resisted attacks, and after one Shift Gear its base 90 Speed becomes extremely difficult for unboosted opponents to match while base 100 Attack rises to threatening levels. Gear Grind is particularly useful competitively because the two hits break Substitute and Focus Sash, but Klinklang's tiny coverage pool leaves it vulnerable to bulky Steel-, Water-, Ground-, and Fire-types depending on the exact generation. Magnet Rise can temporarily remove its Ground weakness and create setup opportunities against some Ground-types, while Wild Charge and Return historically supplied the limited neutral coverage available. Klinklang remained a legitimate NU threat in later generations, including SM, but its viability has consistently depended on whether its few checks have been weakened enough for a late-game Shift Gear sweep.
nuzlocke: Klinklang's pure Steel typing and base 115 Defense make it a useful Nuzlocke Pokemon once the line finally reaches its last evolution at level 49. Shift Gear can turn a slow or middling matchup into a clean sweep, but using a setup turn is only safe when the opponent cannot threaten with Fire, Fighting, or Ground coverage. Gear Grind's ability to break Sturdy and Focus Sash is valuable, yet 85 percent accuracy is a real permadeath concern; a more accurate move is preferable when one is available and already sufficient. Clear Body adds reliability by preventing enemy Intimidate, Sticky Web, or other stat-lowering effects from ruining a setup plan. The biggest story drawback is simply timing: Klink and Klang are much less impressive than the final form, so the family can feel underpowered for a long portion of the game.

pokemon.name: Klink
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Klink consists of two living gears permanently interlocked as a pair. Once two gear bodies join, they cannot freely substitute different partners without separating, and their rotation generates the energy that sustains them. Klink usually inhabits caves, with the earliest recorded modern sightings associated with Chargestone Cave. There is an apparent historical contradiction around the species: some researchers believe it appeared suddenly only about a century ago, while other traditions claim ancient humans based the invention of mechanical gears on Klink.

pokemon.name: Klang
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Klang adds a larger gear and can communicate its emotions to other Klang by changing the direction and speed of its rotation; anger causes the gears to spin faster. It can launch its smaller gear at high speed as an attack. That minigear is biologically essential, and Pokédex records state that Klang will die if the launched gear fails to return. In Galar, Klang is used so often as an industrial symbol that many companies incorporate its image into their logos.

pokemon.name: Klinklang
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Klinklang adds a red-cored spiked gear that stores enormous amounts of energy generated by the rotating mechanism. It can discharge that stored energy as powerful electricity or launch components at opponents. Evidence from the Mystery Dungeon series suggests that the two faced gears remain independently sentient, while the additional spiked gear is not itself alive. Rapid rotation of the red core allows Klinklang to charge and release much greater energy than its earlier stages.

playthrough: Tynamo evolves into Eelektrik at level 39, and Eelektrik evolves into Eelektross with a Thunder Stone. Standard Eelektross is a pure Electric mixed attacker with base 115 Attack, 105 Special Attack, 85 HP, and only base 50 Speed, but Levitate normally removes Electric's only weakness by granting complete immunity to Ground attacks. Thunderbolt or Discharge, Volt Switch, Wild Charge, Flamethrower, Giga Drain, Drain Punch, Knock Off, Crunch, Coil, and many other physical and special moves make Eelektross one of the most flexible coverage attackers in Unova. Its lack of ordinary type weaknesses is excellent, but Mold Breaker, Gravity, Smack Down, an Iron Ball, or similar effects can expose the Ground weakness that Levitate normally removes. Modest or Quiet suit special and mixed pivot sets, while Adamant can emphasize physical offense and Coil. Mega Eelektross keeps pure Electric typing but rises to base 145 Attack, 135 Special Attack, 90 Special Defense, and 80 Speed; in current ability-enabled data it gains Eelevate, which preserves Ground immunity and raises its highest stat by one stage whenever it scores a knockout.
competitive: Standard Eelektross was a strong BW NU wallbreaker and pivot because Levitate effectively removed its only type weakness, while base 115 Attack, 105 Special Attack, and an unusually broad movepool made safe defensive answers difficult to identify. Volt Switch created slow momentum, and coverage such as Giga Drain, Flamethrower, Knock Off, Drain Punch, and various physical attacks meant conventional Ground-type answers to Electric Pokemon could be punished heavily. That same formula remained successful in later generations; SM Smogon described Eelektross as one of PU's best pivots because almost every matchup allowed it to make progress through damage, item removal, or Volt Switch. Mega Eelektross is much newer and should be separated from that established history. Current data gives the Mega 145 Attack, 135 Special Attack, 80 Speed, and Eelevate, preserving the Ground immunity while adding a snowballing highest-stat boost after each knockout; this creates a far more threatening cleaner, but it does not yet have the long historical tier résumé of standard Eelektross.
nuzlocke: The Eelektross line becomes extremely safe once it reaches Eelektrik because Levitate normally leaves the pure Electric typing with no weaknesses at all. That does not make the family invulnerable—its defenses are only moderate, Tynamo is frail, and Mold Breaker or effects that suppress Levitate can suddenly make Ground attacks super effective—but ordinary matchup planning is unusually forgiving. Volt Switch lets Eelektross deal damage while escaping unfavorable situations, Giga Drain and Drain Punch can restore health, and its broad mixed coverage means the player rarely needs to rely on inaccurate attacks. Mega Eelektross improves Speed and both offenses substantially while keeping a Ground immunity through Eelevate, making successful knockouts progressively more dangerous for the opponent. Quiet or Modest standard Eelektross is excellent for slow pivoting, while Mega Eelektross can justify more Speed-oriented natures because base 80 is much more workable.

pokemon.name: Tynamo
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Tynamo is a tiny eel-like Pokemon whose individual electrical output is weak, so members of the species gather into groups and link their power together. A sufficiently large school can produce electricity comparable to a lightning strike. Tynamo live in caves and other dark environments and are often found clustered together rather than alone.

pokemon.name: Eelektrik
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Eelektrik is a vigorous carnivore with a large appetite. When it identifies prey, it immediately coils around the target and uses the electricity-generating organs along its body to paralyze the victim before eating it. It inhabits both caves and marine environments. The species is therefore much more directly predatory than the schooling Tynamo stage.

pokemon.name: Eelektross
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Eelektross lives primarily in the ocean but can crawl onto land using the fins beneath its body. It hunts terrestrial prey by latching on with its sucker-like mouth, sinking in its fangs, and delivering a powerful electric shock before dragging the victim back toward the sea. Electricity-generating organs are distributed across its torso and arms. Its ability to operate effectively in both water and on land makes it an unusually mobile ambush predator.

pokemon.name: Eelektross
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Mega Evolution greatly strengthens Eelektross's electricity-generating organs and causes them to secrete large quantities of electrified white mucus. That mucus forms two long structures on its arms resembling gelatinous Eelektrik, officially described as 'false Eelektrik,' through which Mega Eelektross discharges much of its electricity. It produces roughly ten times as much electricity as the standard form and can stun extremely large Pokemon such as Wailord. The false Eelektrik also stabilize it in water and allow it to swim nearly twice as fast, while its electrical output is strong enough to keep the entire body levitating continuously.

playthrough: Elgyem evolves into Beheeyem at level 42, producing a very slow pure Psychic special attacker with base 125 Special Attack, 95 Special Defense, and only base 40 Speed. Psychic or Psyshock, Shadow Ball, Energy Ball, Thunderbolt, Signal Beam in older games, Recover, Calm Mind, Nasty Plot in some generations, and Trick Room support several offensive and defensive approaches. Analytic is especially effective outside Trick Room because it boosts the power of Beheeyem's attacks by 30 percent when it moves last, something its low Speed naturally encourages. Synchronize reflects burn, poison, or paralysis back to the opponent that caused it, while Telepathy protects Beheeyem from damaging moves used by allies in double battles. Trick Room reverses the normal Speed disadvantage and turns Beheeyem into a strong sweeper, but Analytic and Trick Room do not always complement one another because moving first under Trick Room can remove the Analytic boost. Quiet is ideal for Trick Room, while Modest or Bold can support slower wallbreaking or Recover sets.
competitive: Beheeyem was a strong BW PU wallbreaker because base 125 Special Attack combines with Analytic to produce enormous damage whenever it moves after the opponent. Smogon describes it as one of the tier's most threatening breakers, capable of cleanly KOing many offensive Pokemon and heavily damaging even dedicated special walls. Recover, Nasty Plot or Calm Mind, Psychic, and Fighting- or Bug-type coverage in the era also let it function as a bulky setup attacker rather than only a Choice user. Its base 40 Speed creates a natural Trick Room niche in singles and doubles, while Telepathy provides useful doubles synergy with spread moves such as Earthquake. The main limitations are mediocre physical bulk, common Bug-, Dark-, and Ghost-type weaknesses, and the fact that its low Speed forces it to absorb attacks before Analytic-boosted retaliation when Trick Room is not active.
nuzlocke: Beheeyem's base 125 Special Attack can shorten fights dramatically, while Recover gives it a reliable way to restore health between exchanges. Its base 40 Speed is dangerous in ordinary play because opponents usually attack first, but a well-timed Trick Room can reverse that disadvantage and let a Quiet Beheeyem move before much faster enemies. Analytic rewards moving last with extra damage, so even outside Trick Room the low Speed is not completely wasted. Bug, Dark, and Ghost attacks are the primary threats, especially strong physical moves against its merely base 75 Defense. Synchronize can punish status and Telepathy is useful in doubles, but neither replaces careful matchup control; Beheeyem is safest when its huge Special Attack is used to end known favorable matchups quickly.

pokemon.name: Elgyem
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Elgyem is an extraterrestrial Psychic-type whose modern appearance is associated in folklore with a UFO crash site that appeared roughly 50 years before its original Pokédex records. It can exert enough psychic pressure on an opponent's brain to cause severe headaches. Strange images resembling an unknown landscape may appear on nearby television screens when Elgyem is present, and some accounts suggest those images depict its home. Despite its unsettling powers, Elgyem has also been portrayed as cooperative and willing to help during emergencies.

pokemon.name: Beheeyem
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Beheeyem communicates by flashing the red, green, and yellow digits on its hands in complex patterns that researchers have not fully decoded. It can manipulate memories directly, including erasing or rewriting them. Pokédex reports associate Beheeyem with mysterious disappearances of Dubwool from farms, and it is sometimes observed hovering over wheat fields. Animated portrayals expand its abilities further, showing Beheeyem constructing spacecraft and using powerful hypnosis to control other beings.

playthrough: Litwick evolves into Lampent at level 41, and Lampent evolves into Chandelure with a Dusk Stone. Standard Chandelure is a Ghost/Fire special attacker with enormous base 145 Special Attack, solid 90 Defense and Special Defense, and base 80 Speed. Shadow Ball and Flamethrower or Fire Blast provide devastating dual STAB, while Energy Ball, Psychic, Will-O-Wisp, Trick, Calm Mind, Pain Split, and Trick Room give it both coverage and utility. Flash Fire provides a Fire immunity and boosts Fire attacks after absorbing one, Flame Body can burn contact attackers, and from Generation VI onward the Hidden Ability Infiltrator lets Chandelure ignore Substitute and several screen effects. In Generation V the line was coded with Shadow Tag as its Hidden Ability, but that ability was never legitimately obtainable and should not be treated as part of a normal BW playthrough. Mega Chandelure remains Ghost/Fire and rises to base 175 Special Attack, 110 Defense, 110 Special Defense, and 90 Speed; current ability-enabled data gives the Mega Infiltrator. Timid is excellent for standard revenge-killing or Mega sets, while Modest maximizes one of the highest Special Attack stats available.
competitive: Chandelure had a small but legitimate BW OU niche and a much stronger BW UU presence. Base 145 Special Attack, Ghost/Fire STAB, Flash Fire, and access to Choice Scarf, Choice Specs, Trick, and coverage make it an exceptionally powerful wallbreaker and revenge killer, while Ghost typing also historically allowed it to block Rapid Spin. A crucial historical distinction is that Shadow Tag Chandelure was never legal in Generation V standard play despite being coded as its Hidden Ability; from Generation VI onward that Hidden Ability was replaced by Infiltrator. Chandelure remained a strong UU-level attacker in later generations, with Infiltrator offering the ability to ignore Substitute and screens while Flash Fire supplied an extra immunity and potential Fire boost. Mega Chandelure is much newer and should be evaluated separately: current data gives it 175 Special Attack, 110/110 defenses, 90 Speed, and Infiltrator, making it an extraordinary special wallbreaker without yet giving it a long historical tier résumé comparable to the base form.
nuzlocke: Chandelure is extremely powerful in Nuzlockes because base 145 Special Attack can end favorable matchups before the opponent has time to accumulate damage, while Ghost typing provides complete Normal and Fighting immunities. Flash Fire can add a third immunity and create a strong Fire boost, making planned switches especially rewarding. The family is not bulky enough to take repeated neutral hits comfortably because base HP is only 60, and Water, Ground, Rock, Ghost, and Dark attacks are all super effective. Flamethrower is generally safer than Fire Blast when the extra power is unnecessary, and Memento should normally be avoided under permadeath rules because it deliberately faints the user. Mega Chandelure improves both defenses to 110 and Speed to 90 while raising Special Attack to 175, giving it a much larger safety margin, but it retains the same five type weaknesses.

pokemon.name: Litwick
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Litwick's purple flame is fueled by life energy absorbed from people and Pokemon. It often pretends to guide travelers through darkness with its light while actually draining their energy and leading them toward the Ghost World. As it absorbs more energy, the flame can grow larger. Animated portrayals also show groups of Litwick interfering with electronic devices while feeding.

pokemon.name: Lampent
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Lampent can sense when a person is close to death and follows the victim until it can steal the departing spirit. It normally inhabits deep forests but also wanders quietly through cities and is infamous for lingering around hospitals. In urban areas it may pretend to be an ordinary lamp while waiting for a death. The stolen spirits are used as fuel for the flame inside its glass-like head, giving Lampent its reputation as an emissary of death.

pokemon.name: Chandelure
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Chandelure's violet flames do not primarily burn the body; Pokédex lore says they burn the victim's spirit instead. It can hypnotize opponents by rhythmically waving its flames before absorbing the spirit, and beings whose souls have been consumed are said to leave behind empty bodies. The species' association with spirit consumption and hypnotic fire makes it one of the darker Ghost-type predators in the Pokédex. Its multiple flames are controlled as extensions of the main chandelier-like body.

pokemon.name: Chandelure
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Mega Chandelure develops a more elaborate chandelier body and a transformed eye that is described as a window connecting the living world with the afterlife. It draws in hatred from around itself and converts that emotion into power. Mega Evolution amplifies both its spiritual nature and its ability to manipulate the boundary between life and death rather than merely increasing the intensity of its ordinary flames.

playthrough: Axew evolves into Fraxure at level 38 and Haxorus at level 48, so the family matures late but rewards the player with one of the strongest physical attackers in Unova.
