Haxorus has an enormous base 147 Attack and useful base 97 Speed, with Dragon Dance, Swords Dance, Dragon Claw or Outrage, Earthquake, Poison Jab, Brick Break or later Close Combat, and other coverage giving it several ways to sweep. Mold Breaker is usually the best general ability because it lets Haxorus ignore defensive abilities such as Levitate or Unaware when attacking, while Rivalry changes damage according to the target's gender and is much less reliable; the Hidden Ability Unnerve prevents opposing Berries from activating. Pure Dragon gives useful Fire, Water, Grass, and Electric resistances, but Ice and Dragon attacks are dangerous in every generation and Fairy joins those weaknesses from Generation VI onward. Jolly is often the safest nature because base 97 Speed sits just below many important fast threats, while Adamant makes the already exceptional Attack even more overwhelming. Outrage is extremely powerful but locks Haxorus in for multiple turns and causes confusion afterward in older mechanics, so Dragon Claw is often the safer story option.
competitive: Haxorus was an OU Pokemon in BW, but its position there was more nuanced than its base 147 Attack might suggest. It carved out a real niche on Dragon-heavy offensive teams, especially DragMag structures where Magnezone could remove Steel-types such as Skarmory and create openings for Dragon Dance or Swords Dance Haxorus. Mold Breaker is a major part of that identity because Earthquake can ignore abilities such as Levitate, and its combination of Dragon STAB, Fighting coverage, and setup gives defensive teams very little room once checks are weakened. At the same time, Smogon notes that Haxorus competes with faster or more defensively useful Dragons such as Garchomp, Dragonite, Salamence, and Kyurem-B, while base 97 Speed leaves it vulnerable to common revenge killers before or even after setup. Later generations preserved its role as a high-end physical breaker rather than a universal top-tier staple; current SV tiering places it in RUBL with viable UU and Battle Stadium roles. Its competitive identity is therefore remarkably consistent: colossal physical power and excellent setup potential held in check by middling Speed, modest special bulk, and fierce competition from other Dragons.
nuzlocke: Haxorus is a powerful Nuzlocke Pokemon because base 147 Attack often ends favorable matchups immediately, reducing the number of turns in which something can go wrong. Mold Breaker is especially useful because it removes surprises from abilities that would normally block Earthquake or blunt a sweep, while Dragon Dance can create boss-fight sweeps if Haxorus has a genuinely safe setup turn. The family evolves late, however, and Axew and Fraxure are much less forgiving than the final form, so keeping them alive until level 48 can be the hardest part of using the line. Ice and Dragon coverage are dangerous throughout the line's original games, and Fairy becomes an additional weakness from Generation VI onward. Dragon Claw is usually safer than Outrage in permadeath play because it avoids move-locking and post-attack confusion, while Jolly can be safer than Adamant whenever the extra Speed prevents an incoming hit.

pokemon.name: Axew
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Axew uses its tusks to crush Berries, carve territorial marks into trees and boulders, and play with other members of its species. The tusks frequently break or fall out, but they regrow quickly and become harder and sharper each time. In ancient times, humans collected discarded Axew tusks and used them as cutting tools or cooking knives. Axew lives in ground nests and is also an agile climber despite its small size.

pokemon.name: Fraxure
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Fraxure is much more violent and territorial than Axew, and fights between individuals over territory are common. Its tusks can break boulders but no longer regenerate if damaged, so Fraxure sharpens them carefully on river rocks and uses them only when necessary. It competes with Bisharp for good sharpening stones along rivers. Fraxure also uses its tusks to divide captured prey into separate portions, eating one immediately and saving the other for later.

pokemon.name: Haxorus
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Haxorus takes enormous pride in its nearly unbreakable axe-like tusks, which remain sharp even when cutting through steel beams and can sever a metal transmission tower in a single strike. It is generally docile or kindhearted despite its intimidating appearance, but it becomes violently territorial when defending its home or when someone touches its tusks. Haxorus nests in caves and abandoned mines. It licks and eats mineral-rich dirt to obtain the materials needed to keep its tusks in excellent condition.

playthrough: Cubchoo evolves into Beartic at level 37, producing a slow but powerful pure Ice physical attacker. Beartic originally had base 110 Attack in Generations V and VI, but this increased to 130 from Generation VII onward, greatly improving its wallbreaking ability. Icicle Crash, Ice Punch, Aqua Jet, Superpower or Close Combat in later games, Earthquake, Play Rough, Swords Dance, and coverage such as Rock Slide give it several useful physical options. Snow Cloak can increase evasion in hail, Slush Rush from Generation VII onward doubles Speed in hail or snow, and the Hidden Ability Swift Swim doubles Speed in rain, giving Beartic unusual access to two different weather-based Speed boosts in later generations. Its base 50 Speed is poor without weather and pure Ice provides only an Ice resistance while leaving Fire, Fighting, Rock, and Steel weaknesses. Adamant maximizes damage, while Jolly can be worthwhile on Slush Rush or Swift Swim sets where every extra Speed point improves sweeping potential.
competitive: Beartic was a modest lower-tier attacker in BW, where base 110 Attack and very low Speed made it difficult to distinguish from stronger or faster Ice-types. Its competitive ceiling improved in Generation VII when its Attack rose to 130 and it gained access to Slush Rush in addition to the Hidden Ability Swift Swim. That unusual combination lets Beartic function as a physical sweeper under either hail or rain, using Swords Dance, Icicle Crash, Superpower, and coverage to exploit the doubled Speed. Smogon's SM analysis still places it in ZU and notes that even under weather, faster Choice Scarf users can revenge kill it, while pure Ice typing and mediocre bulk make setup opportunities difficult to find. Beartic is therefore best understood as a specialized weather abuser with genuine offensive power rather than a broadly splashable attacker. The stat buff made it much more threatening, but it did not solve its dependence on team support or its poor defensive typing.
nuzlocke: Beartic can hit extremely hard in a Nuzlocke, especially from Generation VII onward with base 130 Attack, but its pure Ice typing gives it very little defensive margin. Fire, Fighting, Rock, and Steel attacks are all super effective, and base 50 Speed means Beartic usually takes a hit before attacking unless Slush Rush or Swift Swim is active. Aqua Jet can safely finish weakened targets before they move, while Icicle Crash is powerful but its 90 percent accuracy introduces more risk than Ice Punch when the extra damage is unnecessary. Weather can make Beartic much safer by doubling Speed, but depending on weather also consumes setup or team-building resources. Adamant is excellent when speed control is already supplied, while Jolly is preferable if outspeeding a specific threat prevents a dangerous retaliation.

pokemon.name: Cubchoo
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Cubchoo constantly produces pale blue nasal mucus that it uses directly in its Ice-type attacks. The mucus can cause frostbite and may also be smeared onto something or someone Cubchoo dislikes. Its consistency is a health indicator: healthy Cubchoo produce thick, sticky mucus and stronger Ice techniques, while illness makes the mucus watery or may stop it entirely. The species lives in cold coastal regions.

pokemon.name: Beartic
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Beartic can freeze its breath at will, creating fangs and claws of ice hard enough to rival steel. It is an excellent swimmer in cold northern seas and can freeze the ocean surface into pathways, or create floating ice so it can rest when tired. Captured prey may be frozen for preservation rather than eaten immediately. Beartic has a fierce reputation that earned it the nickname 'Snow-White Demon,' but it is notably protective toward Cubchoo and will defend younger members of its species.

playthrough: Cryogonal is a single-stage pure Ice special attacker and support Pokemon with base 135 Special Defense, 105 Speed, and 95 Special Attack. Its physical durability improved substantially after Generation VI: HP rose from 70 to 80 and Defense from 30 to 50 in Generation VII, although physical attacks remain its obvious weak point. Levitate grants a complete Ground immunity, while Ice Beam, Freeze-Dry in later games, Recover, Rapid Spin, Haze, Reflect, Light Screen, and Flash Cannon allow Cryogonal to attack, heal, remove hazards, and reset stat boosts. Freeze-Dry is especially valuable where available because it hits Water-types super effectively despite being an Ice move. Pure Ice leaves weaknesses to Fire, Fighting, Rock, and Steel, and only resists Ice itself, so Cryogonal is much safer switching into special attacks or Ground moves than into physical neutral damage. Timid maximizes its useful base 105 Speed, while Calm emphasizes the enormous Special Defense.
competitive: Cryogonal was an important BW RU support Pokemon because Rapid Spin was scarce and its base 135 Special Defense, base 105 Speed, Levitate, and Recover gave it unusual longevity for a hazard remover. Levitate also means Spikes and Toxic Spikes do not affect it, although Stealth Rock still removes a quarter of its HP on entry because pure Ice is weak to Rock. Smogon describes it as the best bulky Rapid Spin user in BW RU, with Haze, Toxic, Reflect, or offensive Ice coverage allowing it to contribute beyond hazard removal. Its original base 30 Defense was a severe weakness that forced careful investment and left it highly vulnerable to Pursuit and strong physical attacks. Generation VII improved that profile by raising HP to 80 and Defense to 50, while later access to Freeze-Dry and Heavy-Duty Boots gave it even better utility in modern lower tiers. Current SV tiering places Cryogonal in ZU, but the same combination of Rapid Spin, Recover, Haze, high Speed, and excellent special bulk continues to define it.
nuzlocke: Cryogonal is very useful in Nuzlockes against special attackers because base 135 Special Defense is exceptional and Recover can restore half of its HP repeatedly. Levitate adds a Ground immunity and Rapid Spin can remove hazards that would otherwise chip the entire team, while Haze can erase dangerous setup boosts without needing to win a stat war. Its physical Defense remains mediocre even after the Generation VII buff, so strong physical priority or coverage can be much more dangerous than the large Special Defense suggests. Fire, Fighting, Rock, and Steel attacks are all super effective, and Stealth Rock itself is especially annoying because Cryogonal loses 25 percent of its HP when switching into it before spinning. Timid helps it act before many threats, while Calm provides an enormous special safety margin.

pokemon.name: Cryogonal
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Cryogonal is composed of living ice crystals and is said to form naturally inside snow clouds. A darker modern rumor claims that people and Pokemon who die on snowy mountains can be reborn as Cryogonal, but this is presented as folklore rather than established biology. When its body temperature rises too far, Cryogonal can turn into vapor and effectively disappear, returning to an icy form when the temperature falls again. It hunts with extendable chains of ice, constricting prey and flash-freezing victims at roughly −148 degrees Fahrenheit before carrying them away.

playthrough: Shelmet evolves into Accelgor only when it is traded specifically for a Karrablast, which simultaneously evolves into Escavalier. The evolution is therefore highly dependent on access to trading, but the result is one of the fastest Pokemon in the series: Accelgor has base 145 Speed and base 100 Special Attack. Bug Buzz is the primary STAB move, while Giga Drain, Focus Blast, Energy Ball, Acid Spray, Encore, Yawn, Spikes, and Recover in later games can support offense or utility. Hydration cures major status at the end of each turn in rain, Sticky Hold prevents most effects that would remove its item, and the Hidden Ability Unburden doubles Speed after Accelgor loses or consumes its held item, though base 145 Speed is already high enough that the boost is often unnecessary in ordinary play. Its 80/40/60 bulk is extremely poor, and pure Bug is weak to Fire, Flying, and Rock while also taking Stealth Rock damage. Timid is the natural nature for ensuring Accelgor maintains its defining speed advantage.
competitive: Accelgor was a significant BW RU Pokemon because base 145 Speed made it one of the fastest Pokemon in the entire generation. Smogon identifies it as both a dangerous special attacker and one of the game's most reliable fast Spikes users, with Bug Buzz, Focus Blast, Giga Drain, Encore, and other support tools allowing it to punish teams that treated it as a passive lead. Suicide-lead sets could combine Spikes with Final Gambit, while offensive sets used its speed to clean weakened teams or force switches and gain hazard turns. The drawback is extreme frailty: base 40 Defense and 60 Special Defense mean almost any serious neutral attack can KO it, and its base 100 Special Attack is good rather than overwhelming. Accelgor remained useful in later lower tiers, including SM NU, where it was still the fastest unboosted Pokemon in the tier and continued to combine Spikes with offensive pressure. Its competitive identity has therefore remained remarkably stable: extraordinary speed and utility balanced by almost nonexistent defensive presence.
nuzlocke: Accelgor's base 145 Speed is excellent for Nuzlockes because it can often act before virtually anything encountered in the story, but it is one of the least forgiving Pokemon if the opponent survives. Base 40 Defense and 60 Special Defense mean even neutral attacks can be fatal, so Accelgor should usually enter after a knockout or against a known resisted move rather than switching directly into damage. Encore, Yawn, Spikes, and later Recover can provide useful control, while Giga Drain may recover some chip damage. Final Gambit should generally be avoided entirely in permadeath play because it deliberately faints the user. The largest practical limitation is evolution access: without the specific Shelmet-for-Karrablast trade, Shelmet cannot become Accelgor under normal main-series rules.

pokemon.name: Shelmet
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Shelmet lives in damp habitats such as bogs and swamps and protects its soft body by closing the visor-like shell around itself. It can spit a sticky poisonous liquid at attackers while remaining protected. This defense is ineffective against Karrablast, which is both a natural predator and evolutionary counterpart capable of opening or removing Shelmet's shell. When Shelmet is traded specifically for Karrablast, an unusual energy exchange causes both species to evolve.

pokemon.name: Accelgor
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Accelgor becomes extraordinarily fast after losing Shelmet's heavy shell and fights with movements repeatedly compared to those of a ninja. A thin blue membrane covers most of its exposed body and prevents it from drying out, which is especially important because it continues to prefer moist habitats such as bogs and swamps. Its permanently displeased expression is attributed to unhappiness over losing its shell. Accelgor is popular enough in-universe to be featured frequently as a heroic or dramatic character in movies and comics.

playthrough: Unovan and Galarian Stunfisk share the same base 109 HP and base 32 Speed but use very different typings and stat emphasis. Unovan Stunfisk is Ground/Electric with 84 Defense, 81 Special Attack, and 99 Special Defense; Discharge, Thunderbolt, Earth Power, Stealth Rock, Yawn, Toxic or Thunder Wave in older games, and other utility make it a slow special tank. Static can paralyze contact attackers, Limber prevents paralysis, and the Hidden Ability Sand Veil increases evasion in sand while preventing sandstorm damage. Galarian Stunfisk becomes Ground/Steel and swaps the offensive and defensive emphasis to 81 Attack, 99 Defense, 66 Special Attack, and 84 Special Defense, favoring Earthquake, Rock Slide, Stealth Rock, Yawn, Curse, Foul Play, and the trapping move Snap Trap. Its only ability, Mimicry, changes its type to match active terrain, which can be useful but also removes the predictable defensive profile that normally makes Ground/Steel valuable. Bold or Calm suit Unovan Stunfisk, while Careful or Impish are natural for the Galarian form.
competitive: Unovan Stunfisk was one of BW PU's best utility walls. Ground/Electric typing, 109 HP, solid mixed defenses, an Electric immunity, Stealth Rock, Discharge, Earth Power, Toxic, and Static let it check many Flying-, Rock-, Poison-, Steel-, and Electric-type threats while spreading paralysis almost incidentally. Smogon describes it as one of the format's most dependable defensive anchors, although Grass-, Water-, Ground-, and Ice-type attacks prevent it from walling indiscriminately. Galarian Stunfisk occupies a different niche in Sword and Shield: Ground/Steel grants excellent resistances and both Electric and Poison immunities, while Stealth Rock, Earthquake, Rock Slide, Yawn, Curse, and Foul Play let it function as a bulky special wall in ZU and PU-level play. Mimicry is often more awkward than a conventional defensive ability because terrain can unexpectedly alter its typing, but the base defensive profile is strong enough to give the regional form a real lower-tier niche. Neither form is a major offensive threat; both succeed by absorbing attacks, setting hazards, and making contact or switching costly.
nuzlocke: Both Stunfisk forms can be useful Nuzlocke walls because base 109 HP and solid defenses allow them to survive many neutral attacks, but their weaknesses are very different and should never be conflated. Unovan Stunfisk is immune to Electric and resists Flying, Poison, Rock, and Steel, but is weak to Water, Grass, Ice, and Ground; Static can occasionally paralyze a contact attacker and make the rest of the battle much safer. Galarian Stunfisk is immune to Electric and Poison and carries a much larger resistance list through Ground/Steel, but is weak to Fire, Water, Fighting, and Ground. Yawn and Stealth Rock offer low-risk team support, while Rock Slide is generally safer than Stone Edge if damage is already sufficient. Galarian Mimicry can unexpectedly change typing under terrain, so players should account for the active terrain before assuming a resistance or immunity is still present.

pokemon.name: Stunfisk
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Unovan Stunfisk lives in mudflats and coastal mud, burying its flat body beneath the surface and waiting for prey to step on it. Symbiotic bacteria associated with its habitat are credited with helping the species develop its electricity-generating organs. Its skin is so tough that even being stepped on by a sumo wrestler does not injure it. When prey makes contact, Stunfisk shocks the victim and inexplicably smiles; if the attack fails to paralyze the target, it can contort its body surprisingly quickly and flop away.

pokemon.name: Stunfisk
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Galarian Stunfisk adapted to iron-rich Galarian mud, losing the electrical abilities of the Unovan form while developing much stronger steel-like fins. It lies buried with only its red-and-white mouth visible, making the mouth resemble a Poké Ball and using that appearance as bait. When prey approaches, the reinforced fins snap shut like a bear trap and hold the victim in place. The form's unique Snap Trap attack and Mimicry ability both reinforce its specialization as an ambush predator shaped by its local environment.

playthrough: Mienfoo evolves into Mienshao at level 50, so the family takes a long time to reach its final form but rewards the wait with an excellent fast Fighting-type. Mienshao has base 125 Attack, 105 Speed, and a usable base 95 Special Attack, letting it use High Jump Kick, Drain Punch, U-turn, Fake Out, Stone Edge, Acrobatics, Knock Off in later games, and mixed coverage such as Aura Sphere or special moves where useful. Regenerator is often the most practical ability because switching out restores one-third of Mienshao's maximum HP, offsetting chip from Life Orb, hazards, or repeated pivoting; Reckless instead boosts recoil and crash moves such as High Jump Kick, while Inner Focus prevents flinching. High Jump Kick offers enormous damage but is dangerous in story play because a miss or failed hit causes crash damage, so Drain Punch or another reliable Fighting move is often safer when the extra power is unnecessary. Pure Fighting is weak to Flying and Psychic in Generation V and gains a Fairy weakness from Generation VI onward. Jolly is usually ideal because preserving base 105 Speed helps Mienshao avoid damage altogether.
competitive: Mienshao was one of BW UU's premier offensive pivots. Base 125 Attack and 105 Speed let it pressure most of the tier with High Jump Kick, while U-turn and Regenerator formed an unusually efficient hit-and-run core: Mienshao could attack, pivot out, and recover one-third of its HP each time it left the field. Reckless offered an alternative that made High Jump Kick even more destructive, and its usable base 95 Special Attack allowed mixed sets to punish physical answers with coverage such as Hidden Power Ice in the era. Mienshao also had a small BW OU niche as a Choice Scarf revenge killer because its Speed and coverage let it pick off boosted or naturally fast threats. Its poor 65/60/60 bulk is the enduring limitation, making prediction and momentum far more important than defensive switching. Later generations continued to use Mienshao as a lower-tier pivot and wallbreaker, with Regenerator remaining one of the best abilities for sustaining an otherwise frail offensive Pokemon.
nuzlocke: Mienshao is excellent at ending favorable Nuzlocke matchups quickly, but it is much less forgiving when an opponent survives. Base 105 Speed and 125 Attack reduce the number of turns in which something can go wrong, while Regenerator can restore large amounts of health just by switching and is particularly valuable over long routes. High Jump Kick is extremely risky under permadeath rules because missing or striking an immune target causes severe crash damage, so Drain Punch is usually the safer Fighting STAB whenever it secures the same knockout. Flying, Psychic, and later Fairy attacks remain dangerous because Mienshao's defenses are only base 60. Jolly Mienshao is safest when used as a fast attacker and pivot rather than as a Pokemon expected to absorb neutral hits.

pokemon.name: Mienfoo
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Mienfoo lives and trains in secluded mountain groups, with different groups developing their own styles of kicks and chops. It specializes in rapid, flowing combinations rather than raw single-hit power, becoming more precise as its concentration improves. A well-trained individual can perform around one hundred arm chops in a minute. Despite its small size, Mienfoo is temperamental and may attack anything that approaches too closely.

pokemon.name: Mienshao
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Mienshao is a disciplined martial artist that uses the long fur on its arms like flexible whips during combat. Before attacking, it may produce a distinctive wail, then strike with extremely fast chains of blows. When facing a genuinely powerful opponent, Mienshao can bite away portions of its own arm fur to reduce weight and move even faster. It is generally portrayed as respectful and focused, frequently training alongside its Trainer rather than behaving as aggressively as Mienfoo.

playthrough: Druddigon is a single-stage pure Dragon-type with base 120 Attack, 90 Defense, 90 Special Defense, and very low base 48 Speed. Dragon Claw or Outrage provides physical STAB, while Earthquake, Rock Slide, Crunch, Sucker Punch, Fire Punch, Thunder Punch, Glare, Stealth Rock, and other coverage or utility let it function as a slow bruiser rather than a sweeper. Rough Skin damages opponents that make contact, Sheer Force boosts moves with secondary effects by 30 percent while removing those effects, and the Hidden Ability Mold Breaker lets Druddigon ignore opposing abilities when attacking. Its balanced defenses make it reasonably sturdy, but pure Dragon is weak to Ice and Dragon in Generation V and Fairy from Generation VI onward. Glare is particularly useful because it can paralyze many targets regardless of type and compensate for Druddigon's terrible Speed. Adamant maximizes physical damage, while Brave works naturally under Trick Room and Careful can reinforce its special bulk.
competitive: Druddigon was one of BW RU's most dangerous Dragon-types. Base 120 Attack, excellent 77/90/90 bulk for the tier, and the scarcity of strong Dragon resists in lower tiers made its STAB extremely difficult to absorb, while Rough Skin punished physical contact and Sheer Force strengthened several coverage moves. It could run Choice Band, Stealth Rock, Glare, Dragon Tail, Sucker Punch, and bulky utility sets, giving it much more flexibility than a simple slow attacker. Smogon specifically highlights Druddigon as one of the tier's premier Dragon-types, where its low base 48 Speed is often offset by bulk, priority, paralysis support, or Trick Room. Its weaknesses are straightforward: faster Ice- or Dragon-type attackers can force it out, and later Fairy-types added another important defensive problem. Druddigon has remained a lower-tier physical tank and breaker rather than moving into sustained upper-tier play, but within those formats it has repeatedly been a serious threat.
nuzlocke: Druddigon is a good Nuzlocke Pokemon because it arrives fully evolved, has no evolution requirement to manage, and combines base 120 Attack with solid 90/90 defenses. Rough Skin is particularly Nuzlocke-friendly because it punishes contact without Druddigon spending a turn, while Glare can slow dangerous opponents and make the rest of the team safer. Its very low Speed means it commonly takes a hit before attacking, so Ice, Dragon, and later Fairy coverage should be scouted carefully rather than relying on bulk alone. Sucker Punch can finish faster weakened targets, but prediction-based priority is less reliable than a straightforward attack when the opponent might use status or setup. Adamant or Careful are both sensible depending on whether the run values immediate damage or a larger defensive margin.

pokemon.name: Druddigon
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Druddigon is an aggressive, cunning cave-dwelling Dragon whose bright red head is harder than rock. Its wings absorb sunlight to warm its body; if it becomes too cold, Druddigon can become unable to move. Rather than excavating its own lairs, it often occupies caves and tunnels created by Pokemon such as Diglett, Dugtrio, Onix, and Excadrill. It hunts by chasing prey through those confined spaces and seizing victims with its long claws.

playthrough: Golett evolves into Golurk at level 43, producing a Ground/Ghost physical attacker with base 124 Attack, 89 HP, and base 55 Speed. Earthquake or High Horsepower and Shadow Punch or later Poltergeist provide powerful STAB, while Dynamic Punch, Drain Punch, Ice Punch, Thunder Punch, Fire Punch, Stealth Rock, and Fly give Golurk unusually broad physical coverage. Iron Fist boosts punching moves by 20 percent, No Guard makes every move used by or against Golurk hit regardless of accuracy, and Klutz suppresses most held-item effects and is generally the least useful ordinary ability. Ground/Ghost grants complete Electric, Normal, and Fighting immunities plus a quadruple Poison resistance, but Water, Grass, Ice, Ghost, and Dark attacks are super effective. Brave is excellent for Trick Room and Adamant maximizes damage in ordinary play. Mega Golurk keeps Ground/Ghost typing and base 55 Speed but rises to base 159 Attack, 105 Defense, and 105 Special Defense; in current ability-enabled data it gains Unseen Fist, allowing contact moves to deal reduced damage even through protection.
competitive: Standard Golurk was one of BW NU's premier physical threats. Ground/Ghost gives it three immunities, strong complementary STAB, and a useful matchup into common Fighting-types such as Sawk and Primeape, while base 124 Attack lets Choice Band sets 2HKO much of the tier with the correct move. Iron Fist powers up Shadow Punch and punching coverage, while No Guard supports perfectly accurate Dynamic Punch and other normally unreliable attacks; Golurk can also use the switches it forces to set Stealth Rock. Its base 55 Speed is the main obstacle, leaving it vulnerable to revenge killing and preventing it from sweeping faster offensive teams without Trick Room or substantial support. Mega Golurk is far newer and should be treated separately from that established résumé. Current data gives it base 159 Attack, 105 Defense, 105 Special Defense, and Unseen Fist, dramatically improving both immediate power and durability while leaving the same low Speed and five weaknesses intact.
nuzlocke: Golurk is very useful in Nuzlockes because Electric, Normal, and Fighting immunities create completely safe entries against known attacks, while base 124 Attack makes its retaliation extremely dangerous. Iron Fist strengthens reliable punching coverage, whereas No Guard can make inaccurate moves perfectly reliable but also guarantees that opposing attacks aimed at Golurk will not miss, removing an occasional source of luck. Water, Grass, Ice, Ghost, and Dark attacks remain serious threats, and base 55 Speed means Golurk often has to absorb one before moving. Mega Golurk improves both defenses to 105 and Attack to 159, making it much safer against neutral physical and special damage, but does not fix the Speed issue or its type weaknesses. Adamant or Brave are natural choices, with Brave especially useful on Trick Room teams.

pokemon.name: Golett
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Golett is an artificial Pokemon created by an ancient civilization from clay or similar material and animated by mysterious energy. A seal on its body helps contain that energy, which otherwise becomes unstable. Golett was built to obey commands and perform labor, often continuing assigned tasks long after the people who created it disappeared. It can remain active for extraordinarily long periods without conventional food or rest.

pokemon.name: Golurk
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Golurk was built by ancient people as a heavy laborer and guardian of both humans and Pokemon. It follows its master's orders with extreme loyalty and can retract its limbs to expose energy outlets, using those openings like rocket thrusters to fly at very high speed despite its enormous size. A seal on its chest restrains the mysterious internal energy that powers it; if the seal is removed, Golurk can enter a violent uncontrolled rampage capable of reducing a town to rubble. One theory proposes that a perpetual-motion mechanism inside its body produces effectively limitless energy, but this has never been proven.

pokemon.name: Golurk
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Mega Evolution overstimulates Golurk's internal energy until its chest seal can no longer contain it properly, leaving Mega Golurk in a constant state close to catastrophic detonation. Bright energy escapes around its joints and torso, and the broken seal hangs almost uselessly from its chest. Mega Golurk can fire its own fists like rockets from the energy-filled structures around its wrists and then draw them back to its arms. The form magnifies the same unstable power source that standard Golurk normally has to keep carefully sealed.

playthrough: Pawniard evolves into Bisharp at the very late level 52, and in Paldea Bisharp evolves into Kingambit after defeating three wild Bisharp that are holding Leader's Crests and then leveling up. The entire family is Dark/Steel, giving it an excellent resistance profile plus Psychic and Poison immunities, but Fighting deals quadruple damage and Fire and Ground are also super effective. Bisharp has base 125 Attack and 70 Speed, while Kingambit trades Speed for much greater bulk and power with base 100 HP, 135 Attack, 120 Defense, and only base 50 Speed. Iron Head, Night Slash or Knock Off in relevant generations, Sucker Punch, Kowtow Cleave on Kingambit, Swords Dance, Low Kick, and other physical coverage give the line excellent offensive tools. Defiant raises Attack by two stages whenever an opponent lowers one of its stats, while Kingambit's signature Supreme Overlord boosts the power of its moves by 10 percent for each fainted ally, up to five. Adamant is usually ideal, though Jolly can help Bisharp and slower Kingambit variants; the biggest story drawback is the extremely late and specialized evolution path.
competitive: Bisharp already had a strong competitive identity before Kingambit existed. Defiant, Swords Dance, powerful Dark and Steel STAB, and Sucker Punch made it an effective lower-tier breaker in BW and a much more prominent threat in later generations, especially once Knock Off became stronger and Defog became widespread because Defiant could punish attempted stat drops from hazard removal. Kingambit then elevated the family into one of SV OU's defining offensive forces. Base 135 Attack, excellent 100/120/85 bulk, Swords Dance, Kowtow Cleave, Iron Head, and powerful STAB Sucker Punch compensate for base 50 Speed, while Supreme Overlord grows stronger as teammates faint and can turn Kingambit into an extraordinary late-game cleaner. Smogon has described Kingambit as one of the most influential Pokemon in SV OU and subjected it to a suspect test because its bulk, priority, Supreme Overlord, and Terastallization interactions could singlehandedly reshape endgames. It remained legal after that process and is still OU, making this one of the clearest examples of a later evolution dramatically raising an older family's competitive ceiling.
nuzlocke: The Pawniard family is very powerful in Nuzlockes once fully evolved because Dark/Steel provides two immunities and many resistances, and both Bisharp and Kingambit can threaten one-hit knockouts with excellent Attack. Sucker Punch is valuable priority but requires the opponent to choose an attacking move, so it should not be treated as guaranteed speed control against setup or status users. The quadruple Fighting weakness is the critical danger: even weak Fighting coverage can kill Bisharp or Kingambit unexpectedly, and Fire or Ground attacks are also serious threats. Kingambit is far more forgiving than Bisharp against neutral physical damage because of 100 HP and 120 Defense, while Supreme Overlord can create strong comeback potential if the run has already suffered losses. The practical drawback is availability—Pawniard reaches Bisharp only at level 52, and Kingambit's Leader's Crest evolution requirement exists only in games that support that later evolution.

pokemon.name: Pawniard
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Pawniard hunts in packs led by Bisharp and obeys its leader even when an attack leaves it injured. It clings to prey and repeatedly stabs with the blades covering its body, then sharpens those blades afterward on favored stones found near rivers. Damage to the blades can be fatal, making maintenance of its metal body a matter of survival rather than appearance. Every member of a pack trains with the ambition of eventually becoming a leader.

pokemon.name: Bisharp
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Bisharp commands packs of Pawniard and fights rival Bisharp to determine which individual will lead; the loser is cast out. During hunts, Pawniard weaken prey while Bisharp delivers the finishing blow, and Bisharp is described as pitiless and willing to use underhanded tactics. A chipped or damaged head blade forces a Bisharp to retire from leadership. Victorious Bisharp can absorb defeated packs into their own group, while the strongest Bisharp may eventually rise further and become Kingambit.

pokemon.name: Kingambit
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Kingambit commands multiple colonies of Pawniard and Bisharp as a personal army and is said to evolve only from exceptionally powerful Bisharp. It is intensely battle-hungry and continues pursuing what it wants until it wins. Despite its commanding appearance, Kingambit is not considered a sophisticated strategist and often relies on sheer numbers and brute force instead. Its long metallic hair is strong enough to support its weight like a seat and can also be shaped into spikes for attacking.

playthrough: Bouffalant is a single-stage pure Normal-type with base 110 Attack, 95 HP, 95 Defense, and 95 Special Defense, giving it an unusually strong combination of power and natural bulk. Head Charge is its signature 120-base-power Normal attack and deals recoil equal to one-quarter of the damage inflicted, while Return in older games, Body Slam, Earthquake, Megahorn, Stone Edge or Rock Slide, Swords Dance, and coverage such as Wild Charge provide alternative options. Reckless boosts recoil moves by 20 percent, making Head Charge even stronger, while Sap Sipper grants complete Grass immunity and raises Attack by one stage when hit by a Grass move; Soundproof blocks most sound-based attacks. Pure Normal has only a Fighting weakness and a Ghost immunity but almost no resistances, so Bouffalant often relies on raw bulk rather than typing to take hits. Adamant is ideal for straightforward wallbreaking, while Brave works well under Trick Room because base 55 Speed is low. Head Charge is powerful enough to solve many story fights immediately, but the recoil should be avoided when a safer move already secures the knockout.
competitive: Bouffalant was a strong BW RU wallbreaker. Base 110 Attack is backed by the exclusive Head Charge, and Reckless can increase that already powerful recoil move by another 20 percent, while 95/95/95 bulk lets Bouffalant survive far more neutral damage than most slow physical attackers. Sap Sipper offers an equally important alternative by creating a Grass immunity and providing an Attack boost, allowing Bouffalant to switch into moves such as Sleep Powder, Leech Seed, or Grass STAB and immediately become more dangerous. Choice Band, Substitute, Swords Dance, Earthquake, Megahorn, and Stone Edge gave it enough options to punish most conventional Normal resists or defensive answers. Its base 55 Speed and weakness to common Fighting attacks kept it from becoming a higher-tier staple, but within RU it was a legitimate breaker capable of forcing significant damage whenever it entered safely.
nuzlocke: Bouffalant is one of the safer slow physical attackers for Nuzlockes because base 95 in HP, Defense, and Special Defense gives it unusually balanced durability. Sap Sipper is particularly valuable because it provides a free Grass immunity and Attack boost, and pure Normal adds a Ghost immunity while leaving Fighting as the only ordinary type weakness. Head Charge can produce huge damage but also creates avoidable recoil, so Body Slam, Return in games where it exists, or another reliable move is usually safer when the extra power is unnecessary. Reckless increases both Head Charge and other recoil-based damage but does nothing to improve survivability, whereas Sap Sipper can create completely safe switch opportunities. Adamant is excellent for general use, while Brave fits especially well on a Trick Room team.

pokemon.name: Bouffalant
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Bouffalant is highly territorial and charges intruders head-first with enough force to destroy cars or even derail a train. Its enormous woolly head covering absorbs much of the impact from those attacks and functions as natural protection. Wild Bouffalant live in herds of roughly twenty individuals, and individuals with more impressive head hair hold higher social positions within the group. Pokédex lore says that a Bouffalant which betrays its herd somehow loses the hair from its head, linking the species' appearance directly to social status and loyalty.

playthrough: Rufflet evolves into Braviary at level 54, making the family a late investment despite the strength of both final forms. Standard Braviary is a Normal/Flying physical attacker with base 123 Attack, 100 HP, and 80 Speed; Brave Bird, Return in older games, Body Slam, Close Combat or Superpower, Rock Slide, U-turn, Roost, and Bulk Up give it strong offense and useful longevity. Keen Eye prevents accuracy drops, Sheer Force boosts attacks with secondary effects while removing those effects, and the Hidden Ability Defiant raises Attack by two stages whenever an opponent lowers one of Braviary's stats. Hisuian Braviary instead becomes Psychic/Flying and shifts toward special offense with base 112 Special Attack, 110 HP, and 65 Speed, using Psychic, Esper Wing, Air Slash or Hurricane, Calm Mind, Roost, and coverage rather than physical Normal STAB. Its abilities are Keen Eye, Sheer Force, and the Hidden Ability Tinted Lens, which doubles the damage of resisted attacks and makes its dual STAB harder to switch into. Adamant or Jolly suit standard Braviary, while Modest or Timid are more natural for the Hisuian form; the main practical drawback for either route is carrying Rufflet all the way to level 54.
competitive: Standard Braviary had a real BW competitive niche despite being officially NU. Smogon describes it as an extremely powerful physical attacker whose base 123 Attack, Brave Bird, Superpower, Return, U-turn, Roost, and Choice items made both Choice Scarf revenge-killing and Choice Band wallbreaking viable in RU and UU play. Defiant is especially useful because opposing Intimidate or other stat drops can turn directly into an Attack boost, while Roost helps offset Brave Bird recoil and Stealth Rock damage. Hisuian Braviary occupies a different modern role: Psychic/Flying typing, base 112 Special Attack, Sheer Force or Tinted Lens, Esper Wing, Psychic, Hurricane, and Calm Mind make it a slower special breaker rather than a direct analogue of the standard form. Its base 65 Speed and five weaknesses prevent easy sweeping without support, but Tinted Lens can make conventional resistances much less reliable. The two forms therefore share strong Flying offense but have almost opposite attacking profiles.
nuzlocke: Braviary is powerful in Nuzlockes once Rufflet finally reaches level 54, but the long unevolved period is itself a meaningful risk. Standard Braviary's base 100 HP and 123 Attack let it survive moderate neutral damage and end fights quickly, while its Ground and Ghost immunities create useful switch opportunities. Brave Bird is extremely strong but recoil can turn a clean victory into dangerous chip, so non-recoil Flying or Normal options are often safer when they already guarantee the knockout. Hisuian Braviary trades the Ghost immunity for a strong Fighting resistance and Psychic resistance, but it becomes weak to Ghost and Dark in addition to Rock, Electric, and Ice. Roost is valuable on either form, and Jolly or Timid natures can be safer than maximum-power alternatives when moving first prevents a dangerous retaliation.

pokemon.name: Rufflet
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Rufflet is a male-only young bird that is extremely combative from birth. It deliberately challenges opponents larger and stronger than itself, sometimes even attacking its own parent, because repeated battles and injuries are believed to make it stronger. Its thick talons can crack hard Berries and even split Shellder shells so Rufflet can eat the contents. Despite its bravado, it cries when it loses a fight.

pokemon.name: Braviary
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Standard Braviary is a powerful aerial fighter known for exceptional courage and loyalty. It will continue battling for its companions even after being badly injured, and individuals with more battle scars are treated with greater respect by other Braviary. Its strong talons can crush large objects, while its wings allow sustained long-distance flight. The species' reputation for bravery has made it a common symbol on emblems and flags.

pokemon.name: Braviary
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Hisuian Braviary is larger and more solitary than the Unovan form and migrates to Hisui from northern regions during winter. It combines flight with powerful psychic abilities, using bloodcurdling cries infused with psychic energy to send shock waves across lakes and stun prey hidden beneath the surface. Once prey floats upward, Braviary seizes it with its talons. Psychic power can also heighten its senses and place it into a trance-like state that increases its physical strength.

playthrough: Vullaby evolves into Mandibuzz at level 54, so like Rufflet it remains unevolved unusually late. Mandibuzz is a Dark/Flying defensive Pokemon with base 110 HP, 105 Defense, 95 Special Defense, and 80 Speed, making it much better at absorbing attacks than dealing direct damage. Foul Play is especially useful because it uses the opponent's Attack stat in its damage calculation, while Knock Off, Roost, Taunt, Toxic in older games, U-turn, and Defog from later generations support a durable utility role. Big Pecks prevents Defense drops, Overcoat blocks weather damage and from Generation VI onward also grants immunity to powder and spore moves, while Weak Armor lowers Defense and raises Speed after physical hits. Dark/Flying gives complete Psychic and Ground immunities but is weak to Electric, Ice, and Rock, with Fairy added from Generation VI onward. Impish or Careful are natural natures, and Mandibuzz is most valuable when used as a wall and support Pokemon rather than being forced into conventional offense.
competitive: Mandibuzz was officially NU in BW but already possessed a serious UU niche because 110/105/95 bulk, Dark/Flying typing, Roost, Taunt, Toxic, and Whirlwind allowed it to function as a durable mixed wall. Smogon specifically notes that its typing and defenses let it check a broad collection of threats despite low offensive stats. Later generations improved Mandibuzz considerably: stronger Knock Off, widespread Defog access, Foul Play, and Overcoat's new powder immunity gave it much more reliable role compression, and it became a recurring upper-tier defensive Pokemon in several formats. Foul Play is central to this identity because Mandibuzz can punish powerful physical attackers without investing in its own mediocre base 65 Attack. Its Stealth Rock weakness, Electric/Ice/Rock coverage, and reliance on Roost remain exploitable, but very few Flying-types combine comparable mixed bulk, item disruption, hazard removal, and two immunities.
nuzlocke: Mandibuzz is one of the safer defensive Flying-types for a Nuzlocke once it finally evolves at level 54. Its large HP and strong mixed defenses give it a substantial margin against neutral attacks, while Ground and Psychic immunities create completely safe switches when the opponent's move is known. Roost provides reliable healing and Foul Play allows Mandibuzz to punish high-Attack opponents without taking offensive risks of its own. Electric, Ice, Rock, and later Fairy attacks are the main danger, and Stealth Rock can repeatedly erode its health before it has a chance to act. Overcoat is particularly useful in later generations because powder moves such as Spore no longer work against it, adding another predictable defensive advantage.

pokemon.name: Vullaby
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Vullaby is a female-only young vulture that wears a cracked skull around its lower body as protective armor. As it grows, it repeatedly outgrows these bones and replaces them, often passing older pieces down to smaller Vullaby. Individuals even quarrel over which bones are the most comfortable. Vullaby has a large appetite and tends to chase weaker creatures despite being unable to fly well.

pokemon.name: Mandibuzz
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Mandibuzz is a scavenging predator that builds nests from collected bones and decorates its body with them, with different bone arrangements apparently going in and out of fashion. It patrols from the air for weakened prey, swoops down to seize victims such as Cubone, and carries them back to its nest. Mandibuzz also cares for Vullaby and can provide the bones worn by younger members of the species. Like Vullaby, Mandibuzz is entirely female.

playthrough: Heatmor is a single-stage pure Fire Pokemon with mixed attacking stats—base 97 Attack and 105 Special Attack—but only base 65 Speed and 66 in both defenses. Flamethrower or Fire Blast, Fire Lash from Generation VII onward, Giga Drain, Superpower, Sucker Punch, Knock Off, Focus Blast, and other coverage let it attack from either side of the spectrum. Gluttony causes certain held Berries to activate at half HP rather than one-quarter, Flash Fire grants a complete Fire immunity and boosts Fire moves after absorbing one, and the Hidden Ability White Smoke prevents opponents from lowering Heatmor's stats. Fire Lash is particularly useful in later generations because it deals physical Fire damage while lowering the target's Defense, allowing Heatmor or a physical teammate to snowball pressure. Pure Fire is weak to Water, Ground, and Rock and resists several common types, but Heatmor's mediocre defenses and low Speed mean it rarely wants to take unnecessary neutral hits. Modest, Mild, Rash, or Adamant can all make sense depending on whether the set is special, mixed, or physical.
competitive: Heatmor was a BW ZU Pokemon with a small lower-tier niche as a mixed attacker. Its 105 Special Attack and 97 Attack let it combine Fire Blast with Giga Drain, Superpower, and Sucker Punch to punish several different kinds of switch-ins, while Flash Fire could generate a free Fire boost if Heatmor entered on the right move. The problem was always its base 65 Speed and mediocre 85/66/66 bulk, which left it easy to revenge kill and difficult to bring into battle safely. Later access to Fire Lash gave Heatmor a distinctive physical tool that always lowers the target's Defense when it connects, but even SM analyses still describe it as badly hindered by low Speed and competition from stronger Fire-types. Heatmor therefore has real offensive flexibility without ever developing the efficiency needed for sustained upper-tier play.
nuzlocke: Heatmor can be useful in a Nuzlocke because it arrives fully evolved and has enough mixed offense to exploit whichever defensive stat is weaker. Flash Fire is the safest ability because it creates a full immunity and can turn a predicted Fire attack into an immediate damage boost. Sucker Punch can finish weakened faster threats, while Giga Drain provides some recovery against Water- or Ground-type targets that do not move first and KO Heatmor. Water, Ground, and Rock attacks are dangerous, and its low Speed means it frequently takes damage before acting. Flamethrower is generally safer than Fire Blast when the extra power is unnecessary, while Fire Lash's guaranteed Defense drop can provide reliable physical utility in later generations.

pokemon.name: Heatmor
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Heatmor is an anteater-like predator whose body functions partly like a furnace. It draws air through the opening in its tail to keep an internal fire burning and expels that fire from its mouth as a long, flame-covered tongue. Durant are its preferred prey: Heatmor uses the fiery tongue to melt through their steel armor and consume the softer body inside. If the tail opening becomes blocked, Heatmor can become ill because it can no longer draw in enough air to maintain its internal combustion.

playthrough: Durant is a single-stage Bug/Steel physical attacker with base 109 Attack, 112 Defense, and an excellent base 109 Speed, but only 58 HP and 48 Special Defense. Iron Head and X-Scissor provide accurate dual STAB, while First Impression in later games, Rock Slide, Crunch, Thunder Fang, Superpower, Stomping Tantrum, Hone Claws, and other coverage can support sweeping or wallbreaking. Swarm boosts Bug attacks at low HP, Hustle raises Attack by 50 percent but multiplies the accuracy of physical moves by only 0.8, and the Hidden Ability Truant forces Durant to skip every other turn and is generally a severe drawback outside specialized strategies. Bug/Steel gives a huge collection of resistances and a Poison immunity, with Fire as its only conventional weakness—but Fire deals quadruple damage. Jolly is usually ideal because base 109 Speed is one of Durant's best assets, while Hone Claws can partly compensate for Hustle's dangerous accuracy penalty.
competitive: Durant was one of BW RU's premier offensive threats. Base 109 Attack and 109 Speed are already excellent for the tier, and Hustle pushes its Attack dramatically higher, allowing Choice Band, Hone Claws, and all-out attacking sets to break teams that would otherwise withstand ordinary Bug- or Steel-type offense. Smogon describes Durant as one of the tier's best Pokemon, capable of functioning as a wallbreaker, sweeper, or revenge killer while its Bug/Steel typing and base 112 Defense provide genuine opportunities to enter the field. Hustle is also its greatest weakness because physical accuracy falls to 80 percent of normal, meaning even apparently favorable turns can be lost to a miss. Special attacks and Fire coverage exploit Durant's terrible 58/48 special bulk, and the quadruple Fire weakness remains catastrophic. Even so, its unusual combination of speed, power, defensive typing, and physical bulk gave it a far stronger competitive résumé than most standalone Unova species.
nuzlocke: Durant is simultaneously powerful and dangerous in a Nuzlocke. Base 109 Speed and Attack let it remove many opponents before they act, while Bug/Steel supplies numerous resistances and strong physical Defense. The problem is Hustle: the 50 percent Attack boost comes with a substantial accuracy penalty, and a single miss can expose Durant's poor special bulk or quadruple Fire weakness. If Hustle is the ability, Hone Claws is valuable because it improves both Attack and accuracy, but setting up is only safe against opponents that cannot threaten Fire coverage. Truant is generally undesirable because losing every other turn is exceptionally dangerous under permadeath rules, while Swarm is predictable but much less powerful. Jolly Durant with accurate STAB is safest when used to exploit its Speed and resistances rather than gambling unnecessarily on low-accuracy coverage.

pokemon.name: Durant
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Durant is an extremely territorial ant Pokemon that forms large colonies inside maze-like tunnel systems excavated through mountains. Its steel armor and rock-crushing mandibles evolved partly as protection against its natural predator, Heatmor. Colony members take on different roles when defending the nest, coordinating attacks against intruders such as Heatmor or Sandaconda. Durant primarily eats vegetation and usually stops pursuing a threat once it has been driven beyond the colony's territory.

playthrough: Deino evolves into Zweilous at level 50 and Zweilous evolves into Hydreigon at level 64, giving this family the highest level requirement for a final evolution achieved purely by leveling. The payoff is substantial: Hydreigon is a Dark/Dragon mixed attacker with base 125 Special Attack, 105 Attack, 98 Speed, and balanced 92/90/90 bulk. Draco Meteor or Dragon Pulse and Dark Pulse provide powerful special STAB, while Flamethrower or Fire Blast, Surf, Earth Power, Flash Cannon, U-turn, and later Nasty Plot give it exceptional coverage and wallbreaking flexibility. Levitate grants a Ground immunity in addition to Dark's Psychic immunity, while Deino and Zweilous are forced to use Hustle, which boosts physical Attack by 50 percent but lowers physical move accuracy to 80 percent of normal. In Generation V Hydreigon is weak to Fighting, Bug, Ice, and Dragon; from Generation VI onward Fairy becomes a quadruple weakness. Timid is usually ideal for special offense, while Modest maximizes damage when Speed control is available.
competitive: Hydreigon was an OU Pokemon in BW and remains one of Generation V's most versatile special attackers. Base 125 Special Attack, 98 Speed, Draco Meteor, Dark Pulse, Fire Blast, Earth Power, Surf, U-turn, and strong mixed options give it coverage against nearly every conventional defensive answer, while Levitate adds Ground immunity and protection from Spikes. Smogon notes that Hydreigon's excellent coverage and defensive utility give it a real OU niche even though faster Dragons and Psychic-types compete heavily for team slots. Fairy typing significantly changed its later-generation outlook by creating a quadruple weakness, but Hydreigon remained an important UU-level breaker and pivot across several generations; current SV tiering still places it in UU with viable OU, Monotype, Battle Stadium, and VGC applications. Nasty Plot in later movepools adds another dangerous route, allowing Hydreigon to transform from a flexible Choice or pivot attacker into a dedicated special sweeper. Its recurring limits are the awkward base 98 Speed tier and vulnerability to common Fighting, Dragon, Ice, and especially Fairy attacks.
nuzlocke: The Deino family can eventually become one of the strongest Nuzlocke encounters in a game, but reaching Hydreigon is itself a major survival challenge. Deino does not evolve until level 50 and Zweilous until level 64, leaving the player with two imperfect middle stages for much longer than almost any other three-stage family. Both Deino and Zweilous are forced to use Hustle, so physical attacks can miss at dangerous moments; special moves do not suffer Hustle's accuracy penalty and can sometimes be safer even before Hydreigon's special-oriented final stats arrive. Once evolved, Hydreigon gains Levitate, two useful immunities, excellent coverage, and enough bulk to survive many neutral attacks, but Fairy moves from Generation VI onward deal quadruple damage. Timid Hydreigon with reliable special attacks is generally safer than recoil-free but inaccurate or overly prediction-dependent options.

pokemon.name: Deino
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Deino cannot see because shaggy fur covers its eyes, so it explores the world primarily by biting and charging into whatever it encounters. This behavior leaves its body covered in wounds, but constant biting also helps it learn about unfamiliar objects. It has a voracious appetite and eats almost anything. Because the species is both blind and naturally aggressive, raising one safely requires significant patience.

pokemon.name: Zweilous
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Zweilous has two heads with separate personalities, preferences, and appetites, and the pair constantly compete with one another. Each head tries to establish dominance by eating more than the other, causing Zweilous to overeat and often leaving it covered in scars from internal fighting even when no outside enemy is present. Once the food supply in an area is exhausted, the Pokemon migrates elsewhere while the heads argue over which direction to travel. Giving unequal attention to the two heads can provoke jealousy and fighting.

pokemon.name: Hydreigon
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Hydreigon has three apparent heads, but only the central head contains a brain; the two secondary heads are actually arm-like structures that lack independent thought. All three mouths can generate attacks, and Hydreigon alternates among them relentlessly until a target is defeated. The species is notoriously destructive and may attack almost anything it sees moving, with old stories describing entire villages being destroyed. Later lore suggests some of this hostility may be linked to centuries of persecution by ancient humans who treated Hydreigon as evil incarnate, while trained individuals can still become obedient and cooperative with trusted Trainers.

playthrough: Larvesta evolves into Volcarona at level 59, one of the latest ordinary level-based evolutions in the series, so the line requires a long investment before reaching its full potential. Volcarona is a Bug/Fire special sweeper with base 135 Special Attack, 105 Special Defense, and 100 Speed, and Quiver Dance is its defining move because one use raises Special Attack, Special Defense, and Speed simultaneously. Fiery Dance or Flamethrower and Bug Buzz provide reliable STAB, while Giga Drain, Psychic, Hurricane in some generations, Morning Sun or Roost where available, and later coverage can round out a sweeping set. Flame Body has a 30 percent chance to burn opponents that make contact, while the Hidden Ability Swarm boosts Bug-type moves when HP is low. The enormous drawback is the quadruple Rock weakness, which makes Rock coverage and especially Stealth Rock extremely dangerous; Water and Flying are also super effective. Timid is usually the safest nature because preserving base 100 Speed makes Quiver Dance sweeps easier, while Modest maximizes damage when speed control is already available.
competitive: Volcarona was a major BW OU win condition and remains one of the most iconic Quiver Dance sweepers in competitive Pokemon. Base 135 Special Attack, 100 Speed, strong Fire/Bug STAB, and Quiver Dance allow it to transform a single free turn into a potential sweep, while Giga Drain, Psychic, or Hidden Power in older generations can punish many conventional Fire-resistant answers. Flame Body also gives physical attackers a significant risk of being burned when they make contact. Its competitive success has always depended heavily on hazard control because a quadruple Rock weakness means Stealth Rock removes half of Volcarona's HP on entry in generations before Heavy-Duty Boots became available. Even with that flaw, Volcarona has remained relevant across many generations because the combination of Quiver Dance, strong STAB, and excellent special stats is difficult to replicate. It is best understood as a high-maintenance but extremely high-upside sweeper rather than a generally safe pivot.
nuzlocke: Volcarona can become one of the strongest late-game Nuzlocke Pokemon available, but reaching level 59 with Larvesta is the main challenge. Once evolved, Quiver Dance can make Volcarona very difficult for special attackers to stop because it raises offense, Speed, and Special Defense together, while Giga Drain or reliable recovery can help offset chip damage. Rock attacks are the critical danger because they deal quadruple damage, and Stealth Rock can remove half of Volcarona's health immediately on entry. Flame Body is useful insurance against physical contact but should be treated as a bonus rather than a survival plan because the burn chance is not guaranteed. Flamethrower or Fiery Dance is generally safer than Fire Blast when the extra power is unnecessary, and Timid Volcarona is safest when it can set up against an opponent that lacks dangerous Rock, Water, or Flying coverage.

pokemon.name: Larvesta
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Larvesta lives around the bases of volcanoes and fires flames from the five horns around its head to frighten predators or prey. Those flames can reach roughly 5,500 degrees Fahrenheit and are described as hot enough to cut through sheets of iron. Larvesta can even use the force of those flames to propel itself through the air. Ancient people believed it came from the sun, calling it an emissary of the sun, although its habit of causing forest fires also made it a serious nuisance.

pokemon.name: Volcarona
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Volcarona scatters burning scales from its six wings and can fill the surrounding area with intense fire. Legends say that when volcanic ash darkened the atmosphere and blocked sunlight, Volcarona's flames replaced the sun's warmth and light for people and Pokemon below. Ancient cultures feared it as the rage or embodiment of the sun and in some places worshiped it as a fire deity. The shrine associated with Volcarona in Relic Castle reflects how seriously those beliefs were once taken.

playthrough: Cobalion is a single-stage Steel/Fighting Legendary with base 129 Defense and 108 Speed, but only base 90 in both attacking stats and 72 Special Defense. Its unusual combination of speed, physical bulk, and typing supports several approaches: Close Combat or Sacred Sword, Iron Head, Volt Switch, Stealth Rock, Swords Dance, Calm Mind, and special coverage such as Flash Cannon can all be useful depending on generation and set. Justified raises Attack by one stage whenever Cobalion is hit by a Dark-type move, which combines well with its natural Dark resistance. Steel/Fighting gives a Poison immunity and many resistances, but Fire, Fighting, and Ground attacks are super effective and strong special attacks can exploit the lower Special Defense. Sacred Sword is safer than Close Combat when the extra power is not required because it does not lower Cobalion's defenses and also ignores the target's defensive stat boosts. Jolly is ideal for physical sets, while Timid can support Calm Mind or special utility.
competitive: Cobalion was a strong BW UU Pokemon whose niche came from role compression rather than overwhelming raw offense. Base 129 Defense and 108 Speed are unusually strong together, while Steel/Fighting typing provides many resistances, a Poison immunity, and a strong matchup into several common Dark-, Rock-, Normal-, and Steel-type threats. Swords Dance, Calm Mind, Stealth Rock, Volt Switch, Taunt, and dual STAB let it function as a sweeper, pivot, or utility setter depending on team needs. That versatility remained relevant in later generations; by SM UU, Smogon described Cobalion as one of the tier's premier threats because it could check major physical attackers while still providing Stealth Rock or offensive setup. Its mediocre base 90 offenses mean it often needs a boost or super-effective hit to break bulky targets, while the low Special Defense makes strong special Fire-, Ground-, or Fighting-type attacks a major problem.
nuzlocke: Cobalion is very reliable in Nuzlockes because base 129 Defense, high Speed, and a large resistance profile make physical damage much easier to manage than with most Fighting-types. Its Poison immunity and resistance to Dark also provide safe switch opportunities, and Justified can turn a predicted Dark move into an Attack boost. The main danger is the base 72 Special Defense: a strong special Fire, Ground, or Fighting attack can do far more damage than the physical bulk suggests. Sacred Sword is particularly Nuzlocke-friendly because it is accurate, ignores opposing Defense boosts, and does not lower Cobalion's own defenses the way Close Combat does. Jolly or Timid are both useful because moving first allows Cobalion to exploit its excellent base 108 Speed rather than relying only on bulk.

pokemon.name: Cobalion
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Cobalion is the calm, commanding leader of the Swords of Justice and is said to possess a heart and body like steel. According to Unovan legend, it joined Terrakion and Virizion in fighting humans after warfare set a forest ablaze and threatened the Pokemon living there. During that crisis, Cobalion directed frightened Pokemon to safety and coordinated the group's resistance. Its presence is so commanding that even unruly Pokemon can be made to obey by its glare.

playthrough: Terrakion is a single-stage Rock/Fighting Legendary built for immediate physical offense, with base 129 Attack, 108 Speed, and balanced 91/90/90 bulk. Close Combat and Stone Edge provide extraordinarily strong dual STAB, while Sacred Sword, Rock Slide, Earthquake, X-Scissor, Swords Dance, Rock Polish, and later coverage support wallbreaking or sweeping. Justified raises Attack by one stage after Terrakion is hit by a Dark-type move, and Dark itself is resisted, making carefully planned switches potentially rewarding. The typing is offensively excellent but defensively awkward, leaving weaknesses to Water, Grass, Fighting, Ground, Psychic, Steel, and later Fairy. Stone Edge's 80 percent accuracy and Close Combat's defensive drops create real story-play risk, so Rock Slide and Sacred Sword can be safer alternatives when their lower power is sufficient. Jolly is usually ideal because base 108 Speed is excellent and preserving that advantage prevents many retaliations.
competitive: Terrakion was one of the best offensive Pokemon in BW OU. Base 129 Attack, 108 Speed, and Rock/Fighting STAB give it near-unresisted offensive coverage, allowing Choice Band, Choice Scarf, Swords Dance, Rock Polish, and even double-boosting sets to all threaten serious damage. Smogon characterized it as one of the generation's premier wallbreakers and revenge killers, with Choice Scarf sets also finding meaningful use in Ubers. Terrakion was similarly prominent in early VGC, where Rock Slide could pressure both opponents at once and Close Combat provided enormous single-target damage. Its many defensive weaknesses prevent it from switching freely, and Stone Edge accuracy can betray even favorable positions, but the raw offensive package is strong enough that those weaknesses rarely erased its value. Few Fighting-types have matched Terrakion's combination of immediate power, Speed, and flexible boosting options.
nuzlocke: Terrakion is extremely powerful in Nuzlockes but requires more care than its balanced defensive stats might suggest because it has many common weaknesses. Base 108 Speed and 129 Attack often allow it to remove threats before they act, while Justified can reward a predicted Dark move with an Attack boost. Close Combat should be used carefully because every use lowers both defenses, and Stone Edge's imperfect accuracy makes Rock Slide the safer choice whenever the lower power still secures the knockout. Sacred Sword is especially useful against opponents that have raised their Defense because it ignores those stat boosts without lowering Terrakion's own defenses. Jolly is generally the safest nature, and Terrakion performs best when treated as an attacker that avoids hits rather than a bulky Legendary that can absorb anything.

pokemon.name: Terrakion
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Terrakion is the physically strongest member of the Swords of Justice and is associated with extraordinary destructive force. Legend claims it can smash through a massive castle wall with a single blow. During the ancient forest fire that drove the Swords of Justice to oppose humans, Terrakion used its strength to reshape the ground and open an escape path for trapped Pokemon. Its role within the group is therefore less about leadership than about raw strength and direct physical protection.

playthrough: Virizion is a single-stage Grass/Fighting Legendary with base 108 Speed, enormous base 129 Special Defense, and balanced base 90 Attack and Special Attack. That mixed profile allows both Swords Dance sets with Leaf Blade and Close Combat or Sacred Sword and Calm Mind sets with Giga Drain, Focus Blast, or special coverage. Stone Edge, Zen Headbutt, Synthesis in relevant generations, Reflect, Light Screen, Taunt, and other utility give it more flexibility than the equal attacking stats initially suggest. Justified raises Attack when hit by a Dark-type move, which combines with Virizion's Dark resistance. Grass/Fighting resists Water, Electric, Grass, Ground, Rock, and Dark but is weak to Fire, Ice, Poison, Psychic, and later Fairy, with Flying dealing quadruple damage in every generation. Jolly or Timid take advantage of base 108 Speed, while Calm can emphasize its exceptional special bulk.
competitive: Virizion was a dangerous BW UU setup Pokemon. Grass/Fighting STAB gives it an excellent matchup against many bulky Water- and Rock-types, while base 108 Speed and base 129 Special Defense provide setup opportunities that most offensive Pokemon do not receive. Swords Dance and Calm Mind allow it to choose either physical or special sweeping, forcing opponents to identify the set before selecting the correct answer. Its physical Attack and Special Attack are only base 90, so boosting is often necessary, and the quadruple Flying weakness leaves several hard checks. Virizion was also highly effective in VGC 2011, where its special bulk, Speed, support options, and resistance to many common spread attacks made it a valuable team piece. Later generations kept the same basic identity in lower tiers: versatile setup, strong special resilience, and useful resistances balanced by middling unboosted power and dangerous Flying coverage.
nuzlocke: Virizion is particularly safe against special Water-, Electric-, Grass-, Rock-, Ground-, and Dark-type attackers because base 129 Special Defense is enormous and the typing resists all of those types. Giga Drain can provide recovery while attacking, while Synthesis where available gives more direct healing. Its base 72 Defense is much less impressive, however, and Flying attacks deal quadruple damage, making even weak physical Flying coverage extremely dangerous. Close Combat also lowers both defenses and can undermine Virizion's best trait, so Sacred Sword is often the safer Fighting move if the extra power is unnecessary. Jolly or Timid help Virizion act first, while Calm can create a very large safety margin against special attackers.

pokemon.name: Virizion
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Virizion is the fastest and most graceful member of the Swords of Justice. During the ancient forest fire associated with the group's conflict with humans, Virizion used its speed to shield fleeing Pokemon from sparks and burning debris while Cobalion guided them and Terrakion opened an escape route. In battle, it darts around opponents at whirlwind-like speed before cutting them with the sharp, blade-like horns on its head. Some portrayals characterize Virizion as the most intelligent and composed member of the group.

playthrough: Tornadus is a pure Flying Legendary with two formes that are changed using the Reveal Glass. Incarnate Forme has base 125 Special Attack, 115 Attack, and 111 Speed, with Prankster giving +1 priority to status moves and the Hidden Ability Defiant sharply raising Attack when an opponent lowers one of its stats. Hurricane, Bleakwind Storm in later games, Focus Blast, Heat Wave, U-turn, Knock Off, Tailwind, Taunt, Rain Dance, and Nasty Plot in later generations allow offensive or support roles. Therian Forme lowers the offenses to 100 Attack and 110 Special Attack but raises Speed to 121, improves both defenses slightly, and replaces the ability with Regenerator, which restores one-third of maximum HP whenever Tornadus switches out. Pure Flying grants a Ground immunity and resistances to Fighting, Bug, and Grass, but Rock, Electric, and Ice are super effective and Stealth Rock causes significant chip. Timid is generally ideal for special offense, while the Incarnate form can also justify Naive or other mixed natures in older generations.
competitive: Tornadus has two sharply different competitive histories. Incarnate Tornadus was a solid BW rain attacker: base 125 Special Attack, 111 Speed, and perfectly accurate Hurricane under rain gave it enormous immediate pressure, while Prankster supported Tailwind, Substitute, Taunt, or Rain Dance. Therian Tornadus was even more oppressive in the original BW metagame because base 121 Speed, Regenerator, U-turn, and rain-boosted Hurricane made it extraordinarily difficult to wear down while still threatening offense; it was eventually banned from BW OU during that era. In later generations, Tornadus-T became one of the game's premier utility pivots, repeatedly appearing in OU thanks to Regenerator, Knock Off, U-turn, Defog in relevant generations, Nasty Plot, broad coverage, and elite Speed. Heavy-Duty Boots later reduced the impact of its Stealth Rock weakness and made the Regenerator pivot cycle even safer. Incarnate Tornadus remains the more explosive Prankster-oriented form, while Therian is generally the superior long-term pivot.
nuzlocke: Both Tornadus formes are useful in Nuzlockes because Flying typing gives a Ground immunity and strong Speed lets them avoid many incoming attacks. Incarnate Tornadus can use Prankster Tailwind, Taunt, or other status moves before most opponents act, creating reliable team support even when direct damage is unnecessary. Therian Tornadus is safer over long routes because Regenerator heals one-third of its HP every time it switches out, making pivoting an efficient source of recovery. Hurricane is extremely powerful but unreliable outside rain, so Bleakwind Storm or more accurate alternatives may be preferable depending on generation and availability; in rain, Hurricane becomes much safer. Electric, Ice, and Rock attacks remain dangerous, and Stealth Rock should be removed or minimized because repeated entry damage undermines both formes, especially before Heavy-Duty Boots exist.

pokemon.name: Tornadus
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Tornadus is a violent wind deity associated with destructive storms and frigid gales. It can travel at roughly 200 miles per hour and whip up winds powerful enough to blow away houses, damage crops, and even alter seasonal weather patterns. Farmers traditionally fear and despise it because of the destruction these storms can cause. Tornadus frequently clashes with Thundurus, and stories portray their battles as disasters that have continued since ancient times.

pokemon.name: Tornadus
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Therian Tornadus has a bird-like body with large wings and is suspected to represent the species' true form, revealed through the Reveal Glass. In this form it travels over oceans searching for a region in which to reside, rather than remaining permanently established in one area. It still controls violent winds but appears more naturally adapted to sustained flight than the cloud-riding Incarnate Forme. Modern records also associate Tornadus with Bleakwind Storm, a frigid wind attack unique to the species.

playthrough: Thundurus is an Electric/Flying Legendary with two interchangeable formes controlled by the Reveal Glass. Incarnate Forme has base 125 Special Attack, 115 Attack, and 111 Speed, while Prankster gives +1 priority to status moves and the Hidden Ability Defiant raises Attack by two stages whenever an opponent lowers one of its stats. Thunderbolt or Thunder, Wildbolt Storm in later games, Volt Switch, Grass Knot, Focus Blast, Psychic, Nasty Plot, Thunder Wave, Taunt, and Rain Dance give it both offensive and support roles. Therian Forme shifts power into base 145 Special Attack while lowering Speed to 101 and gains Volt Absorb, which grants a complete Electric immunity and restores one-quarter of maximum HP when struck by an Electric move. Both formes are immune to Ground and resist Bug, Fighting, Flying, Grass, and Steel, but are weak to Ice and Rock and take significant damage from Stealth Rock. Timid is usually ideal for special sets, while Incarnate can also support mixed or Defiant-oriented strategies.
competitive: Incarnate Thundurus was powerful enough to be removed from standard BW OU and is currently classified in Ubers for the generation.
