Its pure Normal typing is easy to plan around, with only Fighting as a weakness and a complete Ghost immunity. Cotton Guard can make known physical attackers extremely manageable, while Thunder Wave or U-turn provides control without requiring Furfrou to remain exposed. The main limitation is healing: without dependable recovery, repeated neutral hits can accumulate even when each individual hit is small. The nine trims are cosmetic and do not affect Nuzlocke performance, so grooming can be treated purely as an appearance choice.

pokemon.name: Furfrou
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Furfrou is an intelligent and exceptionally loyal canine Pokemon that historically served as a designated guardian of Kalosian royalty. It allows only people it trusts to cut and style its dense white fur. Grooming the coat is said to make its movements swifter, and Kalosian aristocrats once competed to create increasingly elaborate styles. Ten recognized appearances exist—the Natural Form and nine trims—but all are created through grooming rather than biological transformation.

playthrough: Espurr evolves into Meowstic at level 25, with the evolved form's appearance, Hidden Ability, and several learned moves depending on sex. Both ordinary Meowstic share pure Psychic typing and the same 74/48/76/83/81/104 stat line. Male Meowstic is primarily support-oriented and its Hidden Ability Prankster gives +1 priority to status moves such as Reflect, Light Screen, Thunder Wave, Yawn, Trick, and other utility; female Meowstic instead has Competitive, which raises Special Attack by two stages whenever an opposing effect lowers one of its stats, matching its more offensive learnset. Both can also have Keen Eye or Infiltrator, with Infiltrator allowing attacks to bypass Substitute and several screen effects. Mega Meowstic combines the two sexes visually and rises to base 143 Special Attack, 101 Special Defense, and 124 Speed while gaining Trace, which copies an opposing Pokemon's Ability on entry. Timid is ideal for female or Mega offense, while Bold, Calm, or Timid can all support male utility depending on the role.
competitive: Ordinary Meowstic's competitive value differs sharply by sex even though the base stats are identical. Male Meowstic had a legitimate VGC 2014 support niche because Prankster gives priority to Reflect, Light Screen, Thunder Wave, Safeguard, and other support, while Fake Out and base 104 Speed add additional disruption; Smogon nevertheless notes that mediocre bulk and offensive presence can make it difficult to justify over stronger support Pokemon. Female Meowstic is more offensive because Competitive can punish Intimidate and other stat drops by sharply raising Special Attack, but base 83 Special Attack is modest before that activation. Mega Meowstic is a much newer form and should be separated from those established roles: base 143 Special Attack and 124 Speed turn it into a genuine fast special attacker, while Trace can copy powerful opposing abilities and create highly matchup-dependent advantages. It retains pure Psychic typing and the same mediocre physical bulk, so Dark-, Ghost-, and Bug-type priority or strong physical attacks remain important checks.
nuzlocke: Meowstic is useful in Nuzlockes because it evolves relatively early at level 25 and base 104 Speed lets it act before many opponents. Male Meowstic is usually the safer support choice because priority screens or Thunder Wave can protect the entire team, while female Meowstic can capitalize on predictable stat-lowering moves with Competitive and end fights faster. Both forms are weak to Bug, Ghost, and Dark and have only moderate physical Defense, so they should not be treated as tanks. Espurr itself requires care before evolution because its psychic power is strong but its stats are still those of an unevolved Pokemon. Mega Meowstic's base 124 Speed, 143 Special Attack, and 101 Special Defense create a much larger offensive safety margin, but Trace should always be checked mentally because copying the wrong opposing ability can be neutral or even inconvenient rather than helpful.

pokemon.name: Espurr
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Espurr has immense psychic power that it cannot fully control. Two ring-shaped organs beneath its folded ears emit that energy, and Espurr keeps the ears pressed down to prevent the power from leaking out. If released, the psychic force can throw a wrestler or affect an area hundreds of feet across. Its blank expression hides the constant effort required to restrain that energy, and excessive buildup can even cause Espurr to faint.

pokemon.name: Meowstic
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Male Meowstic keeps the eye-like psychic organs inside its ears covered except when threatened. It possesses enough psychic force to destroy extremely heavy machinery, but modern Pokédex accounts describe males as more inclined to support allies than attack directly. This temperament aligns with the male form's status-heavy learnset and Prankster Hidden Ability. Its folded ears therefore function as both a physical restraint on overwhelming power and a deliberate sign of self-control.

pokemon.name: Meowstic
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Female Meowstic has the same enormous psychic potential as males but is described as more aggressive, selfish, and willing to use that power offensively. When threatened, it can unleash its psychic energy at maximum output with little concern for the opponent. Its ears conceal the same eye-like organs that emit the energy, and opening them can release enough force to destroy heavy vehicles. Female Meowstic's more offensive temperament is reflected mechanically by its attacking-oriented learnset and Competitive Hidden Ability.

pokemon.name: Meowstic
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Mega Meowstic visually combines traits of both male and female Meowstic, with no visible difference between the sexes after Mega Evolution. Its ears remain permanently unfurled, fully exposing the psychic organs that ordinary Meowstic normally keep covered. The resulting psychic power is strong enough to compress or expand objects and even contort space itself, while Mega Meowstic constantly levitates under its own power. Its two tails and split coloration deliberately preserve elements of both ordinary gender forms.

playthrough: Honedge evolves into Doublade at level 35, and Doublade evolves into Aegislash with a Dusk Stone. The entire line is Steel/Ghost, giving it complete immunities to Normal, Fighting, and Poison plus a long list of resistances, but weaknesses to Fire, Ground, Ghost, and Dark. Honedge and Doublade use No Guard, which makes moves used by or against them ignore normal accuracy checks; this can make powerful inaccurate coverage reliable, but it also means opposing attacks cannot miss. Aegislash instead has Stance Change and normally begins battle in Shield Forme, using enormous Defense and Special Defense before transforming into Blade Forme immediately before most damaging attacks. King's Shield returns it to Shield Forme while protecting it from damaging moves; in Generations VI and VII, contact into King's Shield lowers the attacker's Attack by two stages, while from Generation VIII onward the drop is only one stage. Aegislash's stance stats were also reduced in Generation VIII from base 150 to base 140 in the relevant offenses or defenses, though it remains extremely strong. Brave or Quiet natures can be useful because moving after an opponent often lets Aegislash absorb a hit in Shield Forme before changing to Blade Forme, while Adamant, Modest, or defensive natures fit more specialized sets.
competitive: Aegislash was one of the most influential new Pokemon of Generation VI. In XY and ORAS its unique Stance Change mechanics, base 150 defensive stats in Shield Forme, base 150 offensive stats in Blade Forme, King's Shield, excellent Steel/Ghost typing, priority Shadow Sneak, Sacred Sword, Shadow Ball, Toxic, and mixed attacking options made it so difficult to prepare for that it was banned from standard OU to Ubers. Its threat was not only raw power: opponents often had to guess whether Aegislash would attack, use King's Shield, spread status, or remain in Shield Forme, and a wrong prediction could cost an attacker both momentum and Attack stages. Doublade also developed its own lower-tier niche with Eviolite, base 150 Defense, Swords Dance, Shadow Sneak, and No Guard. Generation VIII deliberately reduced Aegislash's stance stats from 150 to 140 and weakened King's Shield's Attack penalty, making it substantially more manageable and allowing it to settle into ordinary upper- and mid-tier play rather than remaining an automatic Uber. Its core competitive identity nevertheless remains unique: it controls the timing of offense and defense through form management rather than relying on one fixed stat spread.
nuzlocke: The Honedge line is extremely valuable in Nuzlockes because three immunities and many resistances create a large number of safe switch opportunities. Doublade is physically very sturdy even before evolving, and Eviolite can make it exceptionally difficult for physical attackers to break. No Guard is a double-edged ability, however, because while it prevents your own inaccurate moves from missing, it also prevents enemy attacks from missing Honedge or Doublade. Aegislash is safest when its stance timing is understood: if it moves first with a damaging attack, it enters Blade Forme before the opponent retaliates and loses most of its defensive advantage for that turn; moving second can let it take the hit in Shield Forme and then attack. King's Shield is therefore invaluable for resetting to Shield Forme and scouting, while unexpected Fire, Ground, Ghost, or Dark coverage remains dangerous. A Dusk Stone also determines when Doublade can reach Aegislash, so stone availability matters in game-specific planning.

pokemon.name: Honedge
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Honedge is said to form when the spirit of a person inhabits the sword that killed them long ago. Its blue cloth is prehensile and functions almost like an arm, allowing it to hold its sheath or wrap around other objects. Anyone who carelessly grabs Honedge by the hilt risks having the cloth coil around their arm and drain away their life energy. The species therefore behaves less like an ordinary tool brought to life and more like a predatory spirit attached to a weapon.

pokemon.name: Doublade
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: When Honedge evolves, it becomes two separate swords that communicate through telepathy and coordinate their movements with remarkable precision. The pair uses complex alternating patterns of offense and defense that can overwhelm even highly skilled sword fighters. The two blades can rub together to create an unnerving metallic sound before attacking. Although they function as a coordinated unit, each sword remains visibly distinct and capable of independent movement.

pokemon.name: Aegislash
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Shield Forme is Aegislash's defensive stance, in which it positions its broad shield in front of the sword body and reinforces that protection with spectral power. Aegislash possesses enough supernatural influence to manipulate both people and Pokemon, and legends say it can recognize the qualities of a future ruler. Generations of kings were attended by Aegislash, although its relationship with royalty is not always benevolent; one account says an Aegislash eventually drained the life of the king it served and caused his kingdom to collapse. Shield Forme emphasizes the guarding and controlling side of the species rather than direct attack.

pokemon.name: Aegislash
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Blade Forme is Aegislash's offensive stance, adopted when it commits to an attack and shifts the shield away from the front of its body. In this state it concentrates its spectral energy and the weight of its steel blade into powerful cutting strikes capable of cleaving formidable opponents. The transformation sacrifices much of the protection associated with Shield Forme in exchange for dramatically greater offensive power. Aegislash's ability to alternate between the two stances makes its physical form an active part of its hunting and fighting behavior rather than a fixed anatomy.

playthrough: Spritzee evolves into Aromatisse when traded while holding a Sachet, so access to trading is the largest practical obstacle to using the final form in many playthroughs. Aromatisse is a pure Fairy Pokemon with base 101 HP, 99 Special Attack, 89 Special Defense, and only base 29 Speed. Moonblast, Draining Kiss, Psychic, Calm Mind, Nasty Plot in later generations, Wish, Aromatherapy or Heal Bell in applicable games, and Trick Room let it function as either a slow bulky attacker or team supporter. Healer has a chance to cure an ally's status condition at the end of a turn in doubles, while Aroma Veil protects Aromatisse and its allies from disruption such as Taunt, Encore, Disable, Heal Block, Torment, and Attract. Its extremely low Speed is an advantage under Trick Room, where a Quiet nature can let it attack before far faster opponents. Pure Fairy grants a Dragon immunity and resistances to Fighting, Bug, and Dark, with only Poison and Steel weaknesses. Calm, Bold, or Quiet are all useful depending on whether the role is special wall, mixed support, or Trick Room attacker.
competitive: Aromatisse has spent most of its competitive history in lower tiers, but it has several distinctive strengths. Base 101 HP, respectable mixed bulk, pure Fairy typing, Wish, cleric support, and Aroma Veil make it difficult for conventional Taunt or Encore users to shut down, allowing it to support teammates or set Trick Room more reliably than many slow support Pokemon. In later lower-tier formats it also developed offensive Trick Room and Nasty Plot sets, using base 29 Speed as an advantage and Moonblast plus Psychic coverage to pressure offensive teams. Smogon has highlighted Aroma Veil as one of its defining features because it prevents common disruption aimed at Wish passers or setup Pokemon. Aromatisse's limitations are equally clear: base 99 Special Attack usually needs setup to sweep, physical Defense is only base 72, and Poison- and Steel-types can force it out. It is therefore most successful as a bulky role-compression Fairy rather than as a standalone offensive centerpiece.
nuzlocke: Aromatisse is very safe against many special and Dragon-type opponents because pure Fairy typing, base 101 HP, and good Special Defense give it substantial staying power. Wish, Draining Kiss, or other recovery options can extend that longevity, while Aroma Veil prevents several annoying control effects from stopping its support moves. Its base 29 Speed means it almost always takes a hit before moving outside Trick Room, so strong physical Poison or Steel attacks should be treated very carefully. Trick Room can reverse that disadvantage and make Aromatisse surprisingly effective as a slow sweeper or team enabler. The biggest practical issue is the trade evolution: if trading a Sachet-holding Spritzee is not allowed or possible, the player may be forced to use the substantially weaker unevolved form.

pokemon.name: Spritzee
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Spritzee stores and releases fragrance from a scent pouch inside its body. The exact smell changes according to what it eats, and the resulting aroma can captivate or enrapture people and Pokemon nearby. In the past, wealthy royal women carried Spritzee instead of wearing manufactured perfume. Its curved beak-like face gives it a resemblance to a small bird or a plague doctor's mask, but scent rather than flight is the species' defining biological trait.

pokemon.name: Aromatisse
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Aromatisse can deliberately produce an enormous range of odors, from pleasant fragrances that encourage allies to smells so foul that opponents lose the will to fight. The scent from its fur is so intense that Trainers and companions exposed for long periods can gradually lose sensitivity to smell. This ability makes Aromatisse both a supporter and a deterrent depending on which aroma it chooses to release. Its biology therefore expands Spritzee's perfume-like scent control into a much more powerful chemical defense and communication system.

playthrough: Swirlix evolves into Slurpuff when traded while holding a Whipped Dream, making this another Kalos Fairy family whose final evolution depends on trading. Slurpuff is pure Fairy with balanced base 82 HP, 80 Attack, 86 Defense, 85 Special Attack, 75 Special Defense, and 72 Speed. Play Rough, Drain Punch, Flamethrower, Psychic, Energy Ball, Calm Mind, and utility are usable, but its defining offensive strategy is Belly Drum with the Hidden Ability Unburden. Belly Drum sacrifices half of Slurpuff's maximum HP to maximize Attack; a Sitrus Berry can then activate, restore health, and trigger Unburden, which doubles Speed after the held item is consumed or lost. Sweet Veil instead prevents Slurpuff and its allies from falling asleep, making it a useful support ability in doubles or safer story play. Pure Fairy leaves only Poison and Steel weaknesses and grants a Dragon immunity. Jolly is ideal for maximizing post-Unburden Speed, while Adamant improves Belly Drum damage.
competitive: Slurpuff's competitive identity is built around one of the most explosive setup combinations available to a lower-tier Fairy. Belly Drum immediately maximizes Attack, while consuming a Sitrus Berry can trigger Unburden and double Speed in the same sequence, turning Slurpuff from a middling base 80 Attack and 72 Speed Pokemon into a serious late-game sweeper. Play Rough provides strong Fairy STAB and Drain Punch covers Steel-types while restoring some of the HP sacrificed to Belly Drum. This strategy earned Slurpuff meaningful roles across several generations of lower-tier hyper offense, although it is highly dependent on getting exactly one safe setup turn and keeping its Berry intact. Sweet Veil sets and special options exist, but they have generally been secondary to Belly Drum plus Unburden. The strategy is powerful but brittle: priority, strong Steel- or Poison-types, item disruption, and a single missed Play Rough can end the sweep immediately.
nuzlocke: Slurpuff's strongest competitive strategy is also one of its riskiest Nuzlocke strategies because Belly Drum deliberately removes half of its maximum HP. Sitrus Berry plus Unburden can restore part of that loss and create enormous Attack and Speed, but using the sequence safely requires knowing that the opponent cannot KO Slurpuff during the setup turn. Sweet Veil is a more conservative ability because it prevents sleep for Slurpuff and allies without requiring any sacrifice or item interaction. Play Rough has imperfect accuracy, so a safer neutral move may be preferable when Fairy STAB is not required. Poison and Steel attacks are the principal type dangers, and the trade-with-Whipped-Dream evolution requirement may prevent Slurpuff from being available at all under stricter rules.

pokemon.name: Swirlix
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Swirlix eats almost nothing except sweets and consumes roughly its own body weight in sugar every day. That diet makes its fluffy fur sticky and gives it a strong cotton-candy smell. It can produce sticky white threads to entangle opponents and becomes noticeably irritable when it has not eaten enough sugar. Despite often appearing to float, Swirlix has small paws hidden beneath its fur.

pokemon.name: Slurpuff
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Slurpuff has an extraordinary sense of smell described as roughly one hundred million times more sensitive than a human's. It can distinguish extremely faint odors, identify subtle ingredients, and even infer a person's physical or emotional condition from scent. This makes the species valuable to pastry chefs, who use Slurpuff to judge recipes and ingredients. Its fur contains large amounts of air, leaving the body unusually light and soft despite its evolved size.

playthrough: Inkay evolves into Malamar starting at level 30 through the family's unusual inversion-based evolution method, traditionally requiring the game system to be turned upside down as the level is gained; the exact hardware implementation varies by game. Standard Malamar is Dark/Psychic with base 92 Attack, 88 Defense, 86 HP, and 73 Speed. Contrary is the defining ability because it reverses stat changes: Superpower normally lowers Attack and Defense, but on Contrary Malamar each use instead raises both stats by one stage while dealing 120-base-power Fighting damage. Knock Off, Psycho Cut, Rest, Sleep Talk, Topsy-Turvy, Hypnosis, and coverage provide offense or utility, while Suction Cups prevents forced switching and the Hidden Ability Infiltrator bypasses Substitute and several protective screen effects. Dark/Psychic has a Psychic immunity but no ordinary resistances, a Fairy weakness, and a quadruple Bug weakness. Mega Malamar keeps Dark/Psychic typing, reaches base 102 Attack, 98 Special Attack, 120 Special Defense, and 88 Speed, and retains Contrary as its Mega Ability. Careful is excellent for standard RestTalk sets, while Mega Malamar can justify Careful, Adamant, or more offensively oriented natures depending on the role.
competitive: Standard Malamar established a distinctive XY and ORAS lower-tier niche through Contrary plus Superpower. In XY NU, repeatedly using Superpower simultaneously dealt strong Fighting damage and raised Malamar's Attack and Defense, allowing bulky RestTalk sets to become progressively harder to stop while Knock Off removed important items from Poison-, Psychic-, and Flying-type answers. Contrary also turns opposing stat drops such as Intimidate into boosts, making some conventional forms of physical counterplay actively harmful. Its limitations are severe: Dark/Psychic supplies almost no defensive resistances, Bug attacks deal quadruple damage, base 73 Speed is mediocre, and Rest is often its only reliable recovery. Mega Malamar is a much newer development and should be separated from that established history. Its base 120 Special Defense, improved offenses and Speed, and continued access to Contrary give the same Superpower snowballing strategy a much larger statistical foundation, but the quadruple Bug weakness and Fairy weakness remain intact.
nuzlocke: Malamar can be powerful in a Nuzlocke because Contrary transforms Superpower from a self-weakening attack into a move that simultaneously raises Attack and Defense. Once a safe first boost is obtained, physical opponents can become progressively easier to handle, and Knock Off provides reliable Dark STAB without recoil. The major danger is the quadruple Bug weakness: U-turn, X-Scissor, First Impression, or unexpected Bug coverage can deal catastrophic damage even after Defense boosts. Fairy is also super effective, and Dark/Psychic otherwise offers very little resistance utility beyond a Psychic immunity. Mega Malamar's much higher Special Defense and improved Speed make neutral matchups safer, but neither Mega Evolution nor Contrary removes those type weaknesses. Careful is especially useful when building around repeated Superpower boosts because Defense rises naturally while Special Defense does not.

pokemon.name: Inkay
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Inkay uses the glowing spots inside its translucent body for both defense and communication. Rapid flashes can daze a threatening opponent and make it lose the will to fight, giving Inkay time to escape. The same lights can attract prey close enough for Inkay to ensnare it with its tentacles, and complex flashing rhythms are used to communicate with other Inkay. Animated portrayals also show it spraying ink from its mouth.

pokemon.name: Malamar
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Malamar possesses some of the strongest hypnotic power attributed to any Pokemon. By flashing its luminous body and making specific movements, it can lure prey, control people or Pokemon, and leave victims with little or no memory of what happened while under its influence. It captures prey with its tentacles and finishes them with digestive fluids. Malamar is also portrayed as unusually intelligent, with some individuals able to operate human technology and use manipulation or deception rather than direct violence.

pokemon.name: Malamar
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Mega Evolution enlarges Malamar's brain and causes psychic energy to overflow from its body as vivid multicolored light. That light amplifies its hypnosis far beyond ordinary mind control: Mega Malamar can overwrite a target's memories or personality and make the victim behave like a different individual. Its long glowing tentacles can sense the feelings of nearby beings, and it can insert those tentacles into its enlarged head to stimulate its own brain for additional psychic power. Mega Malamar is highly intelligent, haughty, and manipulative enough to view even its Trainer as a pawn, sometimes hypnotizing the Trainer if it disagrees with an order.

playthrough: Binacle evolves into Barbaracle at level 39, producing a Rock/Water physical attacker with base 105 Attack, 115 Defense, and 68 Speed. Shell Smash is the defining setup move because one use raises Attack, Special Attack, and Speed by two stages while lowering Defense and Special Defense by one stage. Razor Shell or later Liquidation and Stone Edge or Rock Slide provide dual STAB, while Earthquake, Cross Chop or other Fighting coverage, Grass Knot in some competitive sets, and Substitute give useful options. Tough Claws boosts contact moves by 30 percent and is generally the best offensive ability; Sniper increases critical-hit damage, while the Hidden Ability Pickpocket steals an attacker's held item if Barbaracle is not already holding one and is struck by contact. Rock/Water heavily resists Fire and also resists Normal, Flying, Poison, and Ice, but is weak to Electric, Fighting, and Ground and takes quadruple damage from Grass. Adamant is usually ideal after Shell Smash, while Jolly can improve important Speed thresholds.
competitive: Barbaracle became a legitimate XY NU setup sweeper through the combination of Shell Smash and Tough Claws. After one Shell Smash, its Attack and Speed rise sharply enough to threaten offensive teams, while Tough Claws effectively gives contact moves such as Razor Shell and Fighting coverage another substantial damage boost. Compared with other Shell Smash Water-types such as Carracosta, Barbaracle's higher base Speed lets it outrun a much larger portion of the metagame after boosting, though it lacks Carracosta's priority Aqua Jet and some of its setup safety. Later generations strengthened the strategy further with Liquidation and continued access to strong physical coverage. The weaknesses are inherent to Shell Smash itself: both defenses fall after setup, Grass attacks deal quadruple damage, priority can exploit the reduced bulk, and Stone Edge or older Razor Shell sets may introduce accuracy risk. Barbaracle is therefore a dangerous but commitment-heavy late-game cleaner.
nuzlocke: Barbaracle can sweep entire fights after Shell Smash, but the strategy carries real permadeath risk because both defensive stats fall by one stage as the offensive stats and Speed rise. It is safest to set up only against an opponent that cannot threaten strong Grass, Electric, Fighting, or Ground coverage. Grass is particularly dangerous because it deals quadruple damage, and even a weak unexpected Grass move can be lethal after Shell Smash lowers Special Defense. Tough Claws improves several reliable physical attacks without requiring recoil, while Liquidation is generally safer than Stone Edge when neutral Water damage is sufficient. Barbaracle's strong base 115 Defense makes ordinary physical hits manageable before setup, but players should not assume that bulk remains intact once Shell Smash has been used.

pokemon.name: Binacle
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Binacle normally exists as a pair of individuals sharing a single rock, and the two must cooperate to move and survive. They stretch and contract their bodies to yank the rock along in a hopping motion while feeding on seaweed washed onto shore. The partnership is not always peaceful: the two frequently quarrel, and when cooperation breaks down one Binacle may leave the shared rock and seek a different partner. Their survival therefore depends on an unusually direct social relationship between two separate individuals.

pokemon.name: Barbaracle
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: When Binacle evolves into Barbaracle, the original pair multiplies into seven cooperating Binacle units attached to two rocks. Each limb has its own eye, mind, and ability to move independently, giving Barbaracle nearly all-around vision and allowing different limbs to respond to different threats at once. The limbs normally obey the main head's instructions, but in emergencies they can act independently to defeat an enemy without waiting for orders. Barbaracle is therefore less a single conventional organism than a coordinated colony functioning as one Pokemon.

playthrough: Skrelp evolves into Dragalge at level 48, making the family a relatively late-evolving option whose final form is much more durable than the unevolved stage. Standard Dragalge is Poison/Dragon with base 123 Special Defense, 97 Special Attack, and only base 44 Speed; Draco Meteor or Dragon Pulse and Sludge Bomb or Sludge Wave provide strong dual STAB, while Surf, Hydro Pump, Focus Blast, Thunderbolt, Toxic Spikes, Flip Turn in later games, and other coverage or support give it substantial flexibility. Poison Point can poison contact attackers, Poison Touch can poison targets struck by contact moves, and the Hidden Ability Adaptability increases STAB from 1.5× to 2×, turning Dragalge's Draco Meteor and Poison attacks into genuinely powerful wallbreaking tools. Poison/Dragon resists Fire, Water, Electric, Grass, Fighting, Poison, and Bug while taking only neutral damage from Fairy, but Ground, Psychic, Ice, and Dragon are super effective. Mega Dragalge keeps Poison/Dragon typing and base 44 Speed but rises to 132 Special Attack, 105 Defense, and an enormous 163 Special Defense; in current ability-enabled formats it gains Regenerator, restoring one-third of its maximum HP whenever it switches out. Modest or Quiet are ideal for offense, while Calm is excellent for exploiting either form's exceptional special bulk.
competitive: Standard Dragalge developed a meaningful XY competitive niche despite its very low Speed. Adaptability raises the power of its Poison- and Dragon-type STAB to exceptional levels, and Choice Specs Draco Meteor or Sludge Wave could heavily damage even neutral targets while Toxic Spikes and excellent special bulk allowed defensive sets to contribute in other ways. Smogon placed Dragalge in RUBL but documented real OU use because Poison/Dragon typing let it check threats such as Keldeo, Clefable, Rotom-W, Mega Venusaur, and several special attackers while remaining offensively dangerous. It became a solid RU Pokemon in later generations with much the same identity: a slow tank that can either absorb special attacks or force progress with Adaptability. Mega Dragalge is a major modern upgrade rather than a simple extension of that history. Current Champions data places Mega Dragalge in OU with 132 Special Attack, 163 Special Defense, 105 Defense, and Regenerator, shifting the family from an Adaptability wallbreaker toward an extraordinarily resilient special tank and pivot that can repeatedly recover by switching.
nuzlocke: Dragalge is extremely useful in Nuzlockes once Skrelp survives to level 48 because its typing and base 123 Special Defense make many special matchups very safe. Reliable Sludge Bomb or Dragon Pulse is usually preferable to lower-accuracy or stat-dropping options when maximum damage is unnecessary, while Toxic Spikes can support long boss fights without exposing Dragalge every turn. Ground, Psychic, Ice, and Dragon attacks remain dangerous, and base 44 Speed means Dragalge usually takes the first hit outside Trick Room. Adaptability can shorten fights dramatically but does not improve survivability, whereas Poison Point can occasionally punish contact attackers without requiring a turn. Mega Dragalge improves both defenses and Special Attack substantially, and Regenerator in current ability-enabled formats makes switching an unusually strong source of healing, but the same four type weaknesses remain. Calm is especially safe for special tanking, while Modest or Quiet better exploit the offensive side.

pokemon.name: Skrelp
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Skrelp is a poor swimmer that survives by mimicking rotten seaweed and drifting among kelp beds. It eats decaying seaweed and uses material from that diet to produce its poison, then ambushes prey that approaches what appears to be harmless vegetation. During storms it can be washed far from its home because it lacks strong swimming ability, and it sometimes travels by clinging to or riding floating seaweed. Skrelp is also known to coexist peacefully with Dhelmise despite both species living among drifting marine vegetation.

pokemon.name: Dragalge
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Dragalge is a highly territorial marine predator that resembles kelp closely enough to hide among seaweed before ambushing prey such as Finizen. Its liquid poison is powerful enough to corrode the metal hull of a tanker, and sailors tell stories of ships that enter Dragalge territory and never return. The species can absorb sunlight through the plume on its head and convert that energy into Dragon-type power. Although aggressive toward intruders, Dragalge is known to coexist with Dhelmise in the same marine habitats.

pokemon.name: Dragalge
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Mega Dragalge grows larger and becomes covered in far more elaborate kelp-like fronds, including a cape-like crest and antler-shaped antennae containing colorful orbs. Mega Evolution changes the chemistry of its poison dramatically: it produces a liquid that forces cellular regeneration to accelerate uncontrollably. That liquid enhances Mega Dragalge's own ability to recover but acts as a deadly poison to other living things. The form therefore magnifies both sides of Dragalge's biology—its resemblance to marine vegetation and its use of toxins—while giving its regenerative ability a biological explanation.

playthrough: Clauncher evolves into Clawitzer at level 37, producing a slow pure Water special attacker with base 120 Special Attack, respectable 88 Defense and 89 Special Defense, and only base 59 Speed. Mega Launcher is the family's only Ability and boosts aura- and pulse-based moves by 50 percent, turning Water Pulse, Dark Pulse, Aura Sphere, and Dragon Pulse into much stronger coverage while also increasing the amount restored by Heal Pulse in doubles. Clawitzer can combine Water STAB with Aura Sphere, Dark Pulse, Ice Beam, Dragon Pulse, Flip Turn or U-turn in applicable games, and utility such as Heal Pulse to threaten a very wide range of targets. Pure Water has only Electric and Grass weaknesses and resists Fire, Water, Ice, and Steel, giving Clawitzer a much simpler defensive profile than many Kalos attackers. Its low Speed makes Modest natural for ordinary wallbreaking and Quiet particularly useful on Trick Room teams. Unlike its original counterpart Dragalge, Clawitzer has no Mega Evolution or alternate form in current canon.
competitive: Clawitzer was one of XY RU's strongest special wallbreakers. Base 120 Special Attack is already high, and Mega Launcher effectively turns Aura Sphere and Dark Pulse into 120-base-power coverage while strengthening Water Pulse enough to function as a legitimate primary STAB option. Smogon highlighted its ability to 2HKO large portions of the tier through the combination of Water attacks, Dark Pulse, Aura Sphere, and Ice Beam, while its reasonable bulk let it survive a hit when necessary. The main limitation is base 59 Speed, which leaves Clawitzer vulnerable to faster offensive Pokemon and encourages support from slow pivots or Trick Room. Later generations pushed it into lower usage tiers, but the same wallbreaking formula remained intact because Mega Launcher and its unusual coverage are still difficult to replicate. Its role is therefore consistent across generations: a slow special cannon that trades speed and recovery for exceptionally efficient coverage.
nuzlocke: Clawitzer is a good Nuzlocke Pokemon because pure Water has only two weaknesses and its 71/88/89 bulk is sturdy enough to survive many neutral hits. Aura Sphere is particularly safe coverage because it cannot miss under ordinary conditions, while Dark Pulse and Water Pulse benefit from Mega Launcher without recoil or stat drops. Its base 59 Speed means it often has to absorb an attack before acting, so Electric and Grass coverage should be scouted carefully rather than relying on bulk alone. Ice Beam can answer Grass-types offensively, but using it after a Grass attacker has already moved may be too late if the matchup is poor. Modest maximizes damage, while Quiet is especially strong if the team can reliably establish Trick Room.

pokemon.name: Clauncher
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Clauncher's oversized right claw makes ordinary swimming awkward, so it propels itself by detonating gas inside the claw and firing compressed water like a pistol. The same mechanism can shatter rock at close range and knock flying prey out of the air. The large claw occasionally falls off during battle or other stress, after which Clauncher hides until the limb regenerates. The meat inside the discarded claw is edible and valued as a delicacy in some regions, although its distinctive flavor is not universally liked.

pokemon.name: Clawitzer
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Clawitzer's enormous right pincer is larger than the rest of its body and functions as a high-pressure water cannon. It draws water into the claw and fires compressed projectiles powerful enough to pierce the hull of a tanker, while a rear nozzle can propel the Pokemon through the water at speeds approaching 60 knots. Feelers on the claw help locate prey before firing. Clawitzer are territorial and fight one another aggressively, and the unusually large claw itself contains substantial edible meat used as a cooking ingredient.

playthrough: Helioptile evolves into Heliolisk with a Sun Stone, allowing the player to choose when to trade the unevolved form's level-up moves for the final form's much stronger stats. Heliolisk is Electric/Normal with matching base 109 Special Attack and Speed, base 94 Special Defense, but frail 62 HP and 52 Defense. Thunderbolt and Volt Switch provide reliable Electric STAB, Hyper Voice supplies Normal STAB, and Surf, Grass Knot, Dark Pulse, Focus Blast, Glare, and other coverage give it an unusually broad special movepool. Dry Skin is generally the safest ability because Water-type moves heal Heliolisk instead of damaging it and rain restores additional HP, though Fire moves deal extra damage and harsh sunlight causes chip; Sand Veil instead benefits from sand, while the Hidden Ability Solar Power sharply boosts Special Attack in sun at the cost of HP each turn. Electric/Normal grants a Ghost immunity in addition to Electric, Flying, and Steel resistances, but is weak to Fighting and Ground. Timid is usually ideal because base 109 Speed is one of Heliolisk's best defensive tools.
competitive: Heliolisk was an XY UU Pokemon with a clear offensive-pivot niche. Base 109 Speed let it outrun common threats around the base 108 benchmark, while Thunderbolt, Volt Switch, Hyper Voice, Surf, Grass Knot, Focus Blast, and Dark Pulse made switching into it surprisingly difficult. Dry Skin is especially valuable competitively because it grants a Water immunity and rain recovery, allowing Heliolisk to exploit bulky Water-types rather than merely threatening them with Electric STAB. Smogon later described Heliolisk as one of SM NU's best offensive pivots and bulky-Water exploiters for the same reason. The consistent weakness is physical durability: 62 HP and 52 Defense mean even neutral physical attacks can deal enormous damage, so Heliolisk depends on immunities, speed, and Volt Switch rather than conventional switching. Solar Power sun sets can generate much greater immediate damage but are less sustainable because they lose HP every turn in sunlight.
nuzlocke: Heliolisk is extremely useful when its immunities can be planned around. Normal typing grants a Ghost immunity, Dry Skin can add a complete Water immunity, and Volt Switch lets Heliolisk attack while immediately leaving unfavorable matchups. Its physical bulk is extremely poor, however, so strong neutral contact moves can be dangerous even when they are not super effective, and Fighting or Ground attacks are especially threatening. Thunderbolt and Hyper Voice are safer than inaccurate options, while Surf provides reliable coverage against many Ground-types that would otherwise block Electric attacks. Solar Power can create exceptional damage in sun but continuously drains HP, making Dry Skin the more conservative Nuzlocke choice in most games. Timid is generally ideal because moving first is far safer than attempting to absorb physical damage.

pokemon.name: Helioptile
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Helioptile's expandable head frills contain cells that generate electricity when exposed to sunlight, functioning much like biological solar panels. This process allows it to thrive in desert environments without needing to eat constantly because sunlight can supply much of its energy. If its ability to generate solar electricity is interrupted, Helioptile becomes stressed and physically weakened. The species stores and uses the generated electricity for its attacks.

pokemon.name: Heliolisk
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Heliolisk greatly amplifies the solar-electric system of Helioptile. By spreading its neck frill in sunlight, a single Heliolisk can generate enough electricity to power a skyscraper, with some Pokédex accounts claiming an entire city could be powered by one individual. It can channel electricity into its leg muscles strongly enough to sprint one hundred yards in roughly five seconds and has been shown running across the surface of water. An ancient desert kingdom once treasured Heliolisk, and archaeological accounts connect the species with treasure later brought to Galar.

playthrough: Tyrunt is revived from a Jaw Fossil and evolves into Tyrantrum when leveled up during the day starting at level 39. Tyrantrum is Rock/Dragon with base 121 Attack, 119 Defense, and only base 71 Speed and 59 Special Defense, making it an exceptionally strong physical attacker but a vulnerable target for special coverage. Strong Jaw boosts bite-based attacks such as Crunch and elemental fangs by 50 percent, while the Hidden Ability Rock Head prevents recoil and allows Tyrantrum to use the 150-base-power Head Smash without damaging itself. Dragon Claw or Outrage, Head Smash or Rock Slide, Earthquake, Crunch, Psychic Fangs in later generations, Close Combat in applicable games, and Dragon Dance provide excellent physical options. Rock/Dragon resists Normal, Electric, Poison, Flying, and especially Fire, but is weak to Fighting, Ground, Steel, Ice, Dragon, and Fairy. Jolly helps the mediocre base 71 Speed, while Adamant maximizes wallbreaking and is especially effective when Dragon Dance or external speed control is available.
competitive: Tyrantrum was placed in RUBL in XY and developed a serious UU wallbreaking niche. Base 121 Attack and Rock Head give it access to recoil-free Head Smash, one of the strongest repeatable physical STAB attacks available, while Outrage or Dragon Claw and Earthquake provide enough additional coverage to pressure most conventional Rock answers. Strong Jaw is a viable alternative for Crunch and elemental-fang sets, but competitive Tyrantrum is most famous for abusing Rock Head Head Smash. Smogon highlighted both its wallbreaking power and respectable base 119 Defense, but also its mediocre Speed and poor base 59 Special Defense, which allow many faster special attackers to revenge kill it. Dragon Dance can compensate for the Speed problem if Tyrantrum finds a setup opportunity, while Choice Scarf or Choice Band sets emphasize immediate pressure. The species is therefore a classic high-power physical breaker: terrifying when it attacks safely, but easy to exploit from the special side.
nuzlocke: Tyrantrum can be extremely effective in a Nuzlocke because base 121 Attack and 119 Defense allow it to win many physical matchups decisively. Rock Head is particularly valuable if available because it removes Head Smash recoil completely, turning an otherwise dangerous move into an exceptionally powerful repeated attack; with Strong Jaw instead, Crunch and fang moves remain safer accurate options. The family's six weaknesses are the main concern, especially because base 59 Special Defense makes Ice-, Fairy-, Ground-, or Fighting-type special coverage much more dangerous than its overall bulk suggests. Dragon Dance can create sweeps but requires a genuinely safe setup turn. Jolly is often safer when the extra Speed prevents an incoming attack, while Adamant is better when speed control is already guaranteed.

pokemon.name: Tyrunt
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Tyrunt is a Fossil Pokemon reconstructed from remains roughly 100 million years old. It behaves like a spoiled young royal, throwing violent tantrums when something displeases it and often injuring others accidentally even while playing. Its jaws are already powerful enough to shred or crush an automobile. Fossil reconstruction may not perfectly reproduce the original animal, and some modern theories suggest ancient Tyrunt may have had more extensive feathering than reconstructed individuals display.

pokemon.name: Tyrantrum
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Tyrantrum was one of the dominant predators of the ancient world and is repeatedly described as behaving like a king roughly 100 million years ago. Its enormous jaws can demolish a car with a single bite, and Pokédex records claim that almost nothing in its environment could stand against it. Its crown-like head spikes and feathered neck reinforce the royal imagery surrounding the species. As with Tyrunt, incomplete fossil restoration leaves open the possibility that the living animal once had a more extensive feather-like coat than modern reconstructed Tyrantrum.

playthrough: Amaura is revived from a Sail Fossil and evolves into Aurorus when leveled up at night starting at level 39. Aurorus is Rock/Ice with huge base 123 HP, base 99 Special Attack, and 92 Special Defense, but only base 58 Speed and a typing that creates six weaknesses. Refrigerate changes Normal-type attacks into Ice-type moves and boosts their power—by 30 percent in Generation VI and 20 percent from Generation VII onward—making Hyper Voice a strong and accurate Ice STAB option. The Hidden Ability Snow Warning automatically summons hail in older generations or snow under modern rules, making Blizzard perfectly accurate and in Generation IX also increasing the Defense of Ice-types. Freeze-Dry is especially valuable because it hits Water-types super effectively, while Earth Power, Ancient Power or Rock STAB, Stealth Rock, Thunder Wave, and coverage give Aurorus multiple roles. Water, Grass, Ground, and Rock are super effective, while Fighting and Steel deal quadruple damage. Modest is usually best because base 58 Speed is difficult to salvage, while Quiet can support Trick Room.
competitive: Aurorus was an XY NU wallbreaker whose offensive tools were much stronger than its raw base 99 Special Attack initially suggests. Refrigerate turns Hyper Voice into boosted Ice STAB that also bypasses Substitute, while Snow Warning makes Blizzard perfectly accurate and Freeze-Dry punishes Water-types that would normally resist Ice. Earth Power provides excellent coverage against Steel-, Rock-, and Fire-type answers, and Stealth Rock or Rock Polish add useful support and setup options. Smogon described Aurorus as one of XY NU's most fearsome wallbreakers and later as one of SM PU's stronger offensive threats. Its competitive ceiling is held down by defensive typing rather than movepool: six weaknesses, quadruple Fighting and Steel weaknesses, Stealth Rock vulnerability, and base 58 Speed make it easy for faster attackers to revenge kill. Aurorus succeeds by getting onto the field safely and forcing immediate damage rather than by staying in against broad portions of a team.
nuzlocke: Aurorus offers excellent special offense and a very large HP pool, but it is one of the most matchup-sensitive Fossil Pokemon for a Nuzlocke. Fighting and Steel moves deal quadruple damage, while Water, Grass, Ground, and Rock are also super effective, so its 123 HP should never be mistaken for universal durability. Refrigerate Hyper Voice is reliable and accurate, while Snow Warning can make Blizzard safe from an accuracy standpoint and improve physical Ice-type bulk under Generation IX snow. Freeze-Dry is particularly useful because it lets Aurorus defeat Water-types without relying on risky neutral coverage. Its low Speed means it usually takes a hit first, making careful type knowledge far more important than raw damage. Modest maximizes the value of each safe attacking turn, while Quiet is appropriate on Trick Room teams.

pokemon.name: Amaura
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Amaura is reconstructed from a Sail Fossil preserved for more than 100 million years. It originally lived peacefully in cold environments where major predators such as Tyrantrum were absent, and modern revived individuals are not expected to tolerate warm climates especially well. The sail-like structures above its eyes can change color with its mood, while the crystal structures on its body remain permanently cold. When Amaura cries out at night, aurora-like lights have been observed appearing in the sky.

pokemon.name: Aurorus
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Aurorus is generally quiet and gentle despite its enormous size. The diamond-shaped crystals on its body can expel air as cold as roughly −240 degrees Fahrenheit, allowing it to surround enemies in ice or instantly create defensive ice walls. Its long neck sails can change color according to mood, and its howls are associated with auroras appearing in the sky. At least one Aurorus has been discovered preserved in a glacier in a condition resembling the species' ancient living form.

name: Sylveon
biologyAndBehavior: Sylveon's ribbon-like feelers are highly mobile sensory organs that emit an aura capable of suppressing hostility, sometimes ending fights without direct combat. It commonly wraps these feelers around a trusted Trainer's arm, allowing it to sense the person's emotions while they walk together. The same calming ability has a predatory use: Sylveon can lower a target's aggression and distract it with swirling feelers before suddenly pouncing. Despite its gentle and affectionate behavior toward companions, Sylveon is notably fearless against Dragon Pokemon and has been described charging opponents many times its own size without hesitation.
playthrough: Fairy is an outstanding story-mode typing, and Sylveon provides reliable answers to Dark-, Dragon-, and Fighting-types while possessing enough Special Attack to remove enemies rather than merely wall them. Its 95 HP and exceptional 130 Special Defense make it forgiving against special attackers, while its 110 Special Attack provides strong offensive pressure despite its low Speed. Pixilate can turn Normal-type attacks into powerful Fairy-type moves in games where the Hidden Ability is available, further increasing its damage potential. Its main vulnerabilities are weak physical Defense and poor Speed, making strong physical Poison- and Steel-type attackers particularly dangerous.
competitive: Depending on the format, Sylveon can function as either a Wish-supporting special wall or a powerful Pixilate Hyper Voice attacker. Historically, its excellent special bulk and Fairy typing have allowed it to check Dragon-, Dark-, and Fighting-types while supporting teammates with moves such as Wish and, in generations where available, Heal Bell. Offensive sets exploit 110 Special Attack and Pixilate-boosted Hyper Voice to deal substantial Fairy-type damage while retaining far more natural bulk than many dedicated wallbreakers. Its low Speed, mediocre physical Defense, and competition from other powerful Fairy-types limit its universal viability, but the combination of offense, special bulk, and support gives Sylveon considerable role flexibility.
nuzlocke: Sylveon combines excellent special bulk, useful resistances, a Dragon immunity, strong offense, and good recovery and support options with relatively little reliance on setup. Its durability makes unexpected special attacks and neutral hits less dangerous, while Fairy typing provides valuable offensive and defensive matchups against several threatening types. Unlike more passive defensive Pokemon such as Umbreon, Sylveon can also deal substantial direct damage, allowing it to end dangerous battles instead of relying primarily on status or stalling. Its main concern is the physical side, where 65 Defense and low Speed can leave it exposed to strong Steel-, Poison-, or neutral physical attacks.
description: Sylveon is a Fairy-type Pokémon introduced in Generation VI and a final stage of its evolution line, with a base stat total of 525.

playthrough: Hawlucha is a single-stage Fighting/Flying Pokemon with base 118 Speed and 92 Attack, so it functions as a fast physical attacker rather than a bulky Fighting-type. Flying Press is its signature move and is unusual because it is Fighting-type while calculating effectiveness using both Fighting and Flying matchups; High Jump Kick, Acrobatics, Brave Bird, Swords Dance, Roost, U-turn, Stone Edge, and other coverage give Hawlucha several ways to sweep or pivot. Limber prevents paralysis, Mold Breaker lets Hawlucha ignore opposing abilities when attacking, and Unburden doubles Speed after its held item is consumed or otherwise lost, making Unburden the defining setup ability in most competitive and advanced play. Fighting/Flying grants a Ground immunity, a quadruple Bug resistance, and resistances to Fighting, Grass, and Dark, but Electric, Ice, Flying, Psychic, and Fairy are super effective. Mega Hawlucha keeps Fighting/Flying typing and base 118 Speed while rising to base 137 Attack, 100 Defense, and 93 Special Defense; current ability-enabled play gives it No Guard, making every move used by or against it hit regardless of accuracy. Jolly is usually ideal for standard Hawlucha, while Adamant becomes more reasonable after Unburden or when Mega Hawlucha's base 118 Speed is already sufficient.
competitive: Standard Hawlucha has repeatedly found upper-tier niches because Unburden can turn a one-time item activation into effectively unmatched Speed. In XY it was UUBL with genuine OU viability, usually relying on Swords Dance, Acrobatics, High Jump Kick, Substitute or a consumable item to activate Unburden and become a late-game cleaner. Later terrain-based teams made the ability even easier to trigger through Seeds, and Hawlucha became one of the most recognizable setup sweepers of the Tapu era. Its main limitation is that base 92 Attack is modest until boosted, while 78/75/63 bulk leaves little room for a failed setup or inaccurate High Jump Kick. Mega Hawlucha is a newer form and should be separated from that established Unburden history: current Champions data places it in UU with base 137 Attack, 100 Defense, 93 Special Defense, and No Guard. No Guard removes the accuracy risk from moves such as High Jump Kick and other coverage, but also guarantees that opposing attacks aimed at Mega Hawlucha will not miss.
nuzlocke: Hawlucha is very useful in Nuzlockes because base 118 Speed, a Ground immunity, and strong dual STAB let it avoid many retaliations entirely. Flying Press is accurate and distinctive, while Acrobatics can become especially strong after Hawlucha loses its held item; High Jump Kick should be treated with caution because a miss or failed hit can cause severe crash damage. Unburden can create extremely safe sweeps if a Berry or other consumable item is triggered deliberately, but once Hawlucha switches out the Speed boost is lost. Electric, Ice, Flying, Psychic, and Fairy attacks remain dangerous because the ordinary form is not especially bulky. Mega Hawlucha's improved defenses and No Guard remove accuracy risk from its own moves, but No Guard also removes the possibility that an enemy attack misses, so defensive planning still matters.

pokemon.name: Hawlucha
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Hawlucha is a solitary, highly athletic Pokemon whose fighting style resembles lucha libre and aerial wrestling. It uses its wings to control its position in the air, repeatedly exploiting opponents' blind spots and favoring attacks from above because they are difficult to defend against. Hawlucha practices flashy finishing moves in the forests where it lives and is compelled to show off when it believes victory is near, a habit opponents can exploit. Wild Hawlucha also fight frequently with groups of Primeape, making territorial combat a normal part of their lives.

pokemon.name: Hawlucha
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Mega Evolution pumps up nearly every muscle in Hawlucha's body and greatly improves its ability to absorb direct attacks. Mega Hawlucha becomes so confident in that new durability that it deliberately flexes and showboats in front of opponents, attempting to lure them into attacking before retaliating. It then uses the opening to stun or stagger the opponent and follows with a spinning aerial Flying Press. The form exaggerates Hawlucha's existing wrestling persona, combining heavier musculature with even more theatrical crowd-facing behavior.

playthrough: Dedenne is a single-stage Electric/Fairy Pokemon with base 101 Speed, 81 Special Attack, and otherwise modest stats. Thunderbolt, Volt Switch, Dazzling Gleam, Grass Knot, Nuzzle, Charm, Super Fang in older movepools, and support such as Thunder Wave or Eerie Impulse give it utility even when its damage output is limited. Cheek Pouch restores one-third of Dedenne's maximum HP after it eats a Berry in addition to the Berry's normal effect, Pickup can recover or acquire used items in specific situations, and the Hidden Ability Plus raises Special Attack by 50 percent in doubles when an ally has Plus or Minus. Electric/Fairy grants a Dragon immunity and resistances to Electric, Fighting, Flying, Bug, and Dark, while only Ground and Poison are super effective. Timid is usually ideal because Dedenne's best defensive quality is its Speed rather than its 67/57/67 bulk. It is a useful utility Pokemon in ordinary play but should not be mistaken for a high-powered sweeper.
competitive: Dedenne has historically been a very low-tier competitive Pokemon. Its Electric/Fairy typing is genuinely useful and base 101 Speed is respectable, but base 81 Special Attack, poor physical bulk, and shallow offensive coverage leave it badly outclassed by stronger Electric-types in most formats. Smogon's XY analysis explicitly describes it as poor even in PU, where faster or stronger alternatives such as Raichu and Zebstrika generally perform the offensive role better. Its more defensible niches come from utility: Nuzzle provides perfectly accurate paralysis while dealing chip damage, Volt Switch creates momentum, and Cheek Pouch can make Berry-based support sets surprisingly difficult to remove immediately. Dedenne is therefore best evaluated honestly as a situational support Pokemon rather than overstating its competitive relevance.
nuzlocke: Dedenne can still be useful in a Nuzlocke because its typing supplies a Dragon immunity and only two weaknesses. Nuzzle is especially valuable because it deals damage while guaranteeing paralysis, providing safe speed control without depending on Thunder Wave accuracy or prediction. Cheek Pouch can produce a large emergency heal when a Sitrus or other restorative Berry activates, increasing survivability beyond the mediocre defensive stats. Ground and Poison attacks are the main dangers, and strong neutral physical hits can also be threatening because base 57 Defense is low. Timid is usually safest, and Dedenne is most effective when used to control speed, pivot with Volt Switch, and exploit immunities rather than trying to trade direct damage.

pokemon.name: Dedenne
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Dedenne's upper whiskers function like antennae that send and receive electrical signals, allowing individuals to communicate over long distances and share information about food or sources of electricity. Its lower whiskers discharge electricity directly. Because Dedenne's own electrical organ is underdeveloped, it often steals electricity from other Electric-type Pokemon or plugs its tail into household outlets and electrical infrastructure. When its charge runs low, it curls up and sleeps until it can replenish its stored energy.

playthrough: Carbink is a single-stage Rock/Fairy Pokemon built almost entirely around defense, with base 150 Defense and 150 Special Defense but only base 50 HP, offenses, and Speed. Moonblast and Power Gem provide modest STAB, while Stealth Rock, Reflect, Light Screen, Trick Room, Calm Mind, Body Press in later generations, and Rest give it support or slow setup options. Clear Body prevents opposing effects from lowering Carbink's stats, while Sturdy guarantees survival from full HP against a single hit that would otherwise knock it out and also blocks one-hit KO moves. Rock/Fairy grants a Dragon immunity and useful resistances to Normal, Fire, Flying, Bug, and Dark, but Water, Grass, and Ground are super effective and Steel deals quadruple damage. Bold, Calm, Relaxed, or Sassy all fit defensive roles, with minimum Speed particularly useful on Trick Room teams. Carbink's strength lies in reliably creating team support rather than dealing immediate damage.
competitive: Carbink has spent most of its competitive history in very low tiers, but its niche is well defined. Base 150 in both defenses, Stealth Rock, dual screens, Trick Room, Sturdy, and later Body Press allow it to compress several support jobs into one team slot. In XY ZU and PU, Smogon describes Carbink as a premier physical wall on some balance teams, capable of checking Normal- and Fire-types while setting Stealth Rock and using Calm Mind or Rest to avoid complete passivity. In later generations it also became a useful dedicated Trick Room lead because Sturdy can nearly guarantee that Trick Room or hazards go up before Carbink is removed. The central drawback is that base 50 offenses are poor and Steel attacks deal quadruple damage, so many opponents can exploit it if it lacks exactly the right support move.
nuzlocke: Carbink is a safe Nuzlocke support Pokemon because Sturdy can guarantee survival from full HP and its 150/150 defensive stats make many neutral attacks manageable. Stealth Rock, Reflect, Light Screen, and Trick Room can all make later team members safer without requiring Carbink to score knockouts itself. Steel moves are the critical danger because they deal quadruple damage, while Water, Grass, and Ground are also super effective; Sturdy only protects from one hit and can be broken by prior chip damage or multi-hit moves. Rest can provide full recovery but creates two turns of sleep, so it is best used only when the matchup is controlled. Bold or Calm are natural choices depending on whether the team needs stronger physical or special insurance.

pokemon.name: Carbink
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Carbink forms deep underground under enormous heat and pressure and may remain asleep there for millions of years before being uncovered by excavation. It feeds and grows among mineral deposits, using the soft mane around its neck to polish the gemstones of other Carbink. Sableye and Gabite are known predators, and Carbink defends itself by firing high-energy beams from the crystals embedded in its body. On extremely rare occasions a Carbink undergoes a mysterious mutation and becomes Diancie, and legends describe colonies of Carbink living in jeweled underground kingdoms ruled by Diancie.

playthrough: Goomy evolves into Sliggoo at level 40, and ordinary Sliggoo evolves into Goodra starting at level 50 when leveled during rain in the overworld. Standard Goodra is pure Dragon with base 150 Special Defense, 110 Special Attack, 100 Attack, and 90 HP, making it one of the strongest special tanks among pseudo-legendary Pokemon. Dragon Pulse or Draco Meteor, Flamethrower, Thunderbolt, Sludge Bomb, Surf or Muddy Water, Power Whip, Earthquake, and numerous physical or special coverage moves let Goodra exploit either attacking stat. Sap Sipper grants a Grass immunity and raises Attack, Hydration cures status at the end of each turn in rain, and Gooey lowers the Speed of opponents that make contact. In Hisui, Goomy evolves into Hisuian Sliggoo at level 40 and then Hisuian Goodra at level 50 during rain; the regional forms are Steel/Dragon with far greater physical defense, lower Speed, and access to Shell Armor instead of Hydration. Standard Goodra is weak to Ice, Dragon, and Fairy, while Hisuian Goodra trades that profile for only Fighting and Ground weaknesses while gaining many resistances and a Poison immunity. Modest or Calm suit standard Goodra; Calm, Careful, Modest, or Relaxed can all work well for the Hisuian branch.
competitive: Standard Goodra was a solid XY UU special tank rather than a dominant OU pseudo-legendary. Its base 150 Special Defense, Sap Sipper, Dragon typing, and huge mixed movepool let it switch into special Water-, Fire-, Grass-, and Electric-type attacks and immediately threaten the opponent with Draco Meteor, Fire Blast, Sludge Bomb, Power Whip, or other coverage. Smogon's XY analysis emphasizes that Goodra can run Choice Band, Choice Specs, or Assault Vest because both offensive stats are usable, but mediocre base 70 Defense and lack of reliable recovery prevent it from staying healthy indefinitely. Hisuian Goodra substantially improves the defensive profile: Steel/Dragon typing, 100 Defense, 150 Special Defense, and Shell Armor or Sap Sipper make it one of the most dependable special walls in current lower and mid tiers. Smogon describes Hisuian Goodra as a reliable defensive Pokemon that can still make progress through Knock Off, Acid Spray, Heavy Slam, Body Press, or powerful special attacks. The main shared limitation is recovery; neither form has dependable instant healing in ordinary competitive play, so hazards and repeated pivoting can eventually wear them down.
nuzlocke: The Goomy line requires patience because level 40 and rainy-weather evolution conditions delay the final form, but Goodra is an excellent payoff. Standard Goodra is exceptionally safe against special attackers thanks to base 150 Special Defense and can create free switch opportunities with Sap Sipper, while Dragon typing supplies useful Fire, Water, Grass, and Electric resistances. Its base 70 Defense is the main danger, so strong physical Ice, Dragon, or Fairy moves should not be taken lightly. Hisuian Goodra is even more forgiving defensively because Steel/Dragon has only Fighting and Ground weaknesses and base 100 Defense backs up the same 150 Special Defense; Shell Armor can also eliminate unexpected critical hits. The Hisuian branch is slower, so it often takes the first hit, but its defensive typing makes that much safer. Calm is excellent for pure special tanking, while Modest gives either final form stronger immediate offense.

pokemon.name: Goomy
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Goomy is an extremely soft-bodied Dragon Pokemon that depends on a thick layer of slime to keep its body from drying out. Its gelatinous tissues are so weak that ordinary physical force can injure it easily, and it prefers damp, shaded habitats where moisture is abundant. Goomy's feelers act as sensitive sensory organs that help it detect changes in the environment. It is known for a gentle, timid temperament and is often considered one of the weakest Dragon-type Pokemon before evolution.

pokemon.name: Sliggoo
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Standard Sliggoo is a soft, mucus-covered Dragon whose four horn-like feelers are highly sensitive to changes in air and nearby movement. Its eyes have regressed and it relies heavily on those feelers instead of conventional vision. A powerful acidic slime can dissolve nearly anything, allowing Sliggoo to consume food without chewing and defend itself against threats. Its lack of sharp boundaries between body and mucus makes physical contact with Sliggoo unusually slippery and difficult to control.

pokemon.name: Sliggoo
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Hisuian Sliggoo develops a metallic spiral shell that is absent from the ordinary form. The shell is rich in iron and provides much greater physical protection, while the Pokemon can retract much of its body into the shell when threatened. Hisuian Sliggoo is notably more withdrawn and cautious than ordinary Sliggoo and tends to cling tightly to safe locations or trusted companions. Its shell and body chemistry reflect adaptation to Hisui's mineral-rich environment.

pokemon.name: Goodra
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Standard Goodra is affectionate, friendly, and physically much stronger than its soft appearance suggests. It frequently hugs its Trainer, coating people in sticky slime in the process, and it may become lonely or distressed when separated from companions. Its long feelers and tail are powerful enough to strike hard, while its mucus makes the body difficult for attackers to grasp. Despite its reputation as a gentle Dragon, Goodra can defend companions with surprising force when threatened.

pokemon.name: Goodra
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Hisuian Goodra carries a massive metallic shell that can change in hardness and provide fortress-like protection. It is extremely clingy and dislikes solitude even more strongly than ordinary Goodra, sometimes becoming angry or destructive when a person it cares about leaves. The shell's metal content makes the regional form dramatically heavier and gives it Steel typing, while the Pokemon can withdraw into that shell to protect itself. Its combination of immense defensive strength and emotional dependence is one of the clearest behavioral differences between the Hisuian and ordinary forms.

playthrough: Klefki is a single-stage Steel/Fairy Pokemon whose modest 57/80/91/80/87/75 stats are compensated by one of the best support typings and abilities in the series. Steel/Fairy grants immunities to Dragon and Poison, a very large set of resistances, and only Fire and Ground weaknesses. Prankster gives +1 priority to non-damaging moves, letting Klefki use Spikes, Thunder Wave, Reflect, Light Screen, Magnet Rise, Rain Dance, Sunny Day, Fairy Lock, and other support before faster opponents; from Generation VII onward, opposing Dark-types are immune to Prankster-boosted status moves that target them. The Hidden Ability Magician steals the target's held item after Klefki hits it while holding no item, but Prankster is overwhelmingly more useful for most support roles. Dazzling Gleam, Flash Cannon, Foul Play, and Play Rough give limited offensive presence, while Magnet Rise can temporarily remove its Ground weakness. Calm or Bold are generally best because Klefki's value comes from surviving long enough to support the team rather than maximizing damage.
competitive: Klefki was one of Generation VI's most important support Pokemon. In XY UU, Prankster Spikes, Thunder Wave, dual screens, Toxic, Magnet Rise, and Fairy Lock combined with Steel/Fairy typing to let it check numerous Dragons and fast offensive threats while stacking hazards or crippling switch-ins. Its influence extended well beyond UU: Klefki was also a high-ranking XY Ubers support Pokemon and one of the metagame's notable Xerneas checks because it could resist Moonblast, use priority Thunder Wave, and lay Spikes against many otherwise dangerous teams. The notorious Swagger plus Prankster strategies of early Generation VI also contributed to Klefki's reputation, although later mechanics and rules changes reduced that style. Generation VII's Prankster nerf gave Dark-types immunity to targeted priority status moves, removing some of Klefki's universal disruption. Even after that change, Steel/Fairy typing and priority hazards or screens kept it viable across multiple lower and specialized formats.
nuzlocke: Klefki is very safe in Nuzlockes because Steel/Fairy gives two immunities, many resistances, and only Fire and Ground weaknesses. Priority Reflect and Light Screen can protect the entire team before an opponent moves, while Thunder Wave provides emergency speed control and Spikes can help wear down repeated boss switches in formats where the AI uses them. Magnet Rise is especially useful when a predictable Ground move would otherwise threaten Klefki, temporarily leaving Fire as its only ordinary weakness. Its offensive stats are mediocre, so it is better used to create safe situations for stronger teammates than to force knockouts itself. From Generation VII onward, Prankster status moves do not affect opposing Dark-types, an important mechanical exception when planning around priority Thunder Wave or similar support.

pokemon.name: Klefki
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Klefki originally lived in mineral-rich mines, but as those resources became scarce it moved into human settlements and adapted to feeding on metal ions from keys and other metal objects. It collects keys obsessively, especially master keys, and can sneak into homes to steal them. A favored key may be kept for decades, which led nobles and other wealthy people to entrust important vault keys to carefully raised Klefki. The ring-like loop around its body is highly mobile, allowing Klefki to collect, rattle, rearrange, or even use its keys as part of threat displays and communication.

playthrough: Phantump evolves into Trevenant when traded, so the line's main practical obstacle is access to trading rather than level. Trevenant is Ghost/Grass with base 110 Attack, 85 HP, 82 Special Defense, and only base 56 Speed, making it a slow physical attacker and utility Pokemon rather than a sweeper. Horn Leech provides reliable Grass STAB with healing, while Wood Hammer offers much greater power at the cost of recoil; Shadow Claw or Phantom Force, Earthquake, Rock Slide, Will-O-Wisp, Leech Seed, Curse, and Forest's Curse provide offense or disruption. Natural Cure removes non-volatile status when Trevenant switches out, Frisk reveals opposing held items, and the Hidden Ability Harvest has a 50 percent chance each turn to restore a consumed Berry, becoming guaranteed in harsh sunlight. Ghost/Grass grants Normal and Fighting immunities plus resistances to Water, Electric, Grass, and Ground, but Fire, Ice, Flying, Ghost, and Dark are super effective. Adamant is best for direct physical offense, while Careful or specially defensive investment can support Harvest and recovery-based sets.
competitive: Trevenant has generally occupied lower competitive tiers but possesses several distinct niches. Base 110 Attack and STAB Wood Hammer let it function as a physical wallbreaker, while Earthquake and Rock Slide punish several common Grass-resistant switch-ins; Smogon's XY analysis specifically notes that this coverage distinguishes Trevenant from many competing Grass-types. Natural Cure gives offensive sets a valuable status-absorbing role, while Harvest can support slower defensive strategies built around repeatedly restoring Sitrus, Lum, or other Berries alongside Will-O-Wisp, Leech Seed, Horn Leech, or Protect. Its problems are equally consistent: base 56 Speed is poor, its defensive stats are only moderate, and Ghost/Grass carries five weaknesses. Trevenant therefore rewards prediction and role specialization but has never had the efficiency or raw durability to become a sustained upper-tier staple.
nuzlocke: Trevenant is useful in Nuzlockes because two immunities and several resistances create safe switch opportunities, while Horn Leech can restore health without requiring a separate recovery turn. Natural Cure is particularly safe because burns, poison, paralysis, and sleep are removed by switching, while Harvest can create repeated Berry recovery if the Hidden Ability is available. Wood Hammer should be used cautiously because recoil can turn otherwise clean wins into dangerous chip, and Phantom Force's two-turn timing can create unexpected interactions. Fire, Ice, Flying, Ghost, and Dark moves remain the major threats, especially because Trevenant is slow and often takes the first hit. The largest practical drawback is the trade evolution itself: without trading, the player is limited to the substantially weaker Phantump.

pokemon.name: Phantump
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Phantump is a ghostly Pokemon inhabiting a tree stump. Folklore says it is created when the spirit of a child who became lost and died in a forest possesses a stump, although this origin is presented as a legend rather than a demonstrated biological process. Its cries resemble the voice or screams of a child, and people who follow those sounds can become lost; however, Phantump is often described as trying to make friends rather than deliberately luring victims to harm. The green leaves growing from its branches can be brewed into a liquid with curative properties.

pokemon.name: Trevenant
pokemon.biologyAndBehavior: Trevenant is an extremely territorial guardian of old forests that can control nearby trees through its root-like nervous system. It uses its roots to manipulate or trap intruders and is said to curse people who damage the forest, sometimes preventing them from ever finding their way back out. Despite that hostility, Trevenant is protective toward Pokemon that live peacefully within its woods and can act as a caretaker rather than a predator. Lumberjacks historically feared Trevenant enough to mark or avoid forests believed to be under its protection.

playthrough: Pumpkaboo evolves into Gourgeist when traded. Both are Ghost/Grass and come in four size varieties—Small, Medium, Large, and Jumbo—with smaller forms trading HP and Attack for greater Speed while larger forms become slower, bulkier, and physically stronger. Gourgeist has excellent base 122 Defense in every size and can use Seed Bomb, Power Whip, Shadow Sneak, Poltergeist in later generations, Will-O-Wisp, Leech Seed, Synthesis, Trick, Foul Play, Explosion, and the unique Trick-or-Treat. Pickup can recover an item used by another Pokemon in certain situations, Frisk reveals opposing held items on entry, and the Hidden Ability Insomnia prevents sleep. Ghost/Grass grants Normal and Fighting immunities plus four useful resistances, but Fire, Ice, Flying, Ghost, and Dark are super effective. Small Gourgeist is best when Speed matters, Jumbo is the strongest and bulkiest physical form, and the intermediate varieties offer compromises between those extremes. Impish is excellent for defensive variants, while Adamant can support more offensive size choices.
competitive: Gourgeist is unusual because size selection materially changes its competitive role. Small Gourgeist is the fastest and can exploit Will-O-Wisp, Leech Seed, Substitute, Destiny Bond, or Trick more aggressively, while Jumbo Gourgeist sacrifices Speed for greater HP and Attack and has historically been the preferred physically defensive form.
